docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The connect files describe how water and the material it moves travel from one spatial object to the next. Every spatial object (HRU, routing unit, aquifer, channel, reservoir, recall, export coefficient, delivery ratio, outlet, gwflow cell) has one row in the connect file for its object type. The row gives the object its number and name, its area, location and elevation, the record it uses in its property file, its weather station, and the list of objects that receive its outflow. SWAT+ builds the routing network and the order in which objects are run from these rows.

All connect files have the same format. The file names are given on the connect line of file.cio, in this order:

Position on the connect line Default name Object Count column in object.cnt Property column header Property file 1 hru.con HRU hru hru hru-data.hru 2 hru-lte.con HRU-lte lhru hlt hru-lte.hru 3 rout_unit.con Routing unit rtu rtu rout_unit.rtu 4 gwflow.con gwflow cell mfl see gwflow 5 aquifer.con Aquifer aqu aqu aquifer.aqu 6 aquifer2d.con 2-D aquifer aqu2d not read in 62.0.1 7 channel.con Channel (legacy) cha channel.cha 8 reservoir.con Reservoir res res reservoir.res 9 recall.con Recall (point source or inlet) rec rec recall.rec 10 exco.con Export coefficient exco exc exco.exc 11 delratio.con Delivery ratio dlr dlr delratio.del 12 outlet.con Outlet out out none 13 chandeg.con SWAT-DEG channel lcha lcha channel-lte.cha

A file is read only when the matching count in object.cnt is above zero. When a count is above zero the file has to exist, because nothing checks for it: a missing file leaves those objects without connection data. The file named in position 6 is never opened in 62.0.1.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one object. SWAT+ reads as many rows as the count for that object type in object.cnt. It does not match columns by header name, so every row must give the values below in this order.

Each row has 13 leading values followed by out_tot groups of four values that describe the outflow connections, all on the same line.

# Column Units Description 1 id - Object number within its type. Number the rows 1, 2, 3 and so on in file order: the obj_id column of other connect files refers to an object by its row position, while SWAT+ uses id as the object number during the run. 2 name - Object name, up to 16 characters. It appears in the output files and is not used in any calculation. 3 gis_id - Object number in the GIS interface. Not used in calculations. The SWAT+ Editor renumbers objects consecutively when it writes the files, so gis_id and id often differ; use id when matching a channel to a stream gauge. 4 area ha Area of the object. See Area, location and elevation. 5 lat decimal degrees Latitude. 6 lon decimal degrees Longitude. Not used in calculations. 7 elev m Elevation. 8 property column (hru, hlt, rtu, aqu, lcha, res, rec, exc, dlr, out) - Row number in the property file listed in the table above. Called obj in earlier documentation. In recall.con this column is not used: a recall object uses the recall.rec record whose id equals the recall object's id. 9 wst - Weather station name from weather-sta.cli. See Weather station lookup. 10 cst - Constituent pointer. Read but not used. 11 ovfl - Overbank flooding pointer. Read but has no effect in 62.0.1. 12 rule - Name of a flow-control decision table in flo_con.dtl, or null. See Flow-control rule. 13 out_tot - Number of outflow connections that follow on the line. May be 0.

For each of the out_tot connections, four values follow:

Offset Column Units Description +1 obj_typ - Type code of the receiving object. See Receiving object codes. +2 obj_id - Row number of the receiving object in its connect file. +3 hyd_typ - Which outflow hydrograph of this object is sent. See Hydrograph codes. +4 frac fraction Fraction of that hydrograph sent to the receiving object.

When out_tot is 0 the row ends after column 13 and the object sends no outflow through this file. HRUs that belong to a routing unit are usually written this way, because the routing unit collects their outflow (see rout_unit.def and rout_unit.ele).

docs.title: Area, location and elevation
docs.text:
The area value is used in calculations for some object types only:

Object Use of area HRU Area of the HRU. Converts depths (mm) to volumes (m³) and loads per hectare to totals. Routing unit Area of the routing unit. Converts inflow volumes to depths when water is routed across it. Aquifer Area of the aquifer. Converts recharge, storage and seepage between mm and m³. HRU-lte Area of the HRU-lte. Converts runoff and sediment to totals. SWAT-DEG channel Used with aqu_cha.lin to order the channels linked to an aquifer by drainage area, and to express aquifer inflow as a depth in the channel output. See link files. Other objects Not used in calculations.

At the start of the run SWAT+ also adds up the drainage area of every object from the areas of the HRUs, routing units and recall objects upstream of it, weighted by frac, and writes the computed and the input areas to area_calc.out. Comparing the two columns in that file is a quick check of the routing.

elev is used for every object to adjust precipitation and temperature for the difference in elevation between the object and its weather data. With the lapse rates plaps (mm per km) and tlaps (°C per km) from parameters.bsn,

\[\Delta P = \mathrm{plaps}\,\frac{z_{obj} - z_{pcp}}{1000}, \qquad \Delta T = \mathrm{tlaps}\,\frac{z_{tmp} - z_{obj}}{1000}\]

where \(z_{obj}\) is elev and \(z_{pcp}\) and \(z_{tmp}\) are the elevations of the precipitation and temperature gauges, or of the weather generator station when the variable is simulated. For HRUs elev is also the elevation used to compute atmospheric pressure for potential evapotranspiration, and it can be changed in calibration with the parameter elev.

lat matters only for HRUs: an HRU with a negative latitude is treated as being in the Southern Hemisphere, and its yearly reset of base heat units and of skip operations happens on day 181 instead of 31 December.

docs.title: Weather station lookup
docs.text: The wst names are looked up in the list of stations read from weather-sta.cli with a binary search. The search assumes the stations are listed in ascending order of name (character-code order). If the stations are not in that order, or the name is not in the file, the object uses the first station in weather-sta.cli and no message is written.

docs.title: Receiving object codes
docs.text:
obj_typ accepts these codes:

Code Receiving object Notes hru HRU Inflow is routed across the HRU. See Inflow to HRUs and routing units. hlt HRU-lte ru Routing unit The routing unit and each HRU in it are registered as receivers. aqu Aquifer cha Channel in channel.con 62.0.1 does not run these legacy channels, so flow sent to them does not continue downstream. Use sdc for SWAT-DEG channels. res Reservoir exc Export coefficient Export coefficient objects are not run as part of the routing, so inflow to them has no effect. dr Delivery ratio The object multiplies its inflow by the ratios in delratio.del. out Outlet sdc SWAT-DEG channel in chandeg.con

A recall object cannot receive flow. The routing code also has a branch for gwflow cells as receivers, but its code is longer than the three characters obj_typ can store, so no value in a connect file can select it. Any other code is not recognised and leaves the connection without a receiving object, which is likely to stop the run.

docs.title: Hydrograph codes
docs.text:
hyd_typ selects one of the outflow hydrographs of the sending object:

Code HRU, HRU-lte, routing unit Aquifer Channel, reservoir, recall, outlet, export coefficient, delivery ratio tot Surface runoff + lateral flow + tile flow Return flow (groundwater discharge) Total outflow rhg Percolation out of the bottom of the soil profile (recharge) Deep seepage Not filled, sends nothing sur Surface runoff not used not used lat Lateral soil flow not used not used til Tile flow not used not used

Any other code is not recognised. The usual connections are tot from an HRU or routing unit to a channel together with rhg to its aquifer, and tot from an aquifer to a channel.

frac is not checked. The fractions of one hydrograph type from one object should add up to 1, otherwise water is created or lost. Fractions of different types are independent, which is why a routing unit can send 100% of tot to a channel and 100% of rhg to an aquifer. Sending both tot and one of its parts (sur, lat, til) counts that part twice.

docs.title: Inflow to HRUs and routing units
docs.text:
An HRU or routing unit that receives flow keeps surface, lateral and tile inflow separate, so it can route each through the right part of the landscape:

  • From another HRU, HRU-lte or routing unit with tot, the sender's surface runoff is added to surface runon, its lateral flow to lateral inflow and its tile flow to tile inflow.
  • From another HRU, HRU-lte or routing unit with sur, lat or til, that hydrograph goes to surface runon, lateral inflow or tile inflow. An rhg connection to an HRU or routing unit is accepted, but the water is not added anywhere.
  • From any other object (channel, aquifer, reservoir, recall and so on) the total outflow is added to surface runon, whatever hyd_typ says.

For all other receiving objects the selected hydrograph, multiplied by frac, is added to the object's inflow.

docs.title: Flow-control rule
docs.text: A rule name other than null is matched against the decision tables in flo_con.dtl when the files are read. In 62.0.1 the match is stored but no routine uses it, so rule does not change the outflow fractions during the run.

docs.title: Export coefficient objects
docs.text: In exco.con the exc column is the row number in exco.exc. The om name in that row selects a row of exco_om.exc, and that row becomes the object's outflow hydrograph. It is set once when the files are read and stays constant for the whole run. Send it on with hyd_typ tot.

docs.title: Groundwater flow (gwflow) models
docs.text: When the gwflow module is active (gwflow = 1 in codes.bsn) and object.cnt lists gwflow cells, any row that has at least one connection with obj_typ aqu has its connection count reduced by one after reading, because gwflow replaces the aquifer objects. The connection that is dropped is the last one on the line, which is the aquifer connection only when that connection is written last. Put aquifer connections at the end of the line in gwflow models.

docs.title: Routing loops
docs.text: SWAT+ orders the objects so that every object runs after all objects that send it flow. If the connections contain a loop, the ordering cannot finish: after 5000 passes SWAT+ writes the objects that could not be ordered, with their inflow objects, to looping.con, prints an error and stops.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
refdata/Osu_1hru/aquifer.con in the SWAT+ repository:

aquifer.con: written by SWAT+ editor v2.2.0 on 2023-03-22 04:25 for SWAT+ rev.60.5.4
      id  name                gis_id          area           lat           lon          elev       aqu               wst       cst      ovfl      rule   out_tot       obj_typ    obj_id       hyd_typ          frac  
       1  aqu001                   1      10.00000      35.64206     127.38513     322.26395         1    s35610n127290e         0         0         0         1          sdc         1           tot       1.00000

One aquifer of 10 ha that uses row 1 of aquifer.aqu and sends all of its return flow (tot) to SWAT-DEG channel 1.

refdata/Osu_1hru/rout_unit.con:

rout_unit.con: written by SWAT+ editor v2.2.0 on 2023-03-22 04:25 for SWAT+ rev.60.5.4
      id  name                gis_id          area           lat           lon          elev       rtu               wst       cst      ovfl      rule   out_tot       obj_typ    obj_id       hyd_typ          frac  
       1  rtu001                   1       10.0000      35.52014     127.32787     113.51276         1    s35610n127290e         0         0         0         2           sdc         1           tot       1.00000           aqu         1           rhg       1.00000

The routing unit sends its surface, lateral and tile flow (tot) to SWAT-DEG channel 1 and its recharge (rhg) to aquifer 1, each with fraction 1.0. The rule value 0 does not name a table in flo_con.dtl, so it has the same effect as null.

refdata/Osu_1hru/hru.con:

hru.con: written by SWAT+ editor v2.2.0 on 2023-03-22 04:25 for SWAT+ rev.60.5.4
      id  name                gis_id          area           lat           lon          elev       hru               wst       cst      ovfl      rule   out_tot  
       1  hru0001                  1           10       35.65311     127.36763     350.96629         1    s35610n127290e         0         0         0         0

The HRU has no connections in hru.con (out_tot = 0). Its outflow reaches the channel and the aquifer through the routing unit it belongs to.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
constituents.cs lists the pesticides, pathogens, heavy metals, salt ions and other constituents that a run simulates. The last group, the other constituents, is the constituent module: selenate (SeO₄), selenite (SeO₃) and boron in soils, aquifers, channels, reservoirs and wetlands. The module simulates sorption, selenium reduction and selenium release from shale, and the constituents move with water like the other dissolved substances.

The salt ion files are described on the salt inputs page. Apart from constituents.cs, which is named in file.cio, the files are not listed in file.cio; SWAT+ looks for them by name in the run directory.

docs.title: constituents.cs
docs.text:
The master list, named on the simulation line of file.cio (default constituents.cs). If the file is missing or named null, no pesticides, pathogens, salts or other constituents are simulated.

Line 1 is a title. Then come five groups, each as a count followed by that many names:

Group Count Names 1 number of pesticides pesticide names, matched by name to pesticide.pes 2 number of pathogens pathogen names, matched by name to pathogens.pth 3 number of heavy metals metal names, not matched to any database (see metals) 4 number of salt ions salt ion names, in the order given on the salt inputs page 5 number of other constituents constituent names

Each count is read from a separate line and the names that follow are read as one list, starting on the next line, so they can be on one line or several. A count of 0 still needs its names line: SWAT+ skips one line after the count, so leave a blank line (or any text) there. A pesticide or pathogen name that is not in its database is kept in the list but gets no parameters.

The constituent module uses the position of each constituent and not its name. Fertilizer input, selenium reactions and the reservoir parameters assume this order:

Position Constituent 1 seo4 (selenate) 2 seo3 (selenite) 3 boron

docs.title: File overview
docs.text: File Content Linked to objects by cs_hru.ini Initial dissolved and sorbed constituents in HRU soils cs column of soil_plant.ini cs_aqu.ini Initial dissolved and sorbed constituents in aquifers cs column of initial.aqu_cs cs_channel.ini Initial concentrations in channels cs column of initial.cha_cs cs_res Reservoir and wetland parameters and initial concentrations cs column of reservoir.res_cs and wetland.wet_cs cs_irrigation Concentrations in irrigation water from outside the model position, see below fertilizer.frt_cs Constituent content of fertilizers and manures position in the fertilizer list cs_reactions Reaction parameters for soils and aquifers HRU and aquifer order cs_uptake Daily constituent uptake by each plant position in plants.plt cs_atmo.cli Concentration in rainfall and dry deposition atmospheric deposition stations, see climate inputs cs_recall.rec Loads from point sources see recall inputs cs_plants_boron Boron tolerance of plants read but not used cs_urban Constituent content of sediment from impervious areas read but not used cs_streamobs Channels for daily concentration output not read

docs.title: Missing files
docs.text:
cs_hru.ini, cs_aqu.ini and cs_channel.ini are opened whether or not they exist. If one is missing, SWAT+ creates an empty file of that name in the run directory and reads no records from it. An empty file, whether created this way or supplied, is read the same way.

The test project refdata/Ames_sub1 in the SWAT+ repository contains empty cs_hru.ini, cs_aqu.ini and cs_channel.ini files created by earlier runs. It gives null for the constituent file in file.cio, so no constituents are simulated and the empty files have no effect on the results. If constituents are listed in constituents.cs, an empty file behaves as follows:

  • Empty cs_hru.ini: there is no record for the HRUs, but HRU setup still reads record 1, which does not exist. Give at least one record.
  • Empty cs_aqu.ini: when initial.aqu_cs is present, the aquifer search runs over the number of records in cs_irrigation and reads cs_aqu.ini records that do not exist. Give at least as many records as cs_irrigation has.
  • Empty cs_channel.ini: there is no record for the channels, but channel setup still reads record 1, which does not exist. Give at least one record.

Two files are needed as soon as other constituents are listed in constituents.cs, because they are read for every HRU without a check that they were found:

  • cs_irrigation is read for every HRU during setup.
  • cs_uptake is read every day for every HRU with a growing plant.

Provide both whenever constituents are simulated, with zero values if there is nothing to add.

docs.title: cs_hru.ini
docs.text:
Initial constituents in HRU soils. Lines 1 to 5 are skipped. Each record then takes three lines:

Line of record Content 1 Record name 2 Soil values: one dissolved concentration (mg/L) per constituent, then one sorbed concentration (mg/kg of soil) per constituent 3 Plant values: the same number of values, read but not used

An HRU uses the record named in the cs column of its soil_plant.ini record; if the name is not found, the first record is used. soil_plant.ini has the cs column only when event in codes.bsn is not 0. With event at 0, the column is not read and every HRU uses the first record of cs_hru.ini. Every soil layer starts with the same values.

docs.title: cs_aqu.ini
docs.text:
Initial constituents in aquifers. Lines 1 to 3 are skipped. Each later line is one record: name, one dissolved concentration (mg/L) per constituent, then one sorbed concentration (mg/kg) per constituent. The sorbed mass is calculated with an assumed aquifer bulk density of 2000 kg/m³.

Aquifers find their record through initial.aqu_cs (title, header, then rows with name, pest, path, hmet, salt, cs). Aquifer \(n\) uses row \(n\) of initial.aqu_cs, whatever the row's name, and the cs column of that row names a record in cs_aqu.ini. See salt inputs for the same link used by salts.

docs.title: cs_channel.ini
docs.text: Initial concentrations in channel water. Lines 1 and 2 are skipped. Each later line is one record: name and one concentration (mg/L) per constituent. Channels find their record through initial.cha_cs as described for salt_channel.ini, using its cs column.

docs.title: cs_res
docs.text:
Constituent parameters and initial concentrations for reservoirs and wetlands. Lines 1 to 15 are skipped (two title lines, twelve comment lines and a header). The file is ignored when the reservoir nutrient file in file.cio is null. Each later line is one record:

# Column Units Default Description 1 name - - Record name, named in the cs column of reservoir.res_cs or wetland.wet_cs. 2 v_seo4 m/day 0.001 Settling velocity of selenate. 3 v_seo3 m/day 0.001 Settling velocity of selenite. 4 v_born m/day 0.001 Settling velocity of boron. 5 k_seo4 1/day 0.05 First-order loss rate of selenate. 6 k_seo3 1/day 0.03 First-order loss rate of selenite. 7 k_born 1/day 0.0 First-order loss rate of boron. 8 theta_seo4 - 1.08 Temperature factor for the selenate rate. 9 theta_seo3 - 1.08 Temperature factor for the selenite rate. 10 theta_born - 1.08 Temperature factor for the boron rate. 11 c_seo4 mg/L 0.0 Initial selenate concentration. 12 c_seo3 mg/L 0.0 Initial selenite concentration. 13 c_born mg/L 0.0 Initial boron concentration.

All 13 values must be given; a short line takes its remaining values from the next line. A reservoir without a cs_res record starts with no constituents and uses the default rates in the table. reservoir.res_cs and wetland.wet_cs are described under salt_res.

docs.title: cs_irrigation
docs.text:
Concentrations in irrigation water from outside the model. Lines 1 and 2 are skipped. Each later line is one record: name and one concentration (mg/L) per constituent.

An HRU uses the record at the same position as the cs_hru.ini record it uses; the name is not used. In 62.0.1 the transfer of constituents with irrigation water is switched off in water allocation, so these concentrations do not change the constituent balance.

docs.title: fertilizer.frt_cs
docs.text:
Constituent content of each fertilizer. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a header. Then one row per record of fertilizer.frt, in the same order and with the same number of rows:

# Column Units Description 1 name - Fertilizer name. Not checked against fertilizer.frt. 2 seo4 kg/kg Selenate per kg of material applied. 3 seo3 kg/kg Selenite per kg of material applied. 4 boron kg/kg Boron per kg of material applied.

The mass added (kg/ha) is the amount applied (kg/ha) times the value in the table. Constituents are added in the same cases as salts (see salt_fertilizer.frt): with manure operations and decision-table manure actions whose manure has an org_min entry other than the first record of manure_om.frt, and with fertilizer operations on HRUs with standing water. For manure, the whole amount goes into the top soil layer.

docs.title: cs_reactions
docs.text:
Reaction parameters for soils and aquifers, organised in reaction groups and shale formations. Every HRU and every aquifer must have a row.

Section Content Line 1, 2 Title and header, skipped Line 3 Number of parameters \(n_p\) and number of reaction groups \(n_g\) next \(n_p\) lines One parameter per line, with one value per reaction group next line Header, skipped next line Number of shale formations \(n_s\) next \(n_s\) lines Per shale formation: S/Se ratio of the shale, rate constant for autotrophic reduction of oxygen (1/day), rate constant for autotrophic reduction of nitrate (1/day) next line Header, skipped next lines One line per HRU, in HRU order: HRU number, reaction group, \(n_s\) shale fractions (fraction of the HRU area over each shale formation) next line Header, skipped (only when the model has aquifers) next lines One line per aquifer, in aquifer order: aquifer number, reaction group, \(n_s\) shale fractions

The parameter lines are used in this order:

Line Parameter Units Used for 1 Selenium reduction inhibition factor for nitrate - soils, aquifers 2 Oxygen concentration in soil water mg/L soils 3 Oxygen concentration in groundwater mg/L aquifers 4 Sorption coefficient \(K_d\) of selenate L/kg soils, aquifers 5 Sorption coefficient \(K_d\) of selenite L/kg soils, aquifers 6 Sorption coefficient \(K_d\) of boron L/kg soils, aquifers 7 Rate constant for selenate reduction in soil 1/day soils 8 Rate constant for selenate reduction in groundwater 1/day aquifers

The first value of the HRU and aquifer lines is not checked; the line position decides. Further parameter lines are read but not used by soils and aquifers. The rate constant for selenite reduction is not read for soils or aquifers and stays 0, so selenite is not reduced there.

docs.title: cs_uptake
docs.text: Specified daily constituent uptake by plants. Lines 1 to 3 are skipped. Then one row per plant in plants.plt, in the same order: name and one uptake value (kg/ha per day) per constituent. The plant name is not checked. While a plant has roots, its daily uptake of each constituent is split between the soil layers in proportion to the root mass in each layer and is limited to the mass in the layer.

docs.title: cs_plants_boron
docs.text: Boron tolerance of plants. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is skipped, line 3 is a switch (0 = off, 1 = on), lines 4 to 7 are skipped, and then one row per plant in plants.plt: name, threshold \(a\) and slope \(b\). In 62.0.1 the values are read but no routine uses them, so boron has no effect on plant growth.

docs.title: cs_urban
docs.text: Constituent content of sediment washed from impervious areas. Lines 1 and 2 are skipped. Each later line is an urban type name from urban.urb and one concentration (mg per kg of sediment) per constituent. In 62.0.1 the values are read but not used.

docs.title: cs_streamobs
docs.text: A list of channels for daily concentration and load output to cs_streamobs_output: a title line, the number of channels, then one channel number per line. In 62.0.1 the switch that would read it is never set, so the file is not read and the output is not written.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
constituents.cs for a run with one pesticide, the eight salt ions and the three constituents:

constituents.cs: constituent list
1
atrazine
0

0

8
so4 ca mg na k cl co3 hco3
3
seo4 seo3 boron

There are no pathogens or heavy metals, so their counts are 0 and each is followed by an empty names line.

A matching cs_aqu.ini record with 0.005 mg/L selenate in groundwater and 0.2 mg/kg sorbed selenate, values illustrative:

cs_aqu.ini: initial constituents in aquifers
seo4 seo3 boron: dissolved (mg/L), then sorbed (mg/kg)
name          seo4     seo3    boron   seo4_s   seo3_s  boron_s
aqu_cs1      0.005    0.001    0.100    0.200    0.050    1.000

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
A decision table is a set of rules. Each day SWAT+ checks the table's conditions for an object (an HRU, a reservoir, a water allocation object), finds which of the table's alternatives are satisfied, and performs the actions that those alternatives switch on. Decision tables drive automatic management (planting, harvest, fertilizer, irrigation), reservoir and paddy releases, land use change scenarios, and water allocation demands. See decision tables for the concept.

There are four decision table files. Their names are given on the decision_table line of file.cio, in this order:

File Default name Used by land use and management lum.dtl HRUs, through the automatic operations listed in management.sch; HRU-lte growing seasons; manure demands in manure_allo.mnu; irrigation demands, outside-source concentrations and treatment in water allocation reservoir release res_rel.dtl reservoirs and HRU wetlands or paddies that name a release table (see *.res and *.wet) land use scenarios scen_lu.dtl tables listed in scen_dtl.upd, checked for every HRU every day flow control flo_con.dtl saturated buffers, and water allocation demand and source or receiver fractions

A file that is missing, or named null in file.cio, gives an empty set of tables.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
All four files have the same layout. Free format, whitespace-separated.

  • Line 1: title (skipped).
  • Line 2: the number of decision tables in the file.
  • Line 3: skipped (normally blank).
  • Then each table in turn:
    • a header line (skipped);
    • the table line: name, conds, alts, acts (table name, number of conditions, number of alternatives, number of actions);
    • a header line (skipped);
    • conds condition rows;
    • a header line (skipped);
    • acts action rows;
    • in res_rel.dtl, scen_lu.dtl and flo_con.dtl only: one more line, which is skipped. Leave a blank line here. Without it the next table's header is skipped in its place and the following lines are read out of step.

The counts on the table line must match the rows that follow. Extra or missing rows shift every later table. Names are matched exactly, and a name that is not found is not reported.

docs.title: Condition rows
docs.text:
# Column Description 1 var Condition variable (see Condition variables). 2 obj Object type the variable belongs to, for example hru, res, null. For prob_unif, this column contains the application probability instead (see below). 3 obj_num Object number. 0 means the object the table is being checked for. 4 lim_var Limit variable. A name (land use, plant, soil group) or a reference volume, depending on the condition. null when not used. 5 lim_op Limit operator: *, +, - or /. Combines lim_var with lim_const for soil_water, vol and vol_wet. - when not used. 6 lim_const Limit constant. 7 and on alt1, alt2, ... One alternative operator per alternative.

For most conditions the current value of the variable is compared with lim_const. For soil_water, vol and vol_wet it is compared with a target built from lim_var, lim_op and lim_const, for example "emergency volume × 0.8".

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
Each alternative is a column of operators, one per condition. An alternative is satisfied when every one of its conditions is true. For numeric conditions the operators are:

Operator Condition is true when < value < limit > value > limit <= value ≤ limit >= value ≥ limit = value = limit /= value ≠ limit - always (the condition does not apply to this alternative)

Any other text in a numeric condition's alternative column is treated like -. In particular / does not mean "not equal" for numeric conditions.

The yes/no conditions (plant_gro, plant_name_gro, hyd_soil_group, land_use, cal_group, tillage, prob_unif, prob_unif1, prob_unif_lu, ch_order) use only =, meaning the condition must be true. tile_drained and plant_com also accept /, meaning the condition must be false. Every other operator is treated like -.

docs.title: Action rows
docs.text:
# Column Description 1 act_typ Action type (see Land use and management actions and Reservoir release actions). 2 obj Object type. For irrigate, the type of the water source. 3 obj_num Object number. 0 means the object the table is being checked for. 4 name Action name. Used to link days_act conditions to this action, and by irrigate, irr_demand and puddle as described below. Otherwise free text. 5 option Action option, specific to the action type. 6 const First action constant. 7 const2 Second action constant. In lum.dtl, values below 1 are raised to 1. 8 fp File pointer: a name in another input file, specific to the action type. 9 and on outcome1, outcome2, ... y or n for each alternative.

An action runs when at least one alternative is satisfied and the action's outcome for that alternative is y. Actions run in the order of the rows.

In lum.dtl, many actions use const2 as the maximum number of times the action may run in a calendar year for each HRU. The count is reset on 31 December. These actions are marked "per year: const2" in the table below.

docs.title: Condition variables
docs.text:
Units are those of the compared value. "Plants" means the plants of the HRU's plant community.

var Value compared Notes w_stress Average water stress factor of the growing plants (1 = no stress) 1 when no plant is growing. n_stress Average nitrogen stress factor of the growing plants 0 when no plant is growing. p_stress Average phosphorus stress factor of the growing plants 0 when no plant is growing. phu_plant Fraction of potential heat units accumulated by the first plant that has started accumulating (plant 1 if none) phu_base0 Fraction of the annual base-zero heat units accumulated at the HRU's weather station obj must be hru or hlt. precip_cur Precipitation today, mm obj must be hru or hlt. precip_next Precipitation tomorrow, mm obj must be hru or hlt. plant_gro Plant number lim_const (1 if 0) is growing Yes/no. plant_name_gro The plant named in lim_var is in the community and growing Yes/no. days_plant Days since the last planting days_harv Days since the last harvest days_irr Days since the last irrigation days_act Days since the action named in lim_var (an action name in the weather generator p_lab_150 Labile phosphorus in the upper soil, ppm Uses the first two soil layers. soil_temp2 Temperature of soil layer 2, °C soil_carbon Organic carbon of soil layer 1, % tile_drained The HRU has tile drains = true, / false. prob A uniform random number between 0 and 1 Compared with lim_const; use < to act with probability lim_const. prob_unif Today is the drawn application day See Probability conditions. prob_unif1 Random draw within a window that starts on 1 January See Probability conditions. prob_unif_lu Random draw that spreads an operation over the HRUs of a land use See Probability conditions. channel_flo Flow in the current hydrograph, m³/s tile_flo Tile flow from the HRU today, mm irr_demand Irrigation demand of the HRU, m³ irr_pou_dmd Demand of (principal volume) or evol (emergency volume) combined with lim_const by lim_op. With + and -, lim_const is in ha·m. With lim_var e-pv, the target is \(V_p + \mathrm{lim\_const}\,(V_e - V_p)\). res_inflo Inflow to reservoir obj_num, m³/s wet_depth Water depth of the HRU wetland or paddy lim_const in mm. weirh Weir height of the HRU wetland or paddy lim_const in mm. vol_wet Water volume of the HRU wetland or paddy, m³ Target: lim_var pvol or evol combined with lim_const by lim_op.

docs.title: Probability conditions
docs.text:
These three conditions let an operation happen on a random day within a window instead of on a fixed date.

prob_unif uses the columns differently from other conditions: obj is the probability \(f\) that the operation happens at all this year, obj_num is the first day of the window and lim_const is the last day (day of year). On the first day of the window SWAT+ decides, with probability \(f\), whether the operation will happen this year, and if so draws one day in the window at random. The condition is true only on that day. A window that ends before it starts (for example 330 to 30) runs over the turn of the year.

prob_unif1 uses obj_num as a calendar year and lim_const as a number of days. The window starts on 1 January of that year. On each day of the window the condition is true with probability \(1/n\), where \(n\) is the number of days left in the window.

prob_unif_lu uses obj_num as the first day and lim_const as the last day of the window. It is meant to be combined with a land_use condition in the same table: it spreads the operation over the HRUs of that land use so that the share of HRUs treated by day \(d\) follows a uniform distribution over the window.

docs.title: Land use and management actions
docs.text:
Actions in lum.dtl. Unless stated otherwise, obj is hru and obj_num 0 means the HRU being checked.

act_typ option const const2 fp Effect plant plant name in the community - - name in transplant.ops Starts growth of the plant if it is not already growing. With a transplant entry, the plant starts from the transplant state (see management.sch). harvest plant name, or all residue harvest efficiency per year name in harv.ops Harvests the plant. harvest_kill plant name, or all residue harvest efficiency per year name in harv.ops Harvests and kills the plant. kill plant name, or all - per year - Kills the plant; biomass becomes residue. till, tillage name in tillage.til - per year - Tillage. fertilize name in fertilizer.frt amount, kg/ha per year name in chem_app.ops Applies fertilizer. On an HRU with standing water and a method with surf_frac 1, the fertilizer goes into the water. fert_future name in fertilizer.frt amount, kg/ha day of year name in chem_app.ops Schedules a fertilizer application on the given day. obj_num is the sequence number of the fert_future action in the table. manure - amount, kg/ha per year - In 62.0.1 the manure and method names are not looked up, so this action applies an empty fertilizer entry. Use fertilize with a manure from fertilizer.frt, or manure_demand. manure_demand name in chem_app.ops amount, t/ha per year - Sets a manure request for manure allocation. obj_num is the manure source number. pest_apply pesticide name listed in constituents.cs amount, kg/ha per year name in chem_app.ops Applies the amount times the method's app_eff. graze name in graze.ops - - - One day of grazing. burn name in fire.ops - per year - Burns plants and residue. irrigate name in irr.ops depth, mm per year - Irrigates with \(\mathrm{const} \cdot \mathrm{eff\_frac} \cdot (1-\mathrm{sumq\_frac})\). obj and obj_num name the source: aqu, cha or sdc, or res takes the water from that object and irrigates nothing if it has too little; any other obj (for example hru) is an unlimited source. With name ponding, the HRU is a paddy: const is the target ponding depth (mm), const2 the depth below which water is added, and the depth applied is the shortfall from the target. irr_demand name in irr.ops depth, mm per year unlim or other Sets the HRU's irrigation demand for water allocation (\(\mathrm{const} \times\) area). With fp unlim, the amt_mm of the irr.ops entry is applied directly. With name ponding, const and const2 are the target and threshold ponding depths (mm). res_irr_dmd - depth, mm - - Records an irrigation demand on reservoir obj_num. rot_reset - rotation year - - Sets the rotation year (minimum 1). plant_reset, harv_reset, kill_reset, irr_reset - days - - Sets the days since the last planting, harvest, kill or irrigation (minimum 1). pheno_reset - - per year - Restarts the phenology of plants with a moisture_gro trigger in plants.plt. cn_update absval, abschg, pctchg or relchg value per year - Changes the curve number for moisture condition II: set to the value, add the value, change by the value in percent, or multiply by (1 + value). The result is kept between 35 and 95. tiledep_control - drain depth, mm per year - Sets the tile drain depth for drainage water management. impound_on - - - name in wetland.wet Turns on impounded water (paddy or wetland) on the HRU. impound_off - - - - Turns off impounded water on the HRU. weir_height wet, or other height, mm - - With wet, sets the HRU paddy weir height and the principal and emergency volumes from it. Otherwise sets the weir height of reservoir obj_num. puddle name in puddle.ops - per year - Puddles a paddy (see management.sch). The action name must be the tillage operation in tillage.til used for the soil mixing. lu_change - - - name in landuse.lum Changes the HRU's land use and management and reinitialises plants and curve number. Logged in lu_change_out.txt. snow_change - - - name in snow.sno Switches the HRU to another snow parameter set. Logged in lu_change_out.txt. hru_fr_update new ls_unit.ele file - - new rout_unit.ele file Updates HRU area fractions. Logged in lu_change_out.txt. p_factor - new USLE P - - Sets the USLE P factor. contour - - - - Sets \(P = 2.7\,S + 0.26\), with \(S\) the slope (m/m). stripcrop - - - pasture or other Sets \(P = 2.32\,S + 0.36\), halved when fp is pasture. terrace - - - sod_outlet or other Sets \(P = 1.4\,S + 0.13\), doubled when fp is sod_outlet. tile_install - - - name in tiledrain.str Installs tile drains (see *.str). septic_install - - - name in septic.str Installs a septic system. fstrip_install - - - name in filterstrip.str Installs a filter strip. grassww_install, grassww_uninstall - - - name in grassedww.str Installs or removes a grassed waterway. user_def_bmp - - - name in bmpuser.str Applies user-defined BMP removal fractions. grow_init, grow_end - - - - Start and end of the growing season of an HRU-lte (obj hlt). grow_end computes the yield. chan_change - cover stream order - Sets the cover and stream order of the channel being checked. herd - - - - No effect in 62.0.1.

The plant, harvest and harvest_kill actions of the generic tables pl_hv_summer1, pl_hv_winter1 and pl_hv_summer2 take the plant name from management.sch instead of option (see management.sch).

Flow control and water allocation actions, used in flo_con.dtl:

act_typ option const const2 Effect tileflo_control flo_mm, max_mm (at most const mm), min_mm (at least const mm), all_flo, zero_flo, frac (const × tile flow) mm or fraction - Sets the tile flow sent from a saturated buffer source HRU to its receiving HRU. wallo_dmd set_dmd demand, m³ - Sets the demand of a water allocation place of use. wallo_dmd irr_dmd - - Adds the irrigation demand of place of use obj_num. wallo_dmd fill_res, fill_wtow, fill_can target fraction of capacity fraction of the shortfall per day Demand to fill reservoir, water tower or canal obj_num to const times its capacity (for fill_res, fp pvol or evol). duty_fr fr1 to fr6 fraction - Fraction of the demand taken from point of diversion 1 to 6 (or sent to return 1 to 6). duty_reset - point of diversion number new maximum withdrawal Resets the withdrawal limit of a point of diversion of place of use obj_num.

See water allocation for how these demands and fractions are used.

docs.title: Reservoir release actions
docs.text:
In res_rel.dtl the action type is release and option selects how the release is computed. The releases of all actions that run on a day are added together. A table with zero alternatives runs all its actions every day. \(V\) is the current volume, \(V_p\) the principal and \(V_e\) the emergency volume.

option const const2 fp Release rate rate, m³/s - - constant rate rate_pct percent - - const % of \(V_p\) per day inflo_rate maximum rate, m³/s change to inflow, m³/s - the larger of inflow + const2 and const inflo_frac fraction - - const × inflow ab_emer - - - all volume above \(V_e\) days days multiplier null, pvol or evol \((V - V_t)/\mathrm{const}\), with target \(V_t\) = 0, const2 × \(V_p\) or const2 × \(V_e\) dyrt days percent null, pvol or evol \((V - V_t)/\mathrm{const}\) plus const2 % of \(V_p\), with \(V_t\) = 0, \(V_p\) or \(V_e\) dyrt1 days percent con1, con2 or con3 as dyrt, with the target taken from condition 5, 4 or 3 of the table inflo_targ condition number - - inflow plus all volume above \(V_p\) × that condition's lim_const weir - - name in weir.res weir equation meas - - name of a recall object measured outflow natlake inactive storage, fraction of \(V_p\) release coefficient, 1/day - natural lake outflow (Döll et al., 2003) nonirr-h06 \(\alpha\) - - Hanazaki et al. (2006) scheme for non-irrigation reservoirs irr-h06 \(\alpha\) \(\beta\) - Hanazaki et al. (2006) scheme for irrigation reservoirs hydrop amplitude phase - HYPE hydropower scheme (Arheimer et al., 2019)

See *.res for the reservoir side of these options.

docs.title: Land use scenarios
docs.text: Tables in scen_lu.dtl run only if they are listed in scen_dtl.upd. That file has a title line, the number of entries, a header line, and one row per entry with three columns: max_hits, typ and the name of a table in scen_lu.dtl. Each listed table is checked for every HRU every day, before the HRUs are simulated. The usual actions are lu_change and snow_change.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
refdata/Ames_sub1/lum.dtl in the SWAT+ repository contains two tables:

lum.dtl: yearly irrigation limit example for Ames dataset
2

name                     conds      alts      acts       !limit yearly irrigation to 500 mm using irrigate action
irr_year_irr                4         1         1
var                        obj   obj_num           lim_var            lim_op  lim_const      alt1
irr_year                   hru         0              null                 -   500.00000         <
w_stress                   hru         0              null                 -   0.80000           <
phu_plant                  hru         0           phu_mat                 -     0.20000         >
leaf_area                  hru         0           null                    -     0.50000         >
act_typ                    obj   obj_num              name            option    const        const2                fp  outcome
irrigate                   hru        0           sprinkler     sprinkler_ilm    25.00000   20.00000  unlim  y

Table irr_year_irr has four conditions, one alternative and one action. The alternative is satisfied on a day when the irrigation applied so far is below 500 mm, the average water stress factor is below 0.8, the crop has accumulated more than 20% of its heat units, and the leaf area index is above 0.5. On such a day the HRU is irrigated with 25 mm using the sprinkler_ilm entry of irr.ops, at most 20 times a year. obj is hru, so the water comes from an unlimited source. The table is used by naming irr_year_irr as an automatic operation in management.sch. In 62.0.1 the irrigation total behind irr_year is not reset each year, so once 500 mm has been applied over the whole run, the table stops irrigating for the rest of the simulation.

A reservoir table from refdata/Osu_1hru/res_rel.dtl, followed by the blank line that res_rel.dtl needs:

wet_depth                  hru         0          weir_hgt                 -       0.00000         >       -
wet_depth                  hru         0              null                 -       2.00000         >       >

Both alternatives need a water depth above 2 mm, and the first also above 0 mm. When the first alternative is satisfied, the paddy releases its whole volume within one day (days with const 1 and target 0) and also releases over the weir weir1.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: file.cio is the master index of a SWAT+ project. It is the first file SWAT+ opens, and it must be in the run folder under that name. Each line names the files for one input category, so every other input file is reached through file.cio. The last six lines give optional folders for the weather data files and for the output files.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Line 1 is a title and is skipped. Lines 2 to 26 each start with a category label and continue with file names in a fixed order. Lines 27 to 31 each give one weather data folder, and line 32 gives the output folder.

The reader takes the lines by position. The category label is read and discarded, so its text is not checked, and the file names are matched to slots by their order on the line. Values are separated by spaces.

  • Write null for a file the project does not use. Most readers treat a name that does not exist in the run folder the same way as null and skip the file. The exceptions are listed under Missing and null files.
  • File names can be up to 25 characters long. Longer names are cut to 25 characters.
  • Each line must give at least as many names as its category has slots. If a line is short, the reader continues onto the next line to fill the missing slots, and every later line is then read one line out of step. Extra names at the end of a line are ignored.

docs.title: Unused slots
docs.text:
These names are read from file.cio, but SWAT+ 62.0.1 never opens the file they name. Any name or null can be given.

  • connect: aquifer2d.con (slot 6).
  • routing_unit: rout_unit.dr (slot 4).
  • herd: all three slots.
  • hru_parm_db: metals.mtl and salt.slt (slots 6 and 7).
  • init: hmet_water.ini, salt_hru.ini and salt_water.ini (slots 9 to 11).
  • regions: ls_cal.reg and ch_catunit.ele (slots 5 and 6).

Two of these files are read under a fixed name instead. When salts are simulated, the HRU salt initial conditions come from a file named salt_hru.ini in the run folder, whatever slot 10 of the init line says. Channel catchment unit elements come from a file named element.ccu.

The climate line has no wind direction file. It has nine slots, and slot 3 is pet.cli.

docs.title: Missing and null files
docs.text:
For most slots, a name of null or a name that does not exist in the run folder means the file is skipped and the related feature is off. Some files behave differently:

  • object.cnt: if it is missing or null, SWAT+ prints Cannot find object.cnt input file and stops.
  • carbon.bsn: read only when carbon = 2 in codes.bsn. It is then required, and SWAT+ stops with an error, written to the screen and to diagnostics.out, if the file named in slot 3 of the basin line does not exist or cannot be opened. The per-layer carbon file has no slot on the line: its name is built from the carbon file name, so carbon.bsn gives carbon_lyr.bsn.
  • time.sim and print.prt: there is no check for a missing file. If the name is not null and the file does not exist, SWAT+ creates an empty file of that name and continues with built-in values. For time.sim this leaves the run without a valid simulation period, so the file is required in practice.
  • place_of_use.wro and point_of_diver.wro: if either is missing or null, SWAT+ creates an empty file of that name (a file called null in the second case), reads nothing from it, and water allocation is off. See water allocation.
  • chan-surf.lin: if the name is not null and the file does not exist, SWAT+ creates an empty file of that name. See link files.

docs.title: Weather data folders
docs.text:
Lines 27 to 31 let the precipitation, temperature, solar radiation, humidity and wind data files be kept outside the run folder. Each line has a label and one value of up to 80 characters. A value of null means the data files are in the run folder.

SWAT+ joins the folder and the file name from the climate index file (for example pcp.cli) without adding a separator, so the folder must end with / or \. The folder is read in the same way as a file name, with two consequences:

  • A folder name that contains spaces must be in quotes.
  • An unquoted / ends the value. data/pcp/ is read as data, and an unquoted value that starts with / is read as empty, so the files are looked for in the run folder. Put any folder that uses forward slashes in quotes, for example "C:/swat/weather/pcp/", or use backslashes on Windows.

There is no folder line for potential evapotranspiration data. Files listed in pet.cli are always read from the run folder.

docs.title: Output folder
docs.text:
Line 32 is optional. It has a label (any word) and a folder name. SWAT+ reads the whole line, drops the first word and takes the rest of the line as the folder, so the folder name can contain spaces and forward slashes without quotes. Up to 256 characters are kept. If the line is missing or empty, or the folder is null or NULL, the output files are written to the run folder.

When a folder is given, SWAT+ converts the separators to the ones the operating system uses, creates the folder and any missing parent folders, and prints Output path set to: with the folder name. A relative folder is taken from the run folder. On Linux and macOS a folder that contains : is treated as a Windows path, and SWAT+ stops with an error. On Windows a folder that starts with / is placed on drive C:. SWAT+ also stops if it cannot create or open the folder.

The standard output files go to this folder, including files_out.out, diagnostics.out, checker.out and the time series outputs switched on in print.prt. In 62.0.1 the gwflow output files and the soft calibration output files (hru-out.cal, hru-new.cal and others) are still written to the run folder.

docs.title: Older file.cio files
docs.text:
Two lines changed length in recent revisions, and a file.cio written for an earlier revision needs both updated before it is run with 62.0.1:

  • The basin line now has three slots. Add carbon.bsn or null after parameters.bsn. With only two names on the basin line, SWAT+ takes the first word of line 4 (climate) as the carbon file name and discards the rest of that line. Every later category is then read from the line below the one it belongs to: the climate files are taken from the connect line, the connection files from the channel line, and so on. No message reports the shift. If carbon = 2 in codes.bsn, SWAT+ stops with ERROR: climate is required when carbon is enabled; otherwise the run continues with wrong file names in every later slot.
  • The water_rights line (line 15) now has two slots, the place-of-use file and the point-of-diversion file. An older line with water_allocation.wro element.wro water_rights.wro makes SWAT+ read water_allocation.wro as the place-of-use file and element.wro as the point-of-diversion file, and the third name is ignored. See water allocation for those files.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Fertilizer and manure applications use three databases.

  • fertilizer.frt lists the fertilizer products: the fractions of mineral and organic nitrogen and phosphorus in each, and how much of the mineral nitrogen is ammonium. fert operations in management.sch and fertilize actions in decision tables name a row of this file.
  • manure_db.frt lists the manure types. Each one points to a row of manure_om.frt and names optional pesticide, pathogen, metal, salt and constituent profiles. manu operations in management.sch, manure actions in decision tables and the manure allocation file name a row of this file.
  • manure_om.frt gives the water, carbon and nutrient make-up of each manure.

fertilizer.frt is named on the hru_parm_db line of file.cio (default fertilizer.frt). The two manure files are not listed in file.cio. SWAT+ looks for them under the fixed names manure_db.frt and manure_om.frt, and leaves the manure databases empty when they are missing.

docs.title: fertilizer.frt
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one product with the values below in this order. The reader does not match columns by header name. It reads the first six values and ignores the rest of the line, so the pathogens and description columns written by the SWAT+ Editor have no effect.

# Column Units Default Description 1 name - - Name of the fertilizer, up to 16 characters. Must be unique. 2 min_n kg mineral N/kg fertilizer 0.0 Fraction of the fertilizer that is mineral nitrogen (nitrate plus ammonium). 3 min_p kg mineral P/kg fertilizer 0.0 Fraction of the fertilizer that is mineral phosphorus. 4 org_n kg organic N/kg fertilizer 0.0 Fraction of the fertilizer that is organic nitrogen. 5 org_p kg organic P/kg fertilizer 0.0 Fraction of the fertilizer that is organic phosphorus. 6 nh3_n kg NH3-N/kg mineral N 0.0 Fraction of the mineral nitrogen that is ammonium. The rest is nitrate.

The fractions are by weight of the product. min_n + min_p + org_n + org_p is the nutrient content and should not exceed 1; the remainder is carrier.

For a commercial fertilizer the grade gives the nitrogen and phosphate content. The phosphate value in a grade is P2O5, so it has to be converted to P (multiply by 0.44) before it goes into min_p.

docs.title: Fertilizer application
docs.text:
A fertilizer operation applies an amount in kg/ha of product. The application method row in chem_app.ops gives the fraction placed in the top 10 mm of soil (surf_frac); the rest goes into the second soil layer. In each of the two layers:

  • min_n × (1 − nh3_n) of the amount is added as nitrate and min_n × nh3_n as ammonium.
  • min_p of the amount is added as labile (soluble) phosphorus.
  • With carbon = 0 in codes.bsn, half of the organic N and P goes to the fresh residue pool and half to the active humus pool.
  • With carbon = 2, organic N and P are added to the soil organic matter pools with a carbon content of 10 times the organic N. The share that goes to the metabolic and structural litter pools depends on the C:N ratio. The split between the fresh and humus parts is manure_c_frac in carbon.bsn.

docs.text:
The first rows of refdata/Ames_sub1/fertilizer.frt in the SWAT+ repository:

elem_p                 0.00000       1.00000       0.00000       0.00000       0.00000              null  ElementalPhosphorous
anh_nh3                0.82000       0.00000       0.00000       0.00000       1.00000              null  AnhydrousAmmonia
urea                   0.46000       0.00000       0.00000       0.00000       1.00000              null  Urea
18_46_00               0.18000       0.20200       0.00000       0.00000       0.00000              null  18_46_00
dairy_fr               0.00700       0.00500       0.03100       0.00300       0.99000              null  Dairy_FreshManure

  • 18_46_00 is an 18-46-0 grade: 18% N and 46% P2O5, which is 20.2% P.
  • dairy_fr is fresh dairy manure, mostly organic N.
  • elem_n has nh3_n = 0, so all its nitrogen is applied as nitrate.

docs.title: manure_db.frt
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one manure type with eight values.

# Column Description 1 name Name of the manure type, up to 25 characters. Manure operations and the manure allocation file refer to it by this name. 2 org_min Name of a row in manure_om.frt that gives the water, carbon and nutrient make-up. 3 pests Name of a pesticide profile, or null. 4 paths Name of a pathogen profile, or null. 5 hmets Name of a heavy metal profile, or null. 6 salts Name of a salt profile, or null. 7 constit Name of a profile for other constituents, or null. 8 description Free text, one word.

In 62.0.1 the pests, paths, hmets, salts and constit names are read but not looked up. Salt and constituent loads in manure come from the fertilizer files of the salt and constituent modules, taken from the row in the same position as the manure type. They are added only when the manure type's org_min names the second or a later row of manure_om.frt.

A manure application takes its make-up from the row of manure_om.frt in the same position as the manure type in manure_db.frt (first with first, second with second). The org_min name is matched against manure_om.frt when the file is read, but the application does not use the match. Keep the two files in the same order, with org_min naming the row in the same position.

docs.title: manure_db.frt example
docs.text:
refdata/Osu_1hru/manure_db.frt:

manure_db.frt: manure database
name          org_min             pests  paths  hmets  salts  constit  description
beef_salt     mw_beef_liq         null   null   null   null   null     midwest_beef_liquid_salt

One manure type, beef_salt, using the mw_beef_liq make-up. mw_beef_liq is also the first row of manure_om.frt below, so the position used by the application and the org_min name agree. Because org_min names the first row, no salt or constituent loads are added when beef_salt is applied, whatever the salt and constituent fertilizer files contain.

docs.title: manure_om.frt
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one manure make-up with nine values.

# Column Units Description 1 name - Name of the make-up, up to 64 characters. 2 frac_water kg water/kg manure as applied Water fraction of the manure as applied. Must be below 1. 3 fcbn kg C/kg dry manure Carbon fraction. 4 fminn kg mineral N/kg dry manure Mineral nitrogen fraction (nitrate plus ammonium). 5 fminp kg mineral P/kg dry manure Mineral phosphorus fraction. 6 forgn kg organic N/kg dry manure Organic nitrogen fraction. 7 forgp kg organic P/kg dry manure Organic phosphorus fraction. 8 fnh3n kg NH3-N/kg mineral N Fraction of the mineral nitrogen that is ammonium. 9 description - Free text, one word.

docs.title: Manure application
docs.text:
The amount in a manure operation is the dry mass of manure in kg/ha. The nutrient fractions apply to that dry mass. The water that comes with it, amount / (1 − frac_water) − amount, is added to the soil water of the two top layers. As for fertilizer, surf_frac of the application method in chem_app.ops goes to the top 10 mm and the rest to the second layer.

Mineral N and P are added the same way as for fertilizer. With carbon = 0, the organic N and P are split between the fresh and humus pools with a fixed fraction of 0.5. With carbon = 2, carbon from fcbn and organic N and P go to the manure and litter pools, and the split uses manure_c_frac in carbon.bsn.

docs.title: manure_om.frt example
docs.text:
refdata/Osu_1hru/manure_om.frt:

manure_om.frt: manure organic matter database
name            frac_water   fcbn          fminn         fminp         forgn         forgp         fnh3n  description
mw_beef_liq     0.988        0.000780576   0.000311751   0.00081295    0.002110312   0.000365707   0.99   midwest_beef_liquid
mw_beef_slur    0.926        0.016786571   0.002697842   0.00081295    0.002110312   0.000365707   0.99   midwest_beef_slurry

Two make-ups of Midwest beef manure. The liquid form is 98.8% water and the slurry 92.6%. Applying 1000 kg/ha of mw_beef_liq adds about 82,300 kg/ha of water, or 8.2 mm.

docs.title: Related files
docs.text:

  • Decision tables: fertilize and manure actions.
