docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
gwflow is a cell-based groundwater model. When it is active it replaces the lumped aquifers, and aquifer.aqu, initial.aqu and the aquifer connect file are not used. The aquifer is divided into cells, and each day SWAT+ solves a water balance for every cell with Darcy flow between neighbouring cells. Cells exchange water with channels and receive recharge from HRUs or landscape units. Optional processes add groundwater ET, groundwater flow into the soil profile, saturation excess flow, tile drainage, pumping, exchange with reservoirs, wetlands, floodplains and canals, recharge ponds, phreatophyte uptake, solute transport and heat transport.

The inputs are spread over a set of small files, most of them with the .gw extension, one file for each part of the model. The files are not listed in file.cio; SWAT+ looks for them by name in the run directory. Units are metres, days and square metres unless a column says otherwise.

docs.title: Activation
docs.text:
Set gwflow to 1 in codes.bsn. At start-up SWAT+ then looks for chancell.gw:

  • If chancell.gw exists, gwflow is active. Unless object.cnt already gives a gwflow object count, SWAT+ counts the channel-cell rows in chancell.gw, uses that count as the number of gwflow objects, removes the aquifer objects from the object total, and reads the channel-cell connections from gwflow.con.
  • If chancell.gw is missing or empty, gwflow is reset to 0 and the run uses the lumped aquifers.

When gwflow is active SWAT+ writes a log of what it read and which options it switched on or off to gwflow_record. Check this file first when a gwflow run does not behave as expected.

When the count comes from chancell.gw, SWAT+ skips three lines before it starts counting, while the file has two lines before the first data row. The first channel-cell row is therefore not counted and the count is one less than the number of rows. chancell.gw is then read for that many rows, so the last row of the file is not used. Giving the gwflow count in object.cnt avoids this.

docs.title: File overview
docs.text:
File Required Read when Purpose chancell.gw yes always Channel-cell links, streambed zone, depth zone and observation flag gwflow.con yes always Connect file for the channel-cell objects codes.gw yes always Grid size, process switches, time step and output switches zones.gw yes always Aquifer and streambed parameters by zone cells.gw yes always Properties and initial state of every cell cellcon.gw yes always Neighbours of every cell outputs.gw yes always Observation wells and output times hrucell.gw one of the two conn_type 1, or 2 without lsucell.gw HRU-cell overlaps for recharge lsucell.gw one of the two conn_type 2, or 1 without hrucell.gw Landscape unit-cell overlaps for recharge chan_depth.gw no file exists Daily channel water depth per depth zone pumpex.gw no pumpex is 1 and file exists Specified pumping from cells hru_pump.gw no file exists HRUs to report irrigation pumping for tile.gw no tile is 1 and file exists Tile drain parameters and tile cells rescell.gw no res is 1 and file exists Reservoir-cell links gwflow.wetland no wet is 1 and file exists Wetland bed thickness floodplain.gw no fp is 1 and file exists Floodplain-cell links gwflow_canal.con no canal is 1 and file exists Canal-cell links phreato.gw, phreato_cell.gw no phreato.gw exists Phreatophyte ET curve and cells tvheads.gw no file exists Time-varying heads for boundary cells solute.gw no solute is 1 and file exists Solute transport settings and solute parameters cell_sol.gw no solute transport on and file exists Initial solute concentration per cell minerals.gw no solute transport on, salts simulated, file exists Salt mineral fractions per cell ponds.gw, pond_cell.gw no ponds.gw exists Recharge ponds and their cells pond_div.gw no ponds active and file exists Daily diversion into each pond sw_group.gw no file exists Groups of channel cells for exchange output transit.gw no structured grid and file exists Cells for transit-time output

When a switch in codes.gw is on and its file is missing, SWAT+ notes it in gwflow_record and the process is not simulated. For tile drainage, floodplain exchange and solute transport the switch is also turned off for the rest of the run.

docs.title: Format conventions
docs.text:
• Values are separated by spaces. Column widths do not matter.
  • Line 1 of every file is a title line and is skipped. Most tables have a column header on line 2, also skipped, and data from line 3. Files with a different layout are described in the section for that file.
  • Cell numbers run from 1 to ncell, in the order of cells.gw, and every file that names a cell uses these numbers.
  • Channel numbers are the numbers of the channels in the channel connect file (chandeg.con). Reservoir numbers follow the reservoir connect file.
  • In cells.gw and zones.gw, an optional value may be given as null, which means it is not set.

docs.title: codes.gw
docs.text:
Grid size, process switches and output switches. Line 1 is a title. Line 2 is a row of key names and line 3 is a row of values, one value under each key. SWAT+ pairs keys and values by position and recognises the keys by name, so the order of the columns does not matter and a missing key keeps its default (0, or empty for grid_type).

Key Units Description grid_type - structured (regular grid) or unstructured. Both use the same cell numbering. ncell - Number of cells. cells.gw and cellcon.gw must have this many rows. cell_size m Cell size of a structured grid. Read but not used; cell areas come from cells.gw. n_rows, n_cols - Rows and columns of a structured grid. Used only by the structured-grid sections of tile.gw and minerals.gw. bc_type - Default boundary condition for boundary cells: 1 = specified head, 2 = no flow. A cell can override it in cells.gw. conn_type - How recharge reaches the cells: 1 = from HRUs (hrucell.gw), 2 = from landscape units (lsucell.gw). Any other value stops the run. gw_soil 0/1 Groundwater transfer into the soil profile when the water table rises into it. Only with HRU connection. satx 0/1 Saturation excess flow: groundwater above the ground surface goes to the channel nearest to the cell. pumpex 0/1 Specified pumping from pumpex.gw. tile 0/1 Tile drainage from tile.gw. res 0/1 Exchange with reservoirs from rescell.gw. wet 0/1 Exchange with wetlands. Only with HRU connection. fp 0/1 Exchange with floodplains from floodplain.gw. canal 0/1 Seepage from canals in gwflow_canal.con. solute 0/1 Solute transport from solute.gw. heat 0/1 Heat transport. time_step day Flow time step. The day is split into int(1/time_step) steps, so use 1 or a fraction of a day such as 0.5. write_day, write_mon, write_yr, write_aa 0/1 Write the gwflow water balance files for each interval. river_thresh m Distance subtracted from every channel-bed elevation in chancell.gw before the channel exchange is calculated. 0 uses the elevations as given.

With LSU connection, SWAT+ turns gw_soil and wet off and says so in gwflow_record.

docs.title: Output switches in print.prt
docs.text:
The write_* keys are defaults. print.prt can list gwflow rows, and a row that is present replaces the corresponding setting before any gwflow output file is opened:

print.prt row Controls Without the row gwflow_wb Water balance files, by interval (replaces write_day to write_aa) write_* keys of codes.gw gwflow_obs Observation well files, by interval all four intervals written gwflow_pump HRU irrigation pumping output (on if any interval is y) on gwflow_flux Canal, pond, tile, channel-group and channel-observation output (on if the daily or yearly column is y) on gwflow_heat Heat balance files: daily, yearly and average annual columns same intervals as the water balance gwflow_solute Solute balance files, by interval same intervals as the water balance

The daily channel hydrograph separation file gwflow_chan_hydsep_day.txt is written when daily water balance output is on. The files are described in the gwflow output reference.

docs.title: zones.gw
docs.text:
Aquifer and streambed parameters, one row per zone. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a column header. The zone number of a row is its position in the file (the first data row is zone 1); the zone_id column is not read.

# Column Units Description 1 zone_id - Zone number. Not read; the row position decides. 2 aquifer_K m/day Horizontal hydraulic conductivity of the aquifer. 3 aquifer_Sy fraction Specific yield of the aquifer. 4 streambed_K m/day Hydraulic conductivity of the streambed, for channel cells that use this zone. 5 streambed_thick m Streambed thickness, for channel cells that use this zone. 6 thermal_K J/day/m/°C Thermal conductivity of the aquifer, used by heat transport. Optional; null or missing means 0.

Cells name a zone for conductivity and a zone for specific yield in cells.gw. Channel cells name a zone for streambed properties in chancell.gw.

docs.title: cells.gw
docs.text:
One row per cell, in cell order. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a column header. Row \(i\) must have id equal to \(i\), or the run stops with a message in gwflow_record. The first 14 columns are required. Columns 15 to 23 are optional: a row can end after column 14, and null in any of them means the value is not set.

# Column Units Description 1 id - Cell number, 1 to ncell, equal to the row number. 2 name - Cell name, used in output files. 3 gis_id - GIS identifier of the cell, written to output files. 4 status - 0 = inactive, 1 = active, 2 = boundary. Boundary cells keep their head and are treated by bc_type. 5 elev m Ground surface elevation. 6 thck m Aquifer thickness. The aquifer bottom is elev - thck. 7 K_zone - Zone (row of zones.gw) for hydraulic conductivity. Also used for thermal_K. 8 Sy_zone - Zone (row of zones.gw) for specific yield. 9 delay day Recharge delay through the unsaturated zone. 10 exdp m Extinction depth for groundwater ET, measured down from the ground surface. 0 turns groundwater ET off for the cell. 11 init m Initial groundwater head (elevation). A value below the aquifer bottom is raised to the bottom. 12 x m x coordinate of the cell centre. 13 y m y coordinate of the cell centre. 14 area m² Cell area. 15 strK m/day Streambed conductivity for this cell, in place of the zone value. 16 strthick m Streambed thickness for this cell, in place of the zone value. 17 bc_type - Boundary condition for this cell, in place of the default in codes.gw. 18 tile_depth m Tile depth for this cell, in place of the value in tile.gw. 19 tile_area m² Tile drainage area for this cell, in place of the value in tile.gw. 20 tile_K 1/day Tile conductance for this cell, in place of the value in tile.gw. 21 row - Grid row of a structured cell (0 for unstructured). Written to output only. 22 col - Grid column of a structured cell (0 for unstructured). Written to output only. 23 init_temp °C Initial groundwater temperature, used by heat transport.

The x and y coordinates are used to find, for each cell, the nearest channel cell (for saturation excess flow and tile drainage) and, for each boundary cell, the nearest active cell, which receives the recharge that falls on the boundary cell.

docs.title: cellcon.gw
docs.text:
The neighbours of every cell, which define where lateral flow can happen. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a column header. One row per cell, in cell order; the first value must equal the row number.

# Column Description 1 cell_id Cell number, equal to the row number. 2 neighbor_tot Number of neighbours. 3+ neighbor_ids neighbor_tot cell numbers.

Flow between a cell and a neighbour uses Darcy's law with the harmonic mean of the two conductivities. The face width is the square root of the smaller of the two cell areas. No flow passes to an inactive neighbour or to a boundary neighbour with bc_type 2.

docs.title: outputs.gw
docs.text:
Output settings, one per row. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a column header. Each row starts with a category and a value; anything after the value (SWAT+ Editor writes a note) is ignored. Rows can be in any order.

category value Effect observation_cell cell number Adds an observation well. Head, water table depth, temperature, nitrate and phosphorus at each well are written to gwflow_obs_*.txt. One row per well. head_output_time date as YYYYDDD A date for a full head output. In 62.0.1 these dates are read but produce no output. detail_debug_cell cell number or 0 Read but not used.

docs.title: chancell.gw
docs.text:
The cells crossed by channels, one row per channel-cell pair. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a column header. A cell crossed by two channels appears on two rows.

# Column Units Description 1 cell_id - Cell crossed by the channel. 2 elev_m m Channel bed elevation in the cell. 3 channel - Channel number in chandeg.con. 4 riv_length_m m Length of the channel within the cell. 5 zone - Zone (row of zones.gw) for streambed conductivity and thickness. 6 dep_zone - Depth zone: column of chan_depth.gw that gives the daily water depth. Optional, default 0. 7 obs 0/1 1 writes daily channel exchange for this cell to gwflow_chan_obs_flow_day.txt. Optional, default 0.

docs.title: Channel exchange
docs.text:
Exchange is calculated each day for every active channel cell with Darcy's law across the streambed. With bed elevation \(z_b\) (elev_m minus river_thresh), water depth \(d\), stage \(z_s = z_b + d\), groundwater head \(h\), streambed conductivity \(K_b\) and thickness \(m_b\), and flow area \(A = w\,L\) (channel width times riv_length_m):

\[Q = \frac{K_b}{m_b}\,A \times \begin{cases} d & h < z_b \\ z_s - h & z_b < h < z_s \\ -(h - z_s) & h > z_s \end{cases}\]

A positive \(Q\) (m³/day) is seepage from the channel into the aquifer and is limited to the water in the channel. A negative \(Q\) is groundwater discharge to the channel and is limited to the water stored in the cell. The width \(w\) is the channel width from the channel data. The depth \(d\) is the channel depth from the channel data, unless chan_depth.gw is present, in which case it is the day's depth for the cell's depth zone.

docs.title: gwflow.con
docs.text: The connect file for the channel-cell objects. It has the usual connect-file layout (title line, header line, then one row per object); see connect files. Each row is one channel cell, with the cell number in the CELL column and one outflow to the channel (sdc, the channel number, tot, 1.0).

docs.title: hrucell.gw
docs.text:
Overlaps between HRUs and cells, used to pass recharge from HRUs to cells and, with gw_soil, groundwater back into the soil. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a column header.

# Column Units Description 1 hru - HRU number. 2 area_m2 m² Total area of the HRU. 3 cell_id - Cell that overlaps the HRU. 4 overlap_m2 m² Area of the overlap.

Rows must be grouped by HRU and the HRUs must be in increasing order, since SWAT+ reads the rows for HRU 1, then HRU 2, and so on. A row with an HRU number outside 1 to the number of HRUs is skipped. Each HRU's recharge is split between its cells by overlap_m2 / area_m2.

The HRU's recharge delay is taken from the delay of its cells in cells.gw. When an HRU overlaps several cells, the delay of the last cell listed for that HRU is used.

docs.title: lsucell.gw
docs.text:
Overlaps between landscape units and cells, used in place of hrucell.gw with LSU connection. The layout differs from the other tables:

Line Content 1 Title 2 Number of landscape units in the model 3 Number \(n\) of landscape units connected to cells next \(n\) lines One landscape unit number per line next 2 lines Headers, skipped rest One row per overlap: landscape unit number, landscape unit area (m²), cell number, overlap area (m²)

The overlap rows must be grouped by landscape unit in increasing order. With LSU connection every HRU uses a recharge delay based on the mean delay of all cells.

SWAT+ Editor writes lsucell.gw as a title followed by rows of cell, landscape unit and area, which is a different layout from the one the model reads.

docs.title: chan_depth.gw
docs.text: Daily channel water depth for each depth zone. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a column header. Then one row per simulated day, in order: day of year, year, and one depth (m) for each depth zone 1 to \(N\), where \(N\) is the largest dep_zone in chancell.gw. One row is read per day in sequence; the day and year values are not checked.

docs.title: pumpex.gw
docs.text:
Specified pumping from cells, read when pumpex is 1. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a column header. One row per pumping period.

# Column Units Description 1 name - Label, not used. 2 cell_id - Pumped cell. 3 rate m³/day Pumping rate during the period. 4 yr_start year First year of the period. 5 dy_start day of year First day of the period. 6 yr_end year Last year of the period. 7 dy_end day of year Last day of the period.

Consecutive rows with the same cell_id form one pump with several periods (up to 1000). Rows for one cell that are not next to each other create separate pumps. Each date is converted to a day count from the start of the simulation as \((\mathrm{year} - \mathrm{first\ year}) \times 365 + \mathrm{day}\), without leap days. A year before the first simulated year is counted as day 1.

docs.title: hru_pump.gw
docs.text: HRUs whose groundwater irrigation pumping is written each day to gwflow_cell_wb_ppag_obs_day.txt. Line 1 is a title, line 2 is the number of HRUs, and then one HRU number per line.

docs.title: tile.gw
docs.text:
Tile drainage, read when tile is 1. Each value is on a separate line:

Line Content 1 Title 2 Tile depth below the ground surface (m), for all cells 3 Tile drainage area (m²), for all cells 4 Tile conductance (1/day), for all cells 5 Group flag: 1 if tile cell groups follow, 0 if not groups If the flag is 1: the number of groups, then for each group a name line, the number of cells, and one cell number per line next Header line, skipped rest Tile flag per cell (1 = tile drained, 0 = not). Unstructured grid: one value per line for all ncell cells. Structured grid: n_rows lines of n_cols values.

Columns 18 to 20 of cells.gw replace the depth, area and conductance for single cells. Each day, an active tile cell whose head \(h\) is above the tile elevation \(z_t\) (elev - tile_depth) drains

\[Q_{tile} = A_{tile}\,K_{tile}\,(h - z_t)\]

in m³/day to the channel nearest to the cell. With groups, the daily tile flow of each group is written to gwflow_tile_group_day.txt.

The structured-grid form of the tile flags depends on grid arrays that 62.0.1 does not set up, so give the tile flags in the unstructured form. SWAT+ Editor writes the three tile values on one line followed by a list of tile cells, which is a different layout from the one the model reads.

docs.title: rescell.gw
docs.text:
Reservoir-cell links, read when res is 1.

Line Content 1, 2 Title and a second line, skipped 3 Reservoir bed thickness (m), for all reservoirs 4 Reservoir bed conductivity (m/day), for all reservoirs 5 Number of rows that follow 6 Header, skipped rest cell_id, res_id, res_stage

res_id is the reservoir number; a row with 0 is skipped. Exchange uses the ground elevation of the cell from cells.gw as the reservoir bed elevation. res_stage is read but not used.

docs.title: gwflow.wetland
docs.text:
Wetland bed thickness, read when wet is 1 and HRUs are connected to cells. Lines 1 and 2 are skipped. Each later row has a wetland name and a bed thickness (m). The digits in the name give the HRU number, so wet019 sets the bed thickness of the wetland in HRU 19. Wetlands not listed use 0.25 m.

SWAT+ Editor writes this information to a file named wetland.gw, which the model does not read, so wetlands then use 0.25 m.

docs.title: floodplain.gw
docs.text: Floodplain-cell links, read when fp is 1. Line 1 is a title, line 2 the number of rows, line 3 a header, then one row per cell: cell number, channel number, floodplain bed conductivity (m/day) and area of the cell inside the floodplain (m²). The area is limited to the cell area.

docs.title: gwflow_canal.con
docs.text:
Canal-cell links, read when canal is 1. The canal dimensions, bed properties and active days come from the canal records in water_canal.wal. Line 1 is a title. Each later row describes one canal:

canal_id  n  cell_1 length_1 elev_1  cell_2 length_2 elev_2  ...

with n triplets of cell number, canal length in the cell (m) and canal bed elevation in the cell (m). A canal with a diversion source is treated as a diversion canal. A canal with no diversion and a start day above 0 is treated as a canal fed from outside the model. Any other canal is linked to a channel through water allocation.

docs.title: phreato.gw and phreato_cell.gw
docs.text:
Groundwater uptake by phreatophytes. Both files are needed when phreato.gw exists; there is no switch in codes.gw.

phreato.gw is the curve of uptake rate against water table depth. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a header, then one point per row: depth to the water table (m) and ET rate (m/day), in order of increasing depth.

phreato_cell.gw lists the cells with phreatophytes. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a header, then one row per cell: cell number and area covered by phreatophytes (m²).

docs.title: tvheads.gw
docs.text: Line 1 is a title and line 2 a header. Each later row gives a cell number and one head per simulated year. In 62.0.1 the file is read but the heads are not applied, so boundary cells keep their initial heads.

docs.title: solute.gw
docs.text:
Solute transport settings, read when solute is 1.

Line Content 1, 2 Title and a second line, skipped 3 Number of transport time steps per flow time step 4 Longitudinal dispersivity (m) 5 Skipped (SWAT+ Editor writes the number of solutes here) rest One row per solute: name, retardation factor, reaction rate constant (1/day), concentration in canal water from outside the model (g/m³)

The solutes and their order are set by the model: nitrate and phosphorus first, then the salt ions and then the other constituents listed in constituents.cs. The file must have one row per solute in that order; the name column is not checked. Further values on a row are ignored. SWAT+ Editor writes an initial concentration as a fifth value, which the model does not read; initial values come from cell_sol.gw.

The retardation factor divides the transport time step, so 1 means no sorption. The reaction term adds concentration × groundwater volume × rate constant (g/day) to the cell, so a negative rate constant gives first-order decay.

When constituents are simulated, SWAT+ also tries to read per-cell reaction groups and shale maps after cell_sol.gw. In 62.0.1 no file is open at that point, so gwflow solute transport cannot run together with the constituent module.

docs.title: cell_sol.gw
docs.text: Initial solute concentration in every cell. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a header, then one row per cell in cell order: cell number and one concentration (g/m³) per solute, in the order of solute.gw. Without this file all concentrations start at 0.

docs.title: minerals.gw
docs.text: Salt mineral fractions per cell, read when solute transport is on, salt ions are simulated and the file exists. Line 1 is a title, line 2 the number of minerals, line 3 a header, then for an unstructured grid one row per cell with one fraction per mineral. The structured-grid form is read but the values are not stored. SWAT+ Editor does not write this file.

docs.title: ponds.gw, pond_cell.gw and pond_div.gw
docs.text:
Recharge ponds. They are active when ponds.gw exists, and pond_cell.gw must then exist too.

ponds.gw has a title line, a header line and one row per pond:

# Column Units Description 1 pond_id - Pond number, matched in pond_cell.gw. 2 area m² Pond area. 3 chan - Channel that supplies the diverted water. 0 if none. 4 canal - Canal that supplies the diverted water, used when chan is 0. 0 if none. 5 unl 0/1 1 = the diverted water comes from outside the model, used when chan and canal are 0. 6 bed_k m/day Conductivity of the pond bed. 7 wsta - Weather station for rainfall and evaporation. 8 evap_co - Evaporation coefficient. Daily evaporation is evap_co × potential ET of the station × pond area. 9 start_yr year Year the pond starts operating. 10 start_mo month Month the pond starts operating. 11 start_day day Day of the month the pond starts operating. 12+ unl_conc_1 ... g/m³ Concentration of each solute in water from outside the model (none when solute transport is off).

The start date is converted to a day count with 365-day years and fixed month lengths; a start year before the first simulated year means day 1.

pond_cell.gw has a title line, a header line and one row per pond-cell connection: pond number, cell number and connection area (m²). The rows for a pond give its cells.

pond_div.gw has a title line, a header line and one row per simulated day: year, month, day and the volume diverted into each pond that day (m³), in the order of ponds.gw. One row is read per day in sequence, so the file needs a row for every simulated day; the dates are not checked. Without the file, no water is diverted into the ponds.

docs.title: sw_group.gw
docs.text: Groups of channel cells whose daily channel exchange is summed and written to gwflow_gwsw_group_day.txt. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a header. Each later row gives a group number, the number of cells \(n\) in the group and \(n\) cell numbers.

docs.title: transit.gw
docs.text: Cells for groundwater transit-time output. Read only for a structured grid. Line 1 is a title, line 2 a header, line 3 the number of cells, then one cell number per line. SWAT+ Editor does not write this file.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Start of a set of inputs for a structured grid of 1454 cells, with illustrative values.

codes.gw (abbreviated):

codes.gw: written by SWAT+ editor
     grid_type         ncell     cell_size        n_rows        n_cols   ...      time_step     write_aa  river_thresh
    structured          1454       5000.00            52            53   ...           1.00            1          5.00

zones.gw:

zones.gw: written by SWAT+ editor
   zone_id     aquifer_K    aquifer_Sy   streambed_K streambed_thick     thermal_K
         1       0.50000       0.20000       0.00500         0.50000       0.00000
         2       2.00000       0.20000       0.00500         0.50000       0.00000

cells.gw (first row, abbreviated):

 id  name      gis_id  status   elev   thck K_zone Sy_zone  delay  exdp   init ...  row  col init_temp
  1  cell0001       1       2 395.00  34.99      1       1   0.00  1.00 390.00 ...   52    1      null

Cell 1 is a boundary cell. Its aquifer bottom is at 395.00 - 34.99 = 360.01 m and it starts with a head of 390.00 m.

chancell.gw:

chancell.gw: written by SWAT+ editor
 cell_id   elev_m  channel  riv_length_m  zone  dep_zone  obs
      42   326.00       66       1853.55     1         0    1
      43   324.50       66        912.10     1         0    0

Channel 66 crosses cells 42 and 43, both with streambed properties from zone 1. With river_thresh at 5.00, the exchange at cell 42 uses a bed elevation of 321.00 m. Daily exchange at cell 42 is written to the channel observation output.

docs.title: Related files
docs.text:
• codes.bsn: gwflow switches the module on.
  • object.cnt: can give the number of gwflow objects directly.
  • print.prt: gwflow output rows.
  • hru-data.hru and connect files: the HRUs, landscape units, channels and reservoirs that cells connect to.
  • water_canal.wal: canal data used by canal seepage.
  • constituents.cs and salt inputs: the salts and constituents added to the gwflow solutes.
  • gwflow outputs.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
hru-lte.hru describes the HRU-lte objects, a simplified kind of HRU. An HRU-lte has one soil layer described by a texture class, a single plant whose growing season is started and ended by decision tables, a curve number for surface runoff, separate shallow and deep groundwater stores and a fixed USLE factor for erosion. It computes no nutrients, pesticides or bacteria. HRU-lte objects can be used alone or together with ordinary HRUs, and they send water and sediment to channels, routing units and other objects like any other spatial object.

The file is named in the second position of the hru line of file.cio (default hru-lte.hru). The objects themselves are defined in hru-lte.con, the second file on the connect line, and their number is the lhru count in object.cnt. The hlt column of hru-lte.con gives the id of the hru-lte.hru row each object uses. The area, latitude, elevation and weather station of the object come from hru-lte.con; see the connection file format.

hru-lte.hru is read only when the file exists and is not named null. When lhru is above zero, the file must be present: without it the HRU-lte objects have no properties and the run fails. A project with HRU-lte objects also needs soils_lte.sol (texture classes), plants.plt (plant parameters) and lum.dtl (the growing-season decision tables).

docs.title: hru-lte.hru
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one HRU-lte with 35 values in the order below. The reader does not match columns by header name, so all 35 values must be present and in this order. Text values must not contain spaces.

# Column Units Typical range Description 1 id - 1 and up Row number. The hlt column of hru-lte.con refers to the row by this number. Ids must be unique; the rows may be in any order. 2 name - - Name of the HRU-lte, up to 16 characters. Not used in calculations; the names in the output files come from hru-lte.con. 3 area km² (in the source) - Drainage area. Used only to estimate the time of concentration when t_conc is zero, which does not work in 62.0.1 (see Time of concentration). The SWAT+ Editor writes the HRU area in hectares here. 4 cn2 - 35 to 98 SCS curve number for moisture condition II. See Surface runoff. 5 cn3_swf fraction 0 to 0.95 Soil water factor for the curve number: the soil water content at which the retention parameter reaches its condition III value, as a fraction of the way from field capacity (0) to saturation (1). A value of 1 makes the shape coefficients of the retention curve infinite; use a value below 1. The SWAT+ Editor writes 0. 6 t_conc min 10 to 1000 Time of concentration. Sets the peak runoff rate for erosion, and the delivery ratio when the HRU-lte is an element of a routing unit with a calculated delivery ratio. Give a value above zero. The SWAT+ Editor writes 26. 7 soil_dp mm 300 to 3000 Depth of the soil profile. Multiplies the available water capacity and porosity of the soil texture. 8 perc_co fraction 0 to 1 Percolation threshold: percolation from the soil profile starts when soil water exceeds perc_co times the available water capacity. Called perco_co in earlier documentation, which gave a range of 0 to 6000. See Percolation. 9 slp m/m 0 to 0.6 Average land surface slope. Used for lateral flow and the USLE slope factor. 10 slp_len m 10 to 150 Slope length. Used for lateral flow and the USLE slope length factor. 11 et_co - 0.8 to 1.2 Evapotranspiration coefficient. Multiplies potential evapotranspiration, and again actual evapotranspiration. Values below 0.4 make evapotranspiration outside the growing season negative. See Evapotranspiration. 12 aqu_sp_yld - 0.01 to 0.3 Specific yield of the shallow aquifer. Read but not used. 13 alpha_bf 1/day 0 to 1 Baseflow recession constant of the groundwater store. See Groundwater. 14 revap fraction 0 to 0.2 Revap coefficient: water removed from the shallow groundwater store each day as a fraction of the day's actual evapotranspiration. 15 rchg_dp fraction 0 to 1 Fraction of the day's percolation that moves from the shallow store to the deep store. 16 sw_init fraction 0 to 1 Initial soil water as a fraction of the available water capacity. 17 aqu_init mm - Initial shallow aquifer storage. Read but not used: the store starts at zero. 18 aqu_sh_flo mm - Initial groundwater flow. Read but not used: the flow starts at zero. 19 aqu_dp_flo mm - Initial deep aquifer storage. Read but not used: the store starts at zero. 20 snow_h2o mm H₂O - Initial snow water content. Read but not used: the snowpack starts at zero. 21 lat degrees -90 to 90 Latitude. Read, and used only in a day length calculation whose result is not used, so it has no effect. 22 soil_text - - Soil texture class, matched against the texture column of soils_lte.sol. See Name matching. 23 trop_flag - non_trop, trop Tropical flag. Read but not used. 24 grow_start - - Name of the lum.dtl decision table that starts the growing season, usually pl_grow_sum (or pl_grow_win for winter crops). 25 grow_end - - Name of the lum.dtl decision table that ends the growing season and computes the yield, usually pl_end_sum (or pl_end_win). 26 plnt_typ - - Plant name, matched against the name column of plants.plt. 27 stress fraction 0 to 1 Plant stress factor for stresses the HRU-lte does not simulate (pests, root restriction, soil quality, nutrients). It multiplies daily biomass growth; 1 means no such stress. With 0 no biomass grows and the yield is zero. The SWAT+ Editor writes 0. 28 pet_flag - harg, p_t Potential evapotranspiration method: harg for Hargreaves; any other value selects Priestley-Taylor. 29 irr_flag - - Irrigation switch. See Irrigation for the values that switch irrigation on in 62.0.1. 30 irr_src - outside_bsn, shal_aqu, deep_aqu Source of irrigation water: the HRU-lte's shallow or deep groundwater store, or an unlimited source outside the basin (any value other than shal_aqu and deep_aqu). 31 t_drain hr 0, or 24 to 72 Time to drain the soil to field capacity through tile drains. 0 means no tile drains. 32 usle_k 0.013 t m² h/(m³ t cm) 0 to 0.65 USLE soil erodibility factor K. 33 usle_c - 0.001 to 0.5 USLE cover and management factor C. It is constant through the year. The SWAT+ Editor writes the usle_c_min of the plant. 34 usle_p - 0 to 1 USLE support practice factor P. 35 usle_ls - - USLE slope length and steepness factor LS. Read but not used: SWAT+ computes LS from slp and slp_len.

docs.title: Name matching
docs.text:
The text columns are compared character by character with the names in the other files. The comparison is case-sensitive and trailing blanks are ignored.

  • soil_text is looked up among the twelve texture classes of soils_lte.sol (see the soils_lte.sol format). The matching class gives the available water capacity and porosity per mm of soil depth and the saturated hydraulic conductivity. If no class matches, the HRU-lte has no soil water capacity, and the run fails or produces invalid numbers when it divides by it. The SWAT+ Editor datasets contain the classes sand, loamy_sand, sandy_loam, loam, silt_loam, silt, silty_clay_loam, clay_loam, sandy_clay_loam, sandy_clay, silty_clay and clay, and the Editor picks one for each HRU-lte from the sand, silt and clay content of the first soil layer.
  • plnt_typ is looked up in the name column of plants.plt. An unknown name writes <name> not found (plants.plt) to diagnostics.out, and the HRU-lte grows with the built-in default plant record, whose leaf area curve is not set up.
  • grow_start and grow_end are looked up by table name in lum.dtl. An unknown name writes <name> entry in (hru-lte.hru) not found in (lum.dtl) to diagnostics.out; the run then refers to a decision table that does not exist, so both names must be present in lum.dtl.
  • pet_flag is compared with harg only.
  • irr_flag and irr_src are compared as described under Irrigation.

docs.title: Daily water balance
docs.text:
Each HRU-lte runs once a day, in the order of the object list. The steps below follow that order. \(SW\) is the soil water content (mm), \(AWC\) and \(POR\) are the available water capacity and the porosity of the profile (mm), and \(K_{sat}\) is the saturated hydraulic conductivity of the texture class (mm/h):

\[AWC = awc \cdot \mathrm{soil\_dp}, \qquad POR = por \cdot \mathrm{soil\_dp}, \qquad SW_0 = \mathrm{sw\_init} \cdot AWC\]

where \(awc\) and \(por\) are the per-mm values of the texture class in soils_lte.sol.

docs.title: Snow
docs.text:
When the mean air temperature \(\bar{T}\) is below 0 °C, the whole day's precipitation is added to the snowpack and there is no runoff or infiltration that day. Otherwise snowmelt is

\[SNO_{mlt} = 4.57\,\bar{T}\]

limited to the snowpack, and rain and melt together form the water input \(P\) for the day. The snow.sno parameters are not used by HRU-lte objects.

docs.title: Surface runoff
docs.text:
Surface runoff uses the SCS curve number method with a retention parameter that varies with soil water (see SCS curve number). At the start of the run the condition I and III curve numbers are derived from cn2:

\[CN_1 = CN_2 - \frac{20\,(100 - CN_2)}{100 - CN_2 + \exp\left(2.533 - 0.063\,(100 - CN_2)\right)}, \qquad CN_1 \ge 0.4\,CN_2\] \[CN_3 = CN_2 \exp\left(0.00673\,(100 - CN_2)\right)\] \[S_{max} = 254\left(\frac{100}{CN_1} - 1\right), \qquad S_3 = 254\left(\frac{100}{CN_3} - 1\right)\]

Each day the retention parameter is

\[S = S_{max}\left(1 - \frac{SW}{SW + \exp(w_1 - w_2\,SW)}\right), \qquad S \ge 3\]

The shape coefficients \(w_1\) and \(w_2\) are fixed at the start so that \(S = S_3\) when \(SW = AWC + \mathrm{cn3\_swf}\,(POR - AWC)\), and \(S = 2.54\) when \(SW = POR\). Runoff is

\[Q_{surf} = \frac{(P - 0.2\,S)^2}{P + 0.8\,S} \quad \text{for } P > 0.2\,S\]

and zero otherwise. The rest of \(P\) is added to the soil water. SWAT+ also stores cn2 limited to 35 to 98, but the runoff curve is built from the value as given in the file, so values outside that range are used as they are.

docs.title: Evapotranspiration
docs.text:
Potential evapotranspiration is computed with the method chosen in pet_flag and multiplied by et_co. With Hargreaves,

\[PET = \mathrm{et\_co} \cdot 0.0032\,\frac{H_0}{2.5 - 0.0022\,\bar{T}}\,(\bar{T} + 17.8)\,(T_{max} - T_{min})^{0.6}\]

where \(H_0\) is the day's maximum possible solar radiation (MJ/m²). With Priestley-Taylor,

\[PET = \mathrm{et\_co} \cdot 1.28\,\frac{\Delta}{\Delta + 0.68}\cdot\frac{23.9\,H\,(1 - 0.23)}{58.3}, \qquad \Delta = \frac{5304}{T_K^2}\exp\left(21.255 - \frac{5304}{T_K}\right)\]

where \(H\) is the day's solar radiation (MJ/m²) and \(T_K\) the mean air temperature in kelvin. Both are simpler forms than those used for ordinary HRUs (see Potential evapotranspiration).

Actual evapotranspiration is proportional to the soil water content:

\[E_a = b \cdot PET\,\frac{SW}{AWC}, \qquad b = \begin{cases}\mathrm{et\_co} & \text{during the growing season}\\ \mathrm{et\_co} - 0.4 & \text{outside it}\end{cases}\]

It is taken from the soil after lateral flow, tile flow and percolation, and is limited to the soil water left at that point. Because et_co enters both \(PET\) and \(b\), a change in et_co changes actual evapotranspiration roughly with its square during the growing season.

docs.title: Lateral flow
docs.text:
When soil water is above the available water capacity,

\[Q_{lat} = 0.024\,\frac{SW - AWC}{POR - AWC}\,K_{sat}\,\frac{\mathrm{slp}}{\mathrm{slp\_len}}\]

limited to the soil water.

docs.title: Tile flow
docs.text:
When t_drain is above zero and soil water is above the available water capacity,

\[Q_{tile} = (SW - AWC)\left(1 - \exp\left(\frac{-24}{\mathrm{t\_drain}}\right)\right), \qquad Q_{tile} \le 10\ \text{mm}\]

docs.title: Percolation
docs.text:
Water above perc_co times the available water capacity drains from the bottom of the profile:

\[w_{perc} = (SW - \mathrm{perc\_co}\cdot AWC)\left(1 - \exp\left(\frac{-24}{TT}\right)\right), \qquad TT = \max\left(2,\ \frac{POR - AWC}{K_{sat}}\right)\]

where \(TT\) is the travel time in hours. With perc_co at 1 only water above field capacity percolates; with perc_co at 0 (the value the SWAT+ Editor writes) the profile can drain well below field capacity.

docs.title: Groundwater
docs.text:
The shallow and deep groundwater stores of an HRU-lte are separate from the aquifer objects. Percolation is added to the shallow store. Groundwater flow follows a recession with \(\alpha\) = alpha_bf:

\[Q_{gw,d} = Q_{gw,d-1}\,e^{-\alpha} + w_{perc}\left(1 - e^{-\alpha}\right)\]

limited to the shallow storage. Then revap (\(\mathrm{revap} \cdot E_a\)) and deep percolation (\(\mathrm{rchg\_dp} \cdot w_{perc}\)) are taken from what is left in the shallow store, each limited to the storage. Deep percolation is added to the deep store, which only irrigation from deep_aqu draws on. Revap leaves the HRU-lte; it is not added to the soil or to the reported evapotranspiration. Both stores and the groundwater flow start at zero.

docs.title: Water yield
docs.text:
The water the HRU-lte sends downstream each day is

\[WYLD = Q_{surf} + Q_{lat} + Q_{tile} + Q_{gw}\]

In the hru-lte_wb output files, latq is the sum of lateral flow and groundwater flow.

docs.title: Plant growth
docs.text: The plant named in plnt_typ grows between the two decision tables. On each day outside the growing season the grow_start table is checked; when its grow_init action runs, growth starts with zero biomass and leaf area. During the season the grow_end table is checked; its grow_end action computes the yield and ends the season. The pl_grow_sum and pl_end_sum tables of the SWAT+ reference data start growth when the fraction of the year's base-zero heat units at the weather station is between 0.15 and 0.2, and end it when the fraction is above 0.5 or on day 330. See decision table actions.

docs.title: Heat units to maturity
docs.text:
At the start of the run SWAT+ estimates the heat units to maturity, \(PHU\), from the long-term monthly mean temperatures in the weather generator of the HRU-lte's station. Daily values of \(\bar{T} - T_{base}\) above zero are summed over the days between a start and an end day, and

\[PHU = \max(500,\ 0.9\,\textstyle\sum(\bar{T} - T_{base}))\]

limited to 2000 for annual plant types (warm_annual, cold_annual and their tuber forms). In 62.0.1 the start and end days of the sum are the positions of the grow_start and grow_end tables in lum.dtl (first table 1, second table 2, and so on). The days of the year of the growing season are not used. For two tables next to each other in lum.dtl the sum covers no days and \(PHU\) takes its minimum of 500.

docs.title: Biomass and leaf area
docs.text:
During the growing season the fraction of heat units \(g\) increases each day by \((\bar{T} - T_{base})/PHU\). Biomass grows with intercepted radiation:

\[\Delta B = \gamma \cdot \mathrm{stress} \cdot bm_e \cdot 0.5\,H\left(1 - e^{-0.65\,(LAI + 0.05)}\right), \qquad \gamma = \min(ws,\ ts,\ as)\]

where \(bm_e\) is bm_e of plants.plt, \(ws = E_a/PET\) is the water stress factor (before the adjustment \(b\)), \(ts\) the temperature stress factor and \(as\) the aeration stress factor:

\[ts = \exp\left(-0.1054\left(\frac{T_{opt} - \bar{T}}{2T_{opt} - T_{base} - \bar{T}}\right)^2\right) \text{ for } \bar{T} > T_{base}, \qquad ts = 0 \text{ otherwise}\]

Aeration stress starts when \(SW\) exceeds \(AWC\) by more than 85% of the drainable range \(POR - AWC\). Leaf area follows the leaf area curve of the plant (frac_hu1, lai_max1, frac_hu2, lai_max2 and lai_pot in plants.plt), with the daily increase scaled by \(\sqrt{\gamma}\). See plant growth for the background of these relations.

docs.title: Yield
docs.text:
When the season ends, the yield is

\[Y = 0.8\,B\,HI', \qquad HI' = (HI - HI_{min})\frac{wur}{wur + \exp(6.13 - 0.0883\,wur)} + HI_{min}\]

where \(HI\) is harv_idx, \(HI_{min}\) is harv_idx_ws of plants.plt, and \(wur\) is 100 times the ratio of actual to potential evapotranspiration summed over the season (100 when the potential sum is below 10 mm). Biomass and leaf area are then set to zero.

Plant growth has no effect on the water balance or on erosion: evapotranspiration does not depend on leaf area, and usle_c is constant. The plant affects the water balance only through the growing season itself (the factor \(b\)) and through irrigation.

docs.title: Irrigation
docs.text:
During the growing season, on days when the water stress factor \(ws\) is below 0.8, the soil is filled to the available water capacity with at most 76.2 mm. With irr_src set to shal_aqu or deep_aqu the water is taken from the HRU-lte's shallow or deep store and limited to what it contains; any other value takes it from an unlimited source outside the basin.

In 62.0.1 irrigation is switched on when irr_flag sorts alphabetically after no_irr. The value irr, listed as the "irrigation" value in earlier documentation, sorts before no_irr and so leaves irrigation off. Values such as yes or sprinkler switch it on.

docs.title: Erosion
docs.text:
Sediment yield is computed with MUSLE (see MUSLE). The slope length and steepness factor is computed at the start of the run from slp and slp_len; the usle_ls column is not used:

\[LS = \left(\frac{\mathrm{slp\_len}}{22.128}\right)^m\left(65.41\,\sin^2\theta + 4.56\,\sin\theta + 0.065\right), \qquad m = 0.6\left(1 - e^{-35.835\,\mathrm{slp}}\right)\]

with \(\theta = \arctan(\mathrm{slp})\). Sediment from surface runoff is

\[sed = 11.8\,(Q_{surf}\; q_{peak} \cdot 1000\,A)^{0.56}\; K\,C\,P\,LS\]

with \(K\), \(C\) and \(P\) from usle_k, usle_c and usle_p, and \(A\) the area of hru-lte.con. A concentration of 500 mg/L in lateral and groundwater flow is added to this. There is no snow cover or residue effect.

docs.title: Time of concentration
docs.text:
The peak runoff rate uses the time of concentration \(t_c\) in seconds (t_conc times 60):

\[q_{peak} = \frac{2\,Q_{surf} \cdot 1000\,A}{1.5\,t_c} + \frac{(Q_{lat} + Q_{gw}) \cdot 1000\,A}{86400}\]

When t_conc is zero, SWAT+ tries to estimate it with the Kirpich formula, using area as the channel length. The slope in that formula is always zero in 62.0.1, so the estimate is infinite: depending on how the model was compiled the run either stops with a floating-point error or continues with no surface runoff in the peak rate. Give t_conc a value above zero.

docs.title: Area units
docs.text: The HRU-lte calculations convert a depth \(D\) in mm to a volume with \(1000\,D\,A\) and report sediment yield per \(100\,A\), which are the conversions for an area \(A\) in km². \(A\) is the area column of hru-lte.con, which is in hectares for every other object type and which the SWAT+ Editor writes in hectares. With hectares, the flow volumes and sediment loads an HRU-lte sends downstream are 100 times the depth over its area, and the peak rate and sediment yield in the output are affected in the same way. Only the total hydrograph is filled: an HRU-lte connection in hru-lte.con that asks for the surface, lateral, tile or recharge hydrograph sends nothing.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
Parameters with the suffix _lte in calibration.cal change hru-lte.hru values (see simplified HRU parameters). The changes are applied after the file has been read and the HRU-lte objects have been set up, so in 62.0.1 they have an effect only for values the daily calculation reads directly from the file:

  • effective: awc_lte (available water capacity of the object), slope_lte and slopelen_lte (lateral flow only), revapc_lte, percc_lte, abf_lte and tc_lte
  • no effect: cn2_lte, etco_lte, soildep_lte, sw_lte, sy_lte, gw_lte, gwflow_lte, gwdeep_lte, snow_lte, uslek_lte, uslec_lte, uslep_lte and uslels_lte

abf_lte changes the daily recession factor \(e^{-\alpha}\) in place of alpha_bf, and tc_lte changes the time of concentration in seconds. Except for awc_lte, a change to object number \(n\) is applied to the hru-lte.hru row with id \(n\); the two agree when row numbers follow the objects, as the SWAT+ Editor writes them.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
No hru-lte.hru is included in the SWAT+ reference data. The file below is illustrative, with the column headers the SWAT+ Editor writes.

hru-lte.hru: illustrative example
id  name    area   cn2  cn3_swf  t_conc  soil_dp  perc_co   slp  slp_len  et_co  aqu_sp_yld  alpha_bf  revap  rchg_dp  sw_init  aqu_init  aqu_sh_flo  aqu_dp_flo  snow_h2o    lat  soil_text  trop_flag  grow_start   grow_end    plnt_typ  stress  pet_flag  irr_flag  irr_src      t_drain  usle_k  usle_c  usle_p  usle_ls
1   hlt001  52.3  77.0     0.00    26.0   1500.0     1.00  0.04     60.0   1.00        0.05      0.05   0.00     0.01     0.50      3.00        0.00      300.00      0.00  41.50  loam       non_trop   pl_grow_sum  pl_end_sum  corn        1.00  harg      no_irr    outside_bsn     0.00    0.28    0.20    1.00     0.53

One HRU-lte with a 1.5 m loam profile that starts half full. Percolation starts above field capacity (perc_co 1). Corn grows between the pl_grow_sum and pl_end_sum tables with no extra stress (stress 1), there is no irrigation and no tile drainage, and potential evapotranspiration follows Hargreaves. The values of area, aqu_sp_yld, aqu_init, aqu_sh_flo, aqu_dp_flo, snow_h2o, lat, trop_flag and usle_ls have no effect in 62.0.1.

docs.title: Related files
docs.text:
• Connection files: hru-lte.con defines the HRU-lte objects, their area, weather station and outflow connections; its hlt column selects a row of this file by id.
  • Object counts: the lhru column of object.cnt gives the number of HRU-lte objects.
  • Master file: file.cio names this file on its hru line, and soils_lte.sol on its soils line.
  • Soil texture classes: soils_lte.sol supplies available water capacity, porosity and conductivity for soil_text.
  • Plant parameters: plants.plt supplies the plant parameters for plnt_typ.
  • Decision tables: the grow_start and grow_end tables in lum.dtl.
  • Weather files: the weather station named in hru-lte.con supplies daily weather and, through its weather generator, the temperatures for the heat units to maturity.
  • Water balance output: hru-lte_wb files; plant growth and stress go to the hru-lte_pw files.
Sources
  • Reader: hru_lte_read.f90, called from main.f90.in after dtbl_lum_read
  • Type definitions: type swatdeg_hru_data and type swatdeg_hru_dynamic in hru_lte_module.f90
  • Daily water balance, plant growth, irrigation and erosion: hru_lte_control.f90, called from command.f90
  • Retention curve shape: ascrv.f90
  • Growing season actions grow_init and grow_end: actions.f90; conditions with obj hlt: conditions.f90
  • Texture classes: soil_lte_db_read.f90, type soil_lte_database in soil_data_module.f90
  • Plant parameters: plant_data_module.f90, plant_parm_read.f90
  • Connection and object numbering: hyd_connect.f90, hyd_read_connect.f90
  • Delivery ratio from t_conc: dr_ru.f90
  • Calibration: cal_parm_select.f90, cal_parmchg_read.f90, proc_cal.f90

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
hru-data.hru lists the HRU property sets of the project. Each row names one record in each of the parameter files an HRU needs: topography, hydrology, soil, land use and management, soil and plant initialization, surface storage (wetland), snow and field. An HRU picks its row through the hru column of hru.con, which gives the id of a row in this file. The file is named on the hru line of file.cio (default hru-data.hru).

The parameter values themselves are in the files the names point to. This file only links them together, so several HRUs can share one hydrology or topography record while having different soils or land uses.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one property set with ten values in the order below. The reader does not match columns by header name, so all ten values must be present and in this order.

# Column Looked up in Description 1 id - Number of the property set. The hru column of hru.con refers to this value. The numbers do not have to be consecutive; the largest id sets the size of the table. 2 name - Name of the property set, up to 40 characters. Not used in calculations. 3 topo topography.hyd Topography record: slope, slope lengths and deposition coefficient. 4 hydro hydrology.hyd Hydrology record: lateral flow, canopy storage, evaporation and percolation parameters. 5 soil soils.sol Soil profile. 6 lu_mgt landuse.lum Land use and management record, which sets the plant community, management schedule, curve numbers, conservation practices and structures such as tile drains. 7 soil_plant_init soil_plant.ini (see initial conditions) Initial soil water, soil nutrients and constituents. The names of the soil test, pesticide, pathogen, heavy metal, salt and constituent records given in that row are matched at the same time. 8 surf_stor wetland.wet Surface storage (wetland or paddy) record, or null for an HRU without surface storage. 9 snow snow.sno Snow parameter set. 10 field field.fld Field dimensions, or null to use the built-in values.

A name must match the record name in the target file character for character, including case. Names in topography.hyd, hydrology.hyd and field.fld are stored with at most 16 characters and soil names with at most 20, so a longer name in this file can never match a record there.

docs.title: Name lookup
docs.text:
Each name is looked up once, when the files are read. The table gives what happens when a name is not found:

Column null or a name that is not found topo, hydro, soil, lu_mgt, soil_plant_init, snow The HRU uses the first record of the target file. No message is written. surf_stor null means no surface storage. Any other name that is not in wetland.wet is reported in diagnostics.out as <name> not found (wetland.wet) and the HRU has no surface storage. field The HRU uses the built-in field values (length 500 m, width 100 m, angle 30°). A name other than null that is not found is reported in diagnostics.out as <name> not found (field.fld).

The reader has checks that would write not found messages for topo, hydro, soil, lu_mgt, soil_plant_init and snow, but they test for a pointer of zero while the pointers start at one, so in 62.0.1 these messages are never written. Check these names by hand, or in the SWAT+ Editor, before a run.

For snow this means that null selects the first row of snow.sno, the same as an unmatched name. A project that has no snow.sno file at all has no first row to fall back on.

The surf_stor name is matched when the wetlands are initialized, which happens only when wetland.wet has at least one record.

docs.title: Tile drainage
docs.text: The lu_mgt record decides whether an HRU has tile drains. For a tile-drained HRU, SWAT+ replaces two values from its hydro record at the start of the run: cn3_swf is set to 0.95 and perco to 0.1. Calibration changes to cn3_swf and perco are also skipped for these HRUs. See hydrology.hyd.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
refdata/Ames_sub1/hru-data.hru in the SWAT+ repository (first four rows):

hru-data.hru: 
      id  name                          topo             hydro              soil            lu_mgt   soil_plant_init         surf_stor              snow             field  
       1  hru0001                topohru0001           hyd0001           soil_01-h1       cosy_lum        soilplant1              null           snow001              null  
       2  hru0002                topohru0002           hyd0002           soil_02          mntill_corn_lum soilplant1              null           snow001              null  
       3  hru0003                topohru0003           hyd0003           soil_03-h3       cosy_lum        soilplant1              null           snow001              null  
       4  hru0004                topohru0004           hyd0004           soil_04          cosy_lum        soilplant1              null           snow001              null

Each HRU has a separate topography record, hydrology record and soil. HRU 2 uses the land use mntill_corn_lum, the others cosy_lum. No HRU has surface storage, all use the snow set snow001, and field is null, so every HRU uses the built-in field dimensions.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This page covers three HRU parameter files and one channel file:

  • hydrology.hyd: lateral flow, canopy storage, evaporation, percolation and enrichment parameters.
  • topography.hyd: slope, slope lengths and the deposition coefficient. Also used by routing units.
  • field.fld: field length and width for routing water and sediment across the landscape. Also used by routing units.
  • shade_factor.shf: daily shade factors for the channel water temperature routine.

An HRU picks one record from each of the first three files by name, in the hydro, topo and field columns of hru-data.hru. hydrology.hyd, topography.hyd and field.fld are named on the hydrology line of file.cio. shade_factor.shf is not listed in file.cio; SWAT+ looks for a file with that name in the project folder.

All four files are free format and whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one record. The readers do not match columns by header name, so every value must be present and in the order given. Record names are stored with at most 16 characters.

An unmatched or misspelt hydro or topo name in hru-data.hru makes the HRU use the first record of the file without a message (see name lookup). hydrology.hyd and topography.hyd must therefore exist and must contain every name used.

docs.title: hydrology.hyd
docs.text:
# Column Units Typical range Description 1 name - - Name of the hydrology record, matched against the hydro column of hru-data.hru. 2 lat_ttime days 0 to 180 Lateral flow travel time, called lat_time in earlier documentation. 0 lets SWAT+ compute it from the soil. See Lateral flow. 3 lat_sed mg/L 0 to 5000 Sediment concentration in lateral and tile flow. 4 can_max mm H₂O 0 to 100 Maximum canopy storage when the canopy is fully developed. 5 esco - 0.01 to 1 Soil evaporation compensation factor. See Soil evaporation. 6 epco - 0.01 to 1 Plant uptake compensation factor. 7 orgn_enrich - 0 to 5 Organic N enrichment ratio for loading with sediment. 0 lets SWAT+ compute it for each runoff event. 8 orgp_enrich - 0 to 5 Organic and sediment-attached P enrichment ratio for loading with sediment. 0 lets SWAT+ compute it for each runoff event. 9 cn3_swf - 0 to 1 Soil water factor for the moisture condition III curve number: 0 puts it at field capacity, 1 at saturation. 10 bio_mix - 0 to 1 Biological mixing efficiency. 11 perco - 0 to 1 Percolation coefficient for the bottom soil layer. See Percolation from the soil profile. 12 lat_orgn mg/L 0 to 200 Organic N concentration in lateral flow. 13 lat_orgp mg/L 0 to 200 Organic P concentration in lateral flow. 14 pet_co - 0.8 to 1.2 Multiplier on potential evapotranspiration. Older files call this column harg_pet. See Potential evapotranspiration. 15 latq_co - 0 to 1 Lateral flow coefficient. See Lateral flow.

For an HRU with tile drains (set in its landuse.lum record), SWAT+ replaces cn3_swf with 0.95 and perco with 0.1 at the start of the run, whatever the record gives, and calibration changes to these two parameters are skipped for that HRU.

docs.title: Lateral flow
docs.text:
Lateral flow is computed for each soil layer below the first with a hillslope storage method:

\[q_{lat,ly} = 0.024\;\mathrm{latq\_co}\;\frac{2\,SW_{ex,ly}}{\phi_{d,ly}/h_{ly}}\;K_{sat,ly}\;\frac{slp}{L_{lat}}\]

where \(SW_{ex,ly}\) is the water above field capacity in the layer (mm), \(\phi_{d,ly}\) the drainable porosity (saturation minus field capacity, mm), \(h_{ly}\) the layer thickness (mm), \(K_{sat,ly}\) the saturated hydraulic conductivity (mm/h), \(slp\) the slp value from topography.hyd and \(L_{lat}\) its lat_len (m). The result is limited to the water above field capacity. The top layer produces no lateral flow. latq_co scales lateral flow linearly; 0 turns it off.

Lateral flow does not leave the HRU on the day it is generated. A fraction of the stored lateral flow is released each day:

\[f_{lat} = 1 - \exp\!\left(-\frac{1}{TT_{lat}}\right)\]

where \(TT_{lat}\) is lat_ttime in days. When lat_ttime is 0, SWAT+ computes it from the soil and the lateral slope length:

\[TT_{lat} = \max\!\left(1,\; 10.4\,\frac{L_{lat}}{K_{sat,mx}}\right)\]

with \(K_{sat,mx}\) the highest saturated hydraulic conductivity in the profile (mm/h). Set lat_ttime to a specific value only when the base flow behaviour of the watershed is well known.

docs.title: Soil evaporation
docs.text:
The evaporative demand on the soil is distributed with depth. The cumulative demand down to depth \(z\) (mm) is

\[E_z = E_s\,\frac{z}{z + \exp(2.374 - 0.00713\,z)}\]

where \(E_s\) is the soil evaporation demand for the day. A layer whose top is at depth \(z_u\) and bottom at \(z_l\) is asked for

\[E_{ly} = E_{z_l} - (1 - \mathrm{esco})\,E_{z_u}\]

so with esco = 0 each layer meets only its share of the depth distribution, and as esco increases more of the demand can be met from lower layers. Layers below the soil evaporation depth do not take part. The demand on a layer is further reduced when the layer is drier than field capacity.

docs.title: Plant uptake compensation
docs.text: epco is copied to every plant of the HRU's plant community when the plants are initialized. As epco approaches 1, more of the water uptake demand can be met by lower layers when upper layers are dry; as it approaches 0, uptake stays closer to the original depth distribution.

docs.title: Enrichment ratios
docs.text: When orgn_enrich or orgp_enrich is above 0.001, it is used as a fixed enrichment ratio for organic N, or for organic and sediment-attached P, for every runoff event. Otherwise SWAT+ computes the enrichment ratio for each event from the sediment concentration in surface runoff. The enrichment ratio is the ratio of the concentration of the constituent in the transported sediment to its concentration in the soil surface layer; it is above 1 because the sediment in runoff contains a larger share of the fine particles that the nutrients are attached to.

docs.title: Curve number soil water factor
docs.text:
cn3_swf sets the soil water content at which the curve number for moisture condition III applies:

\[SW_{CN3} = FC + \mathrm{cn3\_swf}\,(SAT - FC)\]

where \(FC\) and \(SAT\) are the profile water contents at field capacity and saturation. Larger values delay the onset of surface runoff after dry periods. See hydrology in the model theory.

docs.title: Biological mixing
docs.text: Biological mixing redistributes residue and nutrients in the soil through the activity of earthworms and other soil biota, using the same method as a tillage operation with bio_mix as the mixing efficiency. With carbon = 0 in codes.bsn, it is applied once at the end of every calendar year, down to 50 mm or the bottom of the profile if that is shallower. With the other carbon codes this column is not used; carbon = 2 applies a daily biological mixing with an efficiency taken from the tillage data.

docs.title: Percolation from the soil profile
docs.text:
perco limits percolation out of the bottom soil layer, for example to represent an impermeable layer or a high water table. Percolation between the upper layers is not affected. The potential percolation from the bottom layer is multiplied by

\[f_{perc} = \min\!\left[1,\; \exp\!\left(-\left(1.0052\,\ln\!\left(-\ln \mathrm{perco}\right) + 5.6862\right)\right)\right]\]

The relation is strongly non-linear:

perco 0 0.1 0.5 0.8 0.9 0.95 0.99 0.999 and above fraction of potential percolation 0 0.002 0.005 0.015 0.033 0.067 0.35 1

So 0 stops percolation from the profile, values up to about 0.9 allow only a few percent of it, and the restriction is lifted only as perco approaches 1.

docs.title: Potential evapotranspiration
docs.text: pet_co multiplies the potential evapotranspiration of the HRU, whichever method is selected in codes.bsn (Priestley-Taylor, Penman-Monteith, Hargreaves or values read from file). A value of 0 is treated as 1. Values below 0.01 are taken as the old Hargreaves coefficient written to harg_pet by earlier editors and divided by 0.0023, so 0.0023 becomes 1.0.

docs.title: Canopy storage
docs.text:
The canopy storage available on a day is

\[CAN_{day} = \mathrm{can\_max}\;\frac{LAI}{LAI_{mx}}\]

where \(LAI\) is the current leaf area index of the plant community and \(LAI_{mx}\) its maximum. Precipitation fills the canopy before it reaches the ground.

docs.title: Sediment and organic nutrients in lateral flow
docs.text: lat_sed adds sediment to the HRU sediment yield in proportion to lateral and tile flow, and lat_orgn and lat_orgp add organic N and P in proportion to lateral flow. In 62.0.1 the sediment from lat_sed is added twice: once as a mass computed from the HRU area and once again as a value that does not use the area. Sediment yields from HRUs with a non-zero lat_sed therefore include an extra term. The conversion used for lat_orgn and lat_orgp is 100 times smaller than mg/L of lateral flow would give, so the loads are 1% of what the stated units suggest.

docs.title: topography.hyd
docs.text:
# Column Units Built-in value Description 1 name - default Name of the topography record, matched against the topo column of hru-data.hru and of rout_unit.rtu. 2 slp m/m 0.02 Average slope steepness, usually computed from the DEM. Used for lateral flow, the USLE slope-length factor, time of concentration and sediment transport across the HRU. 3 slp_len m 50 Average slope length for erosion: the distance over which sheet flow is the main surface runoff process, measured to the point where flow begins to concentrate. Used in the USLE slope-length factor. The full value is used: 62.0.1 does not apply the maximum slope length of the HRU's conservation practice. 4 lat_len m 50 Slope length for lateral subsurface flow, usually longer than slp_len. A value of 0 is replaced by 50 m. 5 dist_cha m 100 Average distance to the stream. Not used. 6 depos - 1 Deposition coefficient for sediment transport capacity when surface runoff from another object is routed across the HRU. A larger value gives a higher transport capacity, so more sediment leaves the HRU.

The built-in values apply only to a record that is never read; an HRU always uses a record from the file.

When runoff from upslope objects is routed across an HRU, its sediment transport capacity is proportional to

\[\mathrm{depos}\; C\; slp^{1.4}\; w^{1.4}\]

and to the overland flow, where \(C\) is the USLE cover factor of the HRU and \(w\) the field width wd from field.fld.

docs.title: field.fld
docs.text:
# Column Units Built-in value Description 1 name - default Name of the field record, matched against the field column of hru-data.hru and of rout_unit.rtu. 2 len m 500 Field length. Used for the time of concentration of routing units; not used for HRUs. 3 wd m 100 Field width. Used in the sediment transport capacity when surface runoff is routed across an HRU. 4 ang degrees 30 Field angle. Not used.

An HRU whose field entry is null, or a name that is not found, uses the built-in values.

docs.title: shade_factor.shf
docs.text:
# Column Units Description 1 jday day of year Day the value applies to (1 to 365). 2 cha - Channel number (row in chandeg.con). In revisions before 62.0.1 this column was a landscape unit number. 3 value fraction Shade factor, the fraction of incoming solar radiation blocked before it reaches the water surface.

The file has no name column and is read as a list of (day, channel, value) rows. The channel water temperature routine reduces short-wave radiation at the water surface by the factor \((1 - \text{value})\). On day 366 of leap years the factor is 0.5.

The file is meant to be used when sf_on = 1 in temperature.cha. In 62.0.1 the temperature routine takes all its settings from the built-in record instead of from the rows of temperature.cha. The built-in record has sf_on = 0 and ssff = 0.5, so the shade factor is 0.5 for every channel and day, and shade_factor.shf is read but not used. No example dataset in refdata/ has a shade_factor.shf file.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
These parameters can be changed during calibration through calibration.cal (see parameter change files), using these names: lat_ttime, lat_sed, canmx (can_max), esco, epco, erorgn (orgn_enrich), erorgp (orgp_enrich), cn3_swf, biomix (bio_mix), perco, lat_orgn, lat_orgp, petco (pet_co), latq_co, slope (slp), slope_len (slp_len), lat_len, dis_stream (dist_cha), field_len (len), field_wid (wd) and field_ang (ang).

A change to lat_ttime is applied to the daily release fraction \(f_{lat}\), which SWAT+ has already computed from the input, and the result is then converted again as if it were a travel time in days. The effect of a lat_ttime change is therefore not the effect of changing the travel time in the file by the same amount. Changes to dis_stream and field_ang have no effect, because the values are not used.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
refdata/Ames_sub1/hydrology.hyd in the SWAT+ repository (first two rows):

hydrology.hyd:
name                 lat_ttime       lat_sed       can_max          esco          epco   orgn_enrich   orgp_enrich       cn3_swf       bio_mix         perco      lat_orgn      lat_orgp        pet_co       latq_co  
hyd0001                0.00000       0.00000       0.00000       0.95000       1.00000       0.00000       0.00000       0.00000       0.20000       0.50000       0.00000       0.00000       1.00000       0.01000  
hyd0002                0.00000       0.00000       0.00000       0.95000       1.00000       0.00000       0.00000       0.00000       0.20000       0.50000       0.00000       0.00000       1.00000       0.01000

Lateral flow travel time and enrichment ratios are computed by SWAT+, there is no canopy storage, and cn3_swf = 0 puts the moisture condition III curve number at field capacity. perco = 0.5 lets only about 0.5% of the potential percolation leave the bottom of the profile (unless the HRU is tile drained, which resets perco to 0.1), and latq_co = 0.01 keeps lateral flow small.

refdata/Osu_1hru/hydrology.hyd uses the older column header harg_pet with the value 0, which SWAT+ treats as a pet_co of 1.

refdata/Ames_sub1/topography.hyd (first two rows):

topohru0001            0.02500      91.46300      91.46300     100.00000       1.00000  
topohru0002            0.02500      91.46300      91.46300     100.00000       1.00000

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The initialization files set the state of plants, soils and water bodies on the first day of the run. The general ones are:

  • plant.ini: plant communities, with the starting state of each plant. A land use in landuse.lum names a community in its plnt_com column.
  • soil_plant.ini: for each HRU, links to the records that initialize soil nutrients, pesticides, pathogens, salts, heavy metals and constituents. An HRU names a record in the soil_plant_init column of hru-data.hru.
  • nutrients.sol: initial soil nitrate, labile phosphorus and humus properties, named in the nutrients column of soil_plant.ini.
  • om_water.ini: initial water, sediment and nutrient concentrations of channels, reservoirs and wetlands, named in the org_min column of their initial files.

docs.title: Initialization files
docs.text:
The init line of file.cio has eleven file names. nutrients.sol is the second name on the soils line. Several salt and constituent files are opened under fixed names, whatever file.cio says.

File How the name is set Status in 62.0.1 Documented in plant.ini init line, name 1 Read plant.ini soil_plant.ini init line, name 2 Read soil_plant.ini om_water.ini init line, name 3 Read om_water.ini pest_hru.ini init line, name 4 Read pesticides pest_water.ini init line, name 5 Read pesticides path_hru.ini init line, name 6 Read pathogens path_water.ini init line, name 7 Read pathogens hmet_hru.ini init line, name 8 Read, values not used heavy metals hmet_water.ini init line, name 9 Not read heavy metals salt_hru.ini init line, name 10 The file.cio name is not used. SWAT+ opens a file called salt_hru.ini. salts salt_water.ini init line, name 11 Not read.
