docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
parameters.bsn contains the coefficients that apply to the whole watershed: initial soil water, surface runoff lag, peak rate factors, nutrient and pesticide transport coefficients, denitrification, channel routing coefficients, lapse rates, erosion coefficients for sub-daily runs and the starting CO2 concentration. It is named in the second position of the basin line of file.cio (default parameters.bsn). Several of the parameters only matter for the methods selected in codes.bsn.

If the file named in file.cio does not exist, every parameter keeps its built-in value, after the zero-value replacements described in Zero and missing values.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Line 3 contains 44 values in the order below: 42 real numbers followed by two integers. The reader matches values by position only, so all 44 must be present and in this order. The table gives the column headers the SWAT+ Editor writes; several no longer describe what the model does with the value.

# Column Units Built-in value Typical range Description 1 lai_noevap - 3.0 - Not used. Read and can be changed by calibration, but no routine uses it. 2 sw_init fraction 0.0 0 to 1 Initial soil water as a fraction of field capacity, the same for all soils. 0 means it is calculated from average annual precipitation. See Initial soil water. 3 surq_lag - 4.0 1 to 24 Surface runoff lag coefficient. See Surface runoff lag. 4 adj_pkrt - 1.0 0.5 to 2 Multiplier on the monthly mean fraction of daily rain that falls in the maximum half hour, calculated from the weather generator statistics (limited to 0.1 to 0.95). The daily fraction drawn from it is used by the half-hour intensity peak rate method (sed_det = 1), the rainfall erosivity of the MUSLE, urban washoff and the generation of sub-daily rainfall. 5 adj_pkrt_sed - 484.0 - Peak rate factor of the NRCS peak runoff equation, used for HRU erosion when sed_det = 0 in codes.bsn and for wetlands. See Peak rate factor. 6 lin_sed - 0.0 0 and up Pesticide groundwater mixing factor. See Pesticides in aquifers. 7 exp_sed - 0.0 0 or 1 Temperature-dependent pesticide decay: 1 on, any other value off. See Pesticide decay and temperature. 8 orgn_min 1/day 0.003 0.0003 to 0.003 Rate factor for mineralization of the active humus N and P pools (static carbon model, carbon = 0). 9 n_uptake - 20.0 0 to 100 Nitrogen uptake distribution parameter. See Uptake distribution. 10 p_uptake - 20.0 0 to 100 Phosphorus uptake distribution parameter. 11 n_perc - 0.10 0 to 1 Nitrate percolation coefficient: ratio of the nitrate concentration in surface runoff to the concentration in water leaving the top layer. 12 p_perc m³/Mg 10.0 10 to 17.5 Phosphorus percolation coefficient, used in the leaching of soluble P from each layer. 13 p_soil m³/Mg 175.0 100 to 200 Phosphorus soil partitioning coefficient: ratio of soluble P in the top 10 mm of soil to soluble P in surface runoff. 14 p_avail fraction 0.40 0.01 to 0.7 Phosphorus availability index: fraction of fertilizer P that is in solution after the fast reaction period. Sets the balance between the labile and active mineral P pools in the original P model (soil_p = 0). 15 rsd_decomp fraction/day 0.05 0.02 to 0.1 Residue decomposition coefficient: daily fraction of residue that decomposes under ideal conditions. Used for every plant whose plnt_decomp in plants.plt is 0. 16 pest_perc - 0.5 0 to 1 Pesticide percolation coefficient: ratio of the pesticide concentration in surface runoff and lateral flow to the concentration in percolate. 17 msk_co1 - 0.75 0 to 10 Weight of the storage time constant at bankfull depth in the Muskingum storage constant. 18 msk_co2 - 0.25 0 to 10 Weight of the storage time constant at 0.1 bankfull depth in the Muskingum storage constant. 19 msk_x - 0.20 0 to 0.3 Muskingum weighting factor for inflow and outflow in channel storage. 20 nperco_lchtile - 0.5 0 to 1 Ratio of the nitrate concentration in tile flow to the concentration in the mobile water of the tile layer. 21 evap_adj - 0.60 0.5 to 1 Channel evaporation adjustment factor: multiplier on station PET for evaporation from the channel water surface. 22 scoef - 1.0 0 to 1 Channel storage coefficient of the variable storage routing method (rte_cha = 0 in codes.bsn). 23 denit_exp - 1.40 0 to 3 Denitrification exponential rate coefficient. See Denitrification. 24 denit_frac - 1.30 see text Denitrification threshold on the soil water factor. See Denitrification. 25 man_bact fraction 0.15 - Not used. 26 adj_uhyd h 0.0 0 and up Added to the base time of the sub-daily unit hydrograph. See unit hydrograph. 27 cn_froz 1/mm 0.000862 - Frozen soil coefficient of the curve number retention parameter. See Frozen soil. 28 dorm_hr h -1.0 0 to 24 Day length threshold for dormancy. 0 or less means it is calculated from latitude. See Dormancy threshold. 29 plaps mm/km 0.0 - Precipitation lapse rate. Positive values increase precipitation with elevation. Used when lapse = 1 in codes.bsn. 30 tlaps °C/km 6.5 - Temperature lapse rate. Positive values decrease temperature with elevation. Used when lapse = 1 in codes.bsn. 31 n_fix_max kg N/ha/day 20.0 1 to 20 Maximum daily nitrogen fixation of a plant. 32 rsd_decay fraction/day 0.01 0 to 0.05 Minimum daily residue decay fraction. The daily decay rate of residue is never below this value. 33 rsd_cover ha/t 0.75 - Residue cover factor in the USLE C factor. See USLE C factor. 34 urb_init_abst mm 1.0 0 to 10 Maximum initial abstraction on impervious urban areas. Used only with Green-Ampt (gampt = 1). 35 petco_pmpt % 100.0 - Not used. The PET of every method is adjusted with pet_co in hydrology.hyd instead. 36 uhyd_alpha - 1.0 0.5 to 10 Shape coefficient of the gamma unit hydrograph (uhyd = 1 in codes.bsn). 37 splash - 0.0 0.9 to 3.1 Splash erosion coefficient. See Sub-daily erosion. 38 rill - 0.0 0.5 to 2 Rill erosion coefficient, a multiplier on the USLE K factor of the top layer. 39 surq_exp - 0.0 1 to 3 Exponent on bed shear stress in overland flow erosion. 40 cov_mgt - 0.0 0.001 to 0.45 Scaling factor on the cover and management factor in overland flow erosion. 41 cha_d50 mm 0.0 - Not used. The median particle size of each channel is read from the channel input. 42 co2 ppm 400.0 - Atmospheric CO2 concentration, used for every year when there is no co2_yr.dat. See CO2. 43 day_lag_max days 0 - Not used as read. The model always sets it to 2. 44 igen - 5 0 and up Random number seed code. See Random numbers.

Values are read in one free-format read. A line with fewer values continues onto the next line, and the parameters that are not reached keep their built-in values. A value that cannot be read ends the read without a message.

docs.title: Zero and missing values
docs.text:
After reading, SWAT+ replaces values that are zero or negative (strictly, below \(10^{-6}\)) for some parameters. For most of them the replacement is the built-in value, so leaving a column at 0 has the same effect as entering the built-in value. These are: lai_noevap, surq_lag, adj_pkrt, n_uptake, p_uptake, n_perc, p_perc, p_soil, p_avail, rsd_decomp, pest_perc, msk_co1, msk_co2, msk_x, nperco_lchtile, evap_adj, denit_exp, denit_frac, man_bact, cn_froz, n_fix_max, rsd_decay, rsd_cover and uhyd_alpha.

The exceptions are:

Column Value read Value used adj_pkrt_sed 0 or less 1.0 (the built-in value is 484.0) orgn_min 0 or less 0.0003 (the built-in value is 0.003) urb_init_abst 0 or less 0.0 (the built-in value is 1.0) co2 below 100 400.0 day_lag_max any 2

sw_init, adj_uhyd, dorm_hr, splash, rill, surq_exp, cov_mgt and cha_d50 stay at 0 when 0 is read, and 0 has a meaning for some of them (see the sections below). lin_sed, exp_sed, scoef, plaps, tlaps and igen are used as read.

docs.title: Initial soil water
docs.text:
All soils start at the same fraction of field capacity. If sw_init is 0 or less, the fraction is calculated from the average annual precipitation \(P\) (mm) of the HRU's weather generator station:

\[f_{fc} = \frac{P}{P + \exp(9.043 - 0.002135\,P)}\]

A warm-up period of at least one year (nyskip in print.prt) makes results largely independent of sw_init.

docs.title: Surface runoff lag
docs.text:
In HRUs with a long time of concentration, only part of the surface runoff reaches the channel on the day it is generated. The fraction released each day is

\[f_{rel} = 1 - \exp\!\left(-\frac{\mathrm{surq\_lag}}{t_{conc}}\right)\]

with \(t_{conc}\) in hours. In sub-daily runs \(t_{conc}\) is expressed in time steps. The rest is kept in surface storage and added to the next day's runoff. Smaller values of surq_lag keep more water in storage and smooth the hydrograph.

docs.title: Peak rate factor
docs.text: The column labelled adj_pkrt_sed by the SWAT+ Editor is the peak rate factor of the NRCS peak runoff equation (see peak runoff rate). The built-in value, 484, is the standard factor for the NRCS dimensionless unit hydrograph. The Editor writes 1.0 in this column, and a value of 0 is also replaced by 1.0. A factor of 1 gives peak rates 484 times lower than the standard factor, which lowers MUSLE sediment yields from HRUs when sed_det = 0. The value only affects the peak rate used for erosion and in wetlands; it does not change runoff volumes.

docs.title: Pesticides in aquifers
docs.text:
The columns labelled lin_sed and exp_sed by the Editor are pesticide parameters in 62.0.1. In each aquifer, the pesticide concentration in return flow and seepage is the pesticide mass divided by a mixing volume:

\[C = \frac{M_{pest}}{f_{mix}\,S_{aqu} + Q_{rtn} + Q_{revap} + Q_{seep}}\]

where \(f_{mix}\) is lin_sed, \(S_{aqu}\) is the aquifer storage and the \(Q\) terms are the day's return flow, revap and seepage (mm). With lin_sed = 0 the concentration is based on the day's outflows only. Larger values dilute the pesticide in more of the stored water and slow its release.

docs.title: Pesticide decay and temperature
docs.text:
With exp_sed = 1 (the value 1.0; other values such as 2 do not count), pesticide decay in soil, on foliage, in aquifers, in channel water and in channel bed sediment uses half-lives adjusted for temperature with a Q10 model:

\[t_{1/2}(T) = t_{1/2,25}\; Q_{10}^{(25 - T)/10}, \qquad Q_{10} = 2.58\]

where \(t_{1/2,25}\) is the half-life from the pesticide database, taken as the value at 25 °C, and the daily fraction remaining is \(\exp(-0.693 / t_{1/2}(T))\). Soil decay uses the layer temperature, foliar decay the top soil layer temperature, and channel decay the water temperature. In aquifers the temperature is fixed at 0 °C, which makes aquifer half-lives about 10.7 times longer than the database value. Any other value of exp_sed uses the database half-lives without a temperature adjustment.

The Ames example file (see Example) has exp_sed = 1.0, so temperature-dependent decay is on in that dataset.

docs.title: Uptake distribution
docs.text:
The maximum nitrogen uptake from the soil above depth \(z\) is

\[U(z) = U_{pot}\,\frac{1 - \exp(-\beta_n\,z / z_{root})}{1 - \exp(-\beta_n)}\]

where \(\beta_n\) is n_uptake and \(z_{root}\) is the root depth. Larger values concentrate uptake near the surface. Because the top 10 mm interacts with surface runoff, n_uptake affects the nitrate available for runoff; lower layers can make up a shortfall in the upper layers, so plant N stress changes little with this parameter. p_uptake works the same way for phosphorus.

docs.title: Denitrification
docs.text:
Denitrification in a soil layer is

\[N_{denit} = NO_3\left[1 - \exp\!\left(-\mathrm{denit\_exp}\;\gamma_{tmp}\;\frac{OC}{100}\right)\right]\]

where \(\gamma_{tmp}\) is the temperature factor and \(OC\) the organic carbon content (%). It only occurs on days when the soil water factor \(\gamma_{sw}\) is at or above denit_frac.

With the static carbon model (carbon = 0), \(\gamma_{sw} = 0.1 + 0.9\sqrt{SW/FC}\), with no upper limit. With the default denit_frac of 1.3, denitrification needs \(SW/FC \ge 1.78\), that is, a layer well above field capacity.

With the dynamic carbon model (carbon = 2), \(\gamma_{sw}\) comes from the water factor selected in carbon.bsn and is never above 1. Any denit_frac above 1, including the default 1.3, then switches denitrification off for the whole run. Datasets using carbon = 2 need a denit_frac of 1 or less to simulate denitrification.

docs.title: Frozen soil
docs.text:
When the second soil layer is at or below 0 °C, the curve number retention parameter \(S\) is reduced:

\[S_{frz} = S_{max}\left[1 - \exp(-\mathrm{cn\_froz}\cdot S)\right]\]

which increases runoff from frozen soil. The same adjustment is applied with Green-Ampt.

docs.title: Dormancy threshold
docs.text: A plant goes dormant when the day length falls below the station's minimum day length plus a threshold \(t_{dorm}\) (hours). If dorm_hr is above 0, \(t_{dorm}\) = dorm_hr everywhere. Otherwise it depends on the latitude \(\phi\) of the weather generator station: 1 h above 40°, \((|\phi| - 20)/20\) h between 20° and 40°, and -1 h below 20°.

docs.title: USLE C factor
docs.text:
The C factor is the product of a residue factor and a biomass factor:

\[C = \exp\!\left(-\mathrm{rsd\_cover}\cdot\frac{R + 1}{1000}\right)\left[1 - f_{cov}\,\exp(-0.328\,h_c)\right]\]

where \(R\) is the residue on the surface (kg/ha), \(h_c\) is the canopy height (m), and \(f_{cov}\) is the ground cover fraction of the above-ground biomass. This is the only C factor method in 62.0.1 (see USLE C factor).

docs.title: Sub-daily erosion
docs.text:
With Green-Ampt (gampt above 0 in codes.bsn), sediment from each time step is the sum of splash and overland flow erosion. Splash erosion decreases with runoff depth \(h\) (mm) as \(\exp(-\mathrm{splash}\cdot h/1000)\) and depends on rainfall kinetic energy and a soil texture erodibility. Overland flow erosion is

\[E_{ov} = 11.02\;\mathrm{rill}\;K\;\mathrm{cov\_mgt}\;C\;\tau^{\,\mathrm{surq\_exp}}\]

in kg/h/m², where \(K\) is the USLE K factor of the top layer, \(C\) is a cover factor from biomass and residue, and \(\tau\) is the bed shear stress (N/m²). With the built-in values of 0 for rill or cov_mgt, overland flow erosion is zero.

docs.title: CO2
docs.text: Without a co2_yr.dat file in the run folder, every year uses co2. With the file, the yearly values come from it (see co2_yr.dat). The radiation use efficiency of plants is adjusted for CO2 only when co2 in parameters.bsn is above 350 ppm, even when the yearly values come from co2_yr.dat. Penman-Monteith PET uses the yearly values in all cases.

docs.title: Random numbers
docs.text: With igen = 0, the weather generator and other random processes start from fixed seeds, so every run gives the same random sequence. With any other value, each seed is advanced by a number of steps that depends on igen, so different igen values give different sequences. The same igen always gives the same sequence, so a new value is needed for each different realisation.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
These parameters can be changed during calibration through calibration.cal with object type bsn, using their model names: surlag (surq_lag), adj_pkr (adj_pkrt), prf (adj_pkrt_sed), evlai (lai_noevap), ffcb (sw_init), cmn (orgn_min), nperco (n_perc), pperco (p_perc), phoskd (p_soil), psp (p_avail), rsdco (rsd_decomp), percop (pest_perc), msk_co1, msk_co2, msk_x, nperco_lchtile, evrch (evap_adj), cdn (denit_exp), sdnco (denit_frac), tb_adj (adj_uhyd), n_updis (n_uptake), rsd_covco (rsd_cover), dorm_hr, plaps and tlaps. See parameter change files.

The changes in calibration.cal are applied once, after the HRUs, channels and weather stations have been set up. Several of these parameters are only used during that setup, so changing them in calibration.cal has no effect on the run:

  • cmn, nperco, pperco, phoskd, psp and nperco_lchtile have already been copied to each HRU. Use the HRU-level names cmn_h, nperco_h, pperco_h, phoskd_h, psp_h and nperco_lchtile_h instead.
  • ffcb: the initial soil water has already been set.
  • adj_pkr and dorm_hr: the half-hour rainfall fractions and the dormancy thresholds of the weather stations have already been calculated.
  • msk_co1, msk_co2 and msk_x: the Muskingum coefficients of the channels have already been calculated.
  • rsdco: it has already been copied to the plants with plnt_decomp = 0.

surlag is recalculated into the runoff release fraction when it is changed, and the others are used directly during the simulation, so their changes take effect.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:

How the model reads some of these values:

  • sw_init = 0.5: soils start at half of field capacity.
  • adj_pkrt_sed = 1.0: the NRCS peak rate factor is 1. The standard factor is 484.
  • exp_sed = 1.0: temperature-dependent pesticide decay is on.
  • orgn_min = 0.0: replaced by 0.0003.
  • cn_froz = 0.0: replaced by 0.000862.
  • dorm_hr = 0.0: the dormancy threshold is calculated from latitude.
  • plaps = 0.0 and tlaps = 0.0: no lapse rate adjustment, even if lapse = 1 in codes.bsn.
  • denit_frac = 1.3: this dataset uses carbon = 2 in its codes.bsn, so no denitrification occurs (see Denitrification).
  • petco_pmpt, cha_d50 and man_bact have no effect; day_lag_max is set to 2.
  • igen = 0: fixed random seeds.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
A precipitation data file contains the measured precipitation of one gauge, as daily totals or as values for each sub-daily time step. Each file is named on one line of pcp.cli, and a weather station uses it when the pcp column of weather-sta.cli gives the same name. Days without a usable value are filled by the weather generator station named in the wgn column of the same weather station.

SWAT+ does not check the file extension. .pcp is the usual one. If pcp_path in file.cio is not null, its value is put in front of every file name in pcp.cli (see path prefixes).

docs.title: Format
docs.text: Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is a column header; both are skipped. Line 3 describes the gauge and every later line is one record.

docs.title: Gauge line
docs.text:
SWAT+ Editor writes the header nbyr tstep lat lon elev above this line.

# Column Units Description 1 nbyr years Number of years of record. SWAT+ uses it to size the store for the data, so it must be at least the number of calendar years the record spans. 2 tstep values per day 0 for daily data. For sub-daily data, the number of values per day, which must equal step in time.sim (24 for hourly data). 3 lat decimal degrees Latitude of the gauge. Not used by SWAT+. 4 lon decimal degrees Longitude of the gauge. Not used by SWAT+. 5 elev m Elevation of the gauge. Used only for the elevation adjustment.

docs.title: Daily records
docs.text:
With tstep = 0, each record has three values:

# Column Units Description 1 year - Calendar year. 2 day - Day of the year, 1 to 366. Called jday in earlier documentation. 3 pcp mm Precipitation for the day. A value of -97 or less marks the day as missing.

docs.title: Sub-daily records
docs.text:
With tstep greater than 0, each record has six values:

# Column Units Description 1 year - Calendar year. 2 day - Day of the year, 1 to 366. Called jday in earlier documentation. 3 month - Month, called mon in earlier documentation. Not used by SWAT+. 4 day of month - Not used by SWAT+. 5 step - Time step within the day, called hr in earlier documentation. Not used by SWAT+. 6 pcp mm Precipitation for the time step.

SWAT+ places the values of each day in the order they appear, so every day needs step records in time order. The month, day of month and step columns do not position the value.

docs.title: Record order
docs.text: Records must be continuous and in date order. SWAT+ counts years by watching for day 365 or 366 followed by a record from a new year, so a gap at the end of a year shifts every later year of the record. A file that starts or ends part way through a year is fine.

docs.title: Reading and storage
docs.text:
Records before the start of the simulation are skipped when the file is read. Storage starts with the first record whose year is at or after yrc_start and whose day is at or after day_start in time.sim.

When the record starts in a year after the simulation start year and day_start is later than the first day in the file, the records of that first year before day_start are also skipped. Those days then read as 0 mm instead of being filled by the weather generator.

docs.title: Missing days
docs.text:
In a daily run, SWAT+ fills a day from the weather generator when

  • the value is -97 or less (SWAT+ Editor and most tools write -99), or
  • the day is before the first record or after the last record of the file.

Generated precipitation uses the monthly statistics of the station's weather-wgn.cli entry and the wet or dry state of the previous day. The method is described in Climate and weather.

docs.title: Sub-daily runs
docs.text:
A sub-daily file is read when tstep is greater than 0. step in time.sim sets the number of steps per day of the run, and SWAT+ stores that many values per day. If the two numbers differ, the values are assigned to the wrong steps: with step = 0 or 1 and an hourly file, only the last hour of each day is kept.

Missing and out-of-range values are handled differently from daily data in 62.0.1:

  • When a step has a value of -97 or less, SWAT+ calls the generator, but the day's total is still the sum of the file values for that day, missing-value flags included.
  • Days outside the record are not generated. Inside the stored years they read as 0 mm.
  • Values are looked up by simulation year counted from the simulation start, so the record must start on or before the simulation start date.
  • From the second simulation year on, the values used for 1 January come from 1 January of the previous simulation year.

Sub-daily files should therefore be complete, without missing values, and cover the whole simulation period.

docs.title: Elevation adjustment
docs.text:
When lapse = 1 in codes.bsn, the precipitation of each HRU is changed for the difference between the HRU elevation and the gauge elevation:

\[P_{hru} = \max\left(0,\; P + \mathrm{plaps}\,\frac{z_{hru} - z_{gauge}}{1000}\right)\]

where \(P\) is the station precipitation (mm), plaps is the precipitation lapse rate in parameters.bsn (mm per km, default 0), \(z_{hru}\) is the elev column of hru.con and \(z_{gauge}\) is elev from this file (m). When the station's pcp column is sim, the elevation of the weather generator station is used for \(z_{gauge}\).

The adjustment is added every day, dry days included, so a positive plaps gives HRUs above the gauge a small amount of precipitation on every day. The adjustment values are calculated during channel and reservoir routing, so in a model without channels or reservoirs they remain zero.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text: The calibration parameter precip (object type cli) changes the stored daily values of listed precipitation records over a window of days and years. See Climate changes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
First lines of refdata/Ames_sub1/ames.pcp in the SWAT+ repository, and part of 2012:

AME.pcp
 NBYR    TSTEP      LAT     LONG     ELEV
   121        0    42.04   -93.89   316
1900 1 -99
1900 2 -99
1900 3 -99
...
2012 55 12.4
2012 56 0
2012 57 -99
2012 58 0

A daily record (tstep = 0) of 121 years, 1900 to 2020, at 316 m. The Ames run starts in 1975, so the records from 1900 to 1974 are skipped when the file is read. Of the days from 1975 on, 31 are marked missing (-99), such as day 57 of 2012, and the weather generator fills them during the run.

  • codes.bsn and parameters.bsn: lapse switch and plaps rate.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
SWAT+ simulates the pesticides listed in constituents.cs. It follows each one on plant foliage, in the soil layers, in surface runoff, lateral flow, tile flow and percolation, in channel water and bed sediment, in reservoirs and in aquifers. Four files describe them:

File Named in Content pesticide.pes hru_parm_db line of file.cio (default pesticide.pes) Properties of each pesticide. pest_hru.ini init line of file.cio Initial pesticide in soils and on plants. pest_water.ini init line of file.cio Initial pesticide in channels, reservoirs and aquifers. pest_metabolite.pes fixed name, not in file.cio Degradation products (daughters) of each parent pesticide.

Every pesticide named in constituents.cs must have a row in pesticide.pes with the same name. The database can contain many more pesticides than the run simulates. Pesticide applications in management.sch and decision tables name rows of pesticide.pes, and the application method comes from chem_app.ops.

docs.title: pesticide.pes
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one pesticide with 17 values and a description, in the order below. The reader does not match columns by header name, so every value must be present and in this order.

# Column Units Typical range Description 1 name - - Name of the pesticide, up to 16 characters. Must be unique. 2 soil_ads (mg/kg)/(mg/L) 1 to 10⁹ Soil adsorption coefficient normalized for soil organic carbon (\(K_{oc}\)). 3 frac_wash fraction 0 to 1 Fraction of the pesticide on foliage washed off by a rainfall event. 4 hl_foliage days 0 to 10,000 Half-life on foliage. 0 means no decay. 5 hl_soil days 0 to 100,000 Half-life in the soil. 0 means no decay. 6 solub mg/L - Solubility in water. Upper limit of the concentration in water leaving a soil layer. 7 aq_hlife days - Half-life in channel, reservoir and aquifer water. 0 means no decay. Earlier documentation had aq_reac here, a reaction rate in 1/day; the column is now a half-life in days. 8 aq_volat m/day - Volatilization coefficient in channel and reservoir water. 9 mol_wt g/mol - Molecular weight. Used for the water and sediment mixing velocity and for the mass of metabolites. 10 aq_resus m/day - Resuspension velocity of pesticide sorbed to bed sediment. 11 aq_settle m/day - Settling velocity of pesticide sorbed to suspended sediment. 12 ben_act_dep m - Depth of the active bed sediment layer. 13 ben_bury m/day - Burial velocity in bed sediment. 14 ben_hlife days - Half-life in bed sediment. 0 means no decay. Earlier documentation had ben_reac here, a reaction rate in 1/day; the column is now a half-life in days. 15 pl_uptake - 0 and up Transpiration stream concentration factor (TSCF): ratio of the concentration in the water taken up by roots to the dissolved concentration in the soil. 0 turns plant uptake off. 16 harvest_sink 0 or 1 0, 1 1: pesticide taken up by the plant leaves the system. 0: it stays in the plant and returns to the soil with the residue when the plant is harvested or killed. 17 resistance_n fraction 0 to 1 Soil water used for the dissolved concentration in plant uptake. 0 uses the actual soil water, 1 uses field capacity, values in between blend the two. 18 description - - Free text, one word.

Columns 15 to 17 are new in 62.0.1. Files written for earlier revisions have 14 values (name and 13 numbers) and then a description. With such a file the first 14 values of each row are read correctly, and the read of the row stops with an error when it meets the description where pl_uptake is expected. No message is written and the next row is read normally. The three new columns keep their built-in values (pl_uptake = 0, harvest_sink = 1, resistance_n = 1), so there is no plant uptake, which is the behaviour of earlier revisions. To use plant uptake, add the three columns before the description.

docs.title: Half-lives and decay
docs.text:
Each day the pesticide in a compartment decays by first-order kinetics. The fraction left after one day is

\[f = \exp\left(-\frac{0.693}{t_{1/2}}\right)\]

where \(t_{1/2}\) is the half-life of that compartment (hl_foliage, hl_soil, aq_hlife or ben_hlife). The half-life entered is a lumped value covering volatilization, photolysis, hydrolysis, biological degradation and other reactions. In channels the decay is scaled by the travel time through the reach, up to one day.

For most pesticides the foliar half-life is much shorter than the soil half-life because of volatilization and photodecomposition. If no foliar value is available, a common estimate is 0.25 to 0.5 times the soil half-life, lower for pesticides with a vapor pressure below 10⁻⁵ mm Hg, and at most 30 days.

docs.title: Temperature-dependent decay
docs.text:
Column 7 of parameters.bsn switches temperature-dependent decay on. The SWAT+ Editor writes this column under the header exp_sed. When its value is 1, each half-life is taken as the value at 25 °C and adjusted with a Q10 of 2.58:

\[t_{1/2}(T) = t_{1/2,25}\; 2.58^{(25 - T)/10}\]

The temperature \(T\) is the soil layer temperature for soil, the top soil layer temperature for foliage, and the water temperature for channel water and bed sediment. For aquifers the temperature is 0 °C in 62.0.1, so aquifer half-lives are about 10.7 times the 25 °C value. Reservoirs do not use the adjustment.

Any other value in that column gives the constant decay above. Check this column when a model is moved to 62.0.1: editor files commonly have 1.0 there, which switches the adjustment on.

docs.title: Sorption and transport
docs.text:
The soil adsorption coefficient of a layer is

\[K_d = K_{oc}\,\frac{OC}{100}\]

where \(OC\) is the organic carbon content of the layer in percent. The pesticide in a layer is split between the soil and the water flowing through it according to \(K_d\). The concentration in water leaving a layer is limited to solub. The concentration in surface runoff is the concentration in percolate times pest_perc of parameters.bsn.

On a day with at least 2.54 mm of precipitation, frac_wash of the pesticide on each plant's foliage is washed off to the top soil layer.

docs.title: Plant uptake
docs.text:
When pl_uptake is above 0, growing plants take up pesticide from each soil layer with the water they transpire:

\[U = \mathrm{TSCF}\;\frac{W_{up}}{\theta_{eff} + W_{up} + K_d\,\rho_b\,h}\;M\]

where \(W_{up}\) is the water taken up from the layer (mm), \(\theta_{eff}\) is the soil water blended toward field capacity by resistance_n, \(\rho_b\) the bulk density, \(h\) the layer thickness (mm) and \(M\) the pesticide in the layer (kg/ha). Uptake is reported as pl_uptake in the pesticide output. With harvest_sink = 0, the pesticide kept in the plant returns to the soil when the plant is harvested or killed.

docs.title: Metabolites
docs.text:
When a parent pesticide decays, a daughter listed in pest_metabolite.pes receives

\[M_{daughter} = \Delta M_{parent}\; f_{frac}\;\frac{MW_{daughter}}{MW_{parent}}\]

where \(f_{frac}\) is the daughter fraction for that compartment and \(MW\) the mol_wt values. Foliage uses foliar_fr, soil uses soil_fr, channel water uses aq_fr and channel bed sediment uses ben_fr. In 62.0.1 reservoirs (water and bed) and aquifers use soil_fr.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text: These parameters can be changed during calibration through calibration.cal: pst_koc, pst_washoff, pst_foliar_hlife, pst_soil_hlife, pst_solub, pst_aq_hlife, pst_aq_volat, pst_aq_settle, pst_aq_resus, pst_ben_hlife, pst_ben_bury and pst_ben_act_dep. The daily decay factors are computed from the half-lives when pesticide.pes is read, so a calibration change to a half-life only has an effect when temperature-dependent decay is on.

docs.title: pesticide.pes example
docs.text:
The first rows of refdata/Osu_1hru/pesticide.pes in the SWAT+ repository, as shipped:

pesticide.pes: written by SWAT+ editor v2.2.0 on 2023-03-22 04:25 for SWAT+ rev.60.5.4
name                  soil_ads     frac_wash    hl_foliage       hl_soil         solub      aq_hlife      aq_volat        mol_wt      aq_resus     aq_settle   ben_act_dep      ben_bury     ben_hlife  description
245-tp              2600.00000       0.40000       5.00000      20.00000       2.50000       0.00700       0.00001       0.10000       0.00200       0.50000       0.30000       0.00200       0.05000  Silvex_Amine
2plus2                20.00000       0.95000      10.00000      21.00000  660000.00000       0.00700       0.00001       0.10000       0.00200       0.50000       0.30000       0.00200       0.05000  Mecoprop

The file was written for revision 60.5.4 and has no pl_uptake, harvest_sink or resistance_n columns. As described above, each row is read up to ben_hlife, the description is not stored, and the three new columns take their built-in values, so no pesticide is taken up by plants.

Silvex (245-tp) sorbs strongly (\(K_{oc}\) of 2600) and has a soil half-life of 20 days. Mecoprop (2plus2) is very soluble and hardly sorbs.

Every row has aq_hlife = 0.007 and ben_hlife = 0.05. These match the reaction coefficients in 1/day of the older database format, but 62.0.1 reads them as half-lives in days. A half-life of 0.007 days leaves a fraction \(\exp(-0.693/0.007) \approx 10^{-43}\) after one day, and 0.05 days leaves about \(10^{-6}\). Osu_1hru has 1 in column 7 of parameters.bsn, so the half-lives are adjusted for temperature (except in reservoirs), which lengthens them at temperatures below 25 °C but not enough to change the result. Any of these pesticides that reached channel water, bed sediment, a reservoir or an aquifer would be almost entirely gone within a day. Osu_1hru has no constituents.cs, so in that model no pesticide is simulated and the file is read without effect.

docs.title: pest_hru.ini
docs.text:
Initial pesticide in the soil and on plants of HRUs. An HRU selects a record by name in the pest column of soil_plant.ini.

The file is read in two passes that expect different layouts:

  • The first pass counts records. It expects a title line, then for each record a header line, a name line and one line per pesticide.
  • The second pass reads the values. It expects a title line and one header line, then for each record a name line and one line per pesticide.

A file with one record satisfies both. With more than one record the second pass reads the header line of record 2 as its name and the values that follow are shifted, so use one record.

Each pesticide line has three values, one line per pesticide in the order of constituents.cs:

Value Units Description name - Pesticide name, for readability. Not checked. soil mg/kg Concentration in the soil. The same concentration is given to every soil layer. plant kg/ha Pesticide on the foliage. It is shared among the plants by leaf area; if there is no leaf area at the start, nothing is put on the foliage.

docs.title: pest_water.ini
docs.text:
Initial pesticide in channels, reservoirs, wetlands and aquifers. Channels, reservoirs and wetlands select a record by name in their initial condition files (initial.cha, initial.res), and aquifers in initial.aqu.

Line 1 is a title and line 2 a header. Each record starts with a name line. The values follow as one list: a label, then the water value of each pesticide, then the bed sediment value of each pesticide, in the order of constituents.cs. Line breaks within the list are free, but the counting pass expects two lines per pesticide after the name line. For two pesticides:

pest_water.ini: initial pesticide in water
name
ch_init
atrazine  0.002
0.001
0.05
0.02

Here atrazine is the label, the water values are 0.002 and 0.001, and the bed sediment values 0.05 and 0.02.

Value Units Description water mg/L Concentration in the water. Channels multiply it by the initial channel water volume. Aquifers read it as mg/kg of aquifer material over the aquifer depth with a bulk density of 2.0 t/m³. benthic mg/kg Concentration in the active bed sediment layer. Channels multiply it by the volume of the active bed layer.

Reservoirs use both values as given, without a conversion by volume.

docs.title: pest_metabolite.pes
docs.text:
The degradation products of each parent pesticide. SWAT+ reads it if a file of this name exists in the run directory.

Line 1 is a title and line 2 a header. For each parent there is one line with the parent name and the number of daughters, followed by one line per daughter:

Value Units Description name - Daughter pesticide name. Must also be listed in constituents.cs and pesticide.pes. foliar_fr fraction Fraction of the parent decayed on foliage that becomes this daughter. soil_fr fraction Fraction of the parent decayed in the soil that becomes this daughter. Also used in reservoirs and aquifers. aq_fr fraction Fraction of the parent decayed in channel water that becomes this daughter. ben_fr fraction Fraction of the parent decayed in channel bed sediment that becomes this daughter.

The parent name must match a row of pesticide.pes. If it does not, its daughter lines are not skipped and the rest of the file is read out of step.

pest_metabolite.pes: metabolites
parent        num_metab
aatrex        1
deethyl_atr   0.2   0.3   0.1   0.1

Atrazine (aatrex) has one daughter. 30% of the atrazine decayed in the soil, adjusted by the ratio of molecular weights, becomes deethyl_atr.

docs.title: Related files
docs.text:
• constituents.cs: the list of pesticides simulated.
  • soil_plant.ini: links HRUs to pest_hru.ini records.
  • initial.cha, initial.res, initial.aqu: link channels, reservoirs and aquifers to pest_water.ini records.
  • chem_app.ops and management.sch: pesticide applications.
  • parameters.bsn: pest_perc and the temperature-dependent decay switch in column 7.
  • Pathogens and heavy metals use the same initial condition layout.
Sources
  • Readers: pest_parm_read.f90, pest_hru_aqu_read.f90, pest_cha_res_read.f90, pest_metabolite_read.f90
  • Types: type pesticide_db, type pesticide_cp, type daughter_decay_fractions in pesticide_data_module.f90; type cs_soil_init_concentrations and type cs_water_init_concentrations in constituent_mass_module.f90

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
plants.plt is the plant growth database. Each row is one plant species, crop variety or land cover, with the parameters SWAT+ needs to grow it: plant type, heat units to maturity, leaf area development, radiation use efficiency, canopy height, rooting depth, temperature limits, nutrient content, stomatal conductance and residue properties.

Plant communities in plant.ini, plant operations in management.sch and decision tables, and land uses in landuse.lum all refer to rows of this file by name. The names are also used by the GIS interfaces to link land cover maps to SWAT+ land uses.

The file is named on the hru_parm_db line of file.cio (default plants.plt). If the file is missing, the database is empty.

The database distributed with SWAT+ has parameters for most common crops, grasses, trees and land covers. If a land use or plant is not in it, start from a row for a plant with similar growth habits.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one plant with 56 values in the order below. The reader does not match columns by header name, so every value must be present and in this order. It ignores anything after the 56th value, so the description column written by the SWAT+ Editor has no effect.

If the event column of codes.bsn is not 0, one more word is read after the 56th value: a plant class name of up to 25 characters (for example row_crop). In that case the plant class takes the place of the description.

# Column Units Default Description 1 name - - Name of the plant or land cover, up to 40 characters. Must be unique. 2 plnt_typ - - Plant type: warm_annual, cold_annual, warm_annual_tuber, cold_annual_tuber or perennial. See Plant types. 3 gro_trig - - Growth trigger: temp_gro (growth driven by temperature and day length) or moisture_gro (tropical plants whose growth starts with the monsoon). 4 nfix_co - 0.0 Nitrogen fixation coefficient: 0.5 for legumes, 0 for non-legumes. Any value above 0 lets the plant fix nitrogen when soil nitrate cannot meet its demand. 5 days_mat days 110 Days to maturity, an integer. Used to compute the heat units to maturity. 0 means the plant uses the heat units of the whole year. See Heat units to maturity. 6 bm_e (kg/ha)/(MJ/m²) 15.0 Biomass-energy ratio (radiation use efficiency): dry biomass produced, including roots, per unit of intercepted photosynthetically active radiation, with no stress, at ambient CO2 and a vapor pressure deficit of 1 kPa. 7 harv_idx (kg/ha)/(kg/ha) 0.76 Harvest index for optimal growing conditions: fraction of above-ground biomass removed as yield. Values above 0.7 are replaced by 0.02 (see Values set by the model). 8 lai_pot m²/m² 5.0 Maximum potential leaf area index. Values are limited to 0 to 10. 9 frac_hu1 fraction 0.05 Fraction of heat units to maturity at the 1st point of the optimal leaf area development curve. 10 lai_max1 fraction 0.05 Fraction of lai_pot at the 1st point of the optimal leaf area development curve. 11 frac_hu2 fraction 0.40 Fraction of heat units to maturity at the 2nd point of the optimal leaf area development curve. 12 lai_max2 fraction 0.95 Fraction of lai_pot at the 2nd point of the optimal leaf area development curve. 13 hu_lai_decl fraction 0.99 Fraction of heat units to maturity at which leaf area starts to decline. 14 dlai_rate - 1.0 Exponent of the leaf area decline of annuals after hu_lai_decl. 1 gives a linear decline. 15 can_ht_max m 6.0 Maximum canopy height. 16 rt_dp_max m 3.5 Maximum rooting depth. The soil profile depth also limits roots. 17 tmp_opt °C 30.0 Optimal temperature for plant growth. 18 tmp_base °C 10.0 Base (minimum) temperature for plant growth. Heat units accumulate only above it. 19 frac_n_yld kg N/kg yield 0.0015 Fraction of nitrogen in the yield, dry weight. 20 frac_p_yld kg P/kg yield 0.0003 Fraction of phosphorus in the yield, dry weight. 21 frac_n_em kg N/kg biomass 0.006 Normal fraction of nitrogen in plant biomass at emergence. 22 frac_n_50 kg N/kg biomass 0.002 Normal fraction of nitrogen in plant biomass at 50% maturity. 23 frac_n_mat kg N/kg biomass 0.0015 Normal fraction of nitrogen in plant biomass at maturity. 24 frac_p_em kg P/kg biomass 0.0007 Normal fraction of phosphorus in plant biomass at emergence. 25 frac_p_50 kg P/kg biomass 0.0004 Normal fraction of phosphorus in plant biomass at 50% maturity. 26 frac_p_mat kg P/kg biomass 0.0003 Normal fraction of phosphorus in plant biomass at maturity. 27 harv_idx_ws (kg/ha)/(kg/ha) 0.01 Harvest index under severe water stress: the lowest harvest index expected, between 0 and harv_idx. 28 usle_c_min - 0.001 Minimum USLE C factor for water erosion. Values are limited to 0.001 to 1. 29 stcon_max m/s 0.002 Maximum stomatal conductance at high solar radiation and low vapor pressure deficit. Used with the Penman-Monteith ET method. 30 vpd kPa 4.0 Vapor pressure deficit at the 2nd point of the stomatal conductance curve. 31 frac_stcon fraction 0.75 Fraction of stcon_max at the 2nd point of the stomatal conductance curve. 32 ru_vpd (kg/ha)/(MJ/m²)/kPa 8.0 Rate of decline in radiation use efficiency per unit increase in vapor pressure deficit above 1 kPa. 0 turns the adjustment off. 33 co2_hi µL CO2/L air 660.0 Elevated CO2 concentration at the 2nd point of the radiation use efficiency curve. 34 bm_e_hi (kg/ha)/(MJ/m²) 16.0 Biomass-energy ratio at the CO2 concentration co2_hi. 35 plnt_decomp - 0.05 Plant residue decomposition coefficient: fraction of residue that decomposes in a day under optimal moisture, temperature, C:N and C:P. 0 takes rsd_decomp from parameters.bsn. 36 lai_min m²/m² 0.75 Minimum leaf area index of perennials during the dormant period. 37 bm_tree_acc - 0.3 Exponent that limits the maximum leaf area index of young perennials. See Perennials and trees. 38 yrs_mat years 10 Years for a perennial to reach full development, an integer. Values below 1 are set to 1. 39 bm_tree_max t/ha 1000.0 Maximum above-ground biomass. Checked once a year. 40 ext_co - 0.65 Light extinction coefficient for intercepted photosynthetically active radiation. 0 is replaced by 0.65. 41 leaf_tov_mn months 12.0 Leaf turnover time of moisture_gro perennials with minimum stress. Called leaf_tov_min in earlier documentation. 42 leaf_tov_mx months 3.0 Leaf turnover time of moisture_gro perennials with maximum stress. Called leaf_tov_max in earlier documentation. 43 bm_dieoff fraction 0.0 Factor on the excess biomass removed when above-ground biomass exceeds bm_tree_max. 0 is replaced by 1. 44 rt_st_beg fraction 0.0 Root to shoot ratio at the start of the growing season. 0 is replaced by 0.4. 45 rt_st_end fraction 0.0 Root to shoot ratio at the end of the growing season. 0 is replaced by 0.2. Tuber types always use 0.7. 46 plnt_pop1 plants/m² 0.0 Plant population at the 1st point of the population and leaf area curve. 47 frac_lai1 fraction 0.0 Fraction of lai_pot at the 1st point of the population and leaf area curve. 48 plnt_pop2 plants/m² 0.0 Plant population at the 2nd point of the population and leaf area curve. 49 frac_lai2 fraction 0.0 Fraction of lai_pot at the 2nd point of the population and leaf area curve. 50 frac_sw_gro - 0.5 Intended as the 30-day precipitation to PET ratio that starts growth of moisture_gro plants. Read but not used, which uses a fixed 0.5. 51 aeration fraction 0.2 Aeration stress threshold: the fraction of pore space above field capacity that can fill with water before the plant is stressed by lack of air. 0 is replaced by 0.2. 52 rsd_pctcov - 0.0 Residue factor for the percent cover equation. 0 is replaced by 0.4. 53 rsd_covfac - 0.0 Residue factor for the surface cover (C factor) equation. 0 is replaced by 0.04. 54 avg_lig_frac fraction 0.85 Average lignin fraction of residue. Read but not used. 55 ab_lig_frac fraction 0.15 Lignin fraction of above-ground residue. Used by the dynamic carbon model only. 56 bg_lig_frac fraction 0.12 Lignin fraction of below-ground residue (roots). Used by the dynamic carbon model only.

The defaults are the values SWAT+ uses for a component that is not set. They are not filled in for missing columns, since every row must have all 56 values.

docs.title: Plant types
docs.text:
plnt_typ decides how the plant goes through the year.

  • warm_annual and cold_annual are annual crops. A cold_annual is planted in the fall and goes dormant over winter when day length falls below the dormancy threshold. Leaf area declines after hu_lai_decl, following dlai_rate.
  • warm_annual_tuber and cold_annual_tuber are annuals whose yield is below ground. Their root to shoot ratio at the end of the season is fixed at 0.7.
  • perennial covers grasses, shrubs and trees. Perennials go dormant when day length falls below the threshold, keep at least lai_min of leaf area, and develop over yrs_mat years.

gro_trig = moisture_gro is for tropical plants. If the plant was planted with the monsoon option, it starts growing when the 30-day ratio of precipitation to potential ET reaches 0.5. Leaf turnover of moisture_gro perennials varies between leaf_tov_mx and leaf_tov_mn months with moisture stress.

docs.title: Heat units to maturity
docs.text:
SWAT+ computes the heat units a plant needs to reach maturity at the start of the run, from the monthly mean temperatures of the HRU's weather generator station.

  • days_mat = 0: the plant grows through the whole year. Heat units to maturity are 95% of the year's sum of mean daily temperature above tmp_base.
  • days_mat > 0 for an annual: the planting date is taken as the day when the sum of mean daily temperatures above 0 °C reaches 15% of the annual sum. Heat units above tmp_base are then summed for days_mat days from that date.

The calculation works in both hemispheres. Giving the days of a variety (for example 90, 100, 110 or 120 days for corn) lets one database support several varieties. If days_mat is longer than the growing season at a site, the heat units of the whole season are used.

docs.title: Leaf area development
docs.text:
The optimal leaf area index follows a curve through two points, (frac_hu1, lai_max1) and (frac_hu2, lai_max2), where the first value is the fraction of heat units to maturity and the second the fraction of lai_pot:

\[f_{LAI} = \frac{f_{PHU}}{f_{PHU} + \exp(l_1 - l_2\,f_{PHU})}\]

\(l_1\) and \(l_2\) are set at the start of the run so that the curve passes through both points. The values of lai_pot in the standard database are for typical plant densities in rainfed agriculture. Drought-prone regions with low planting densities, or irrigated land with high densities, may need different values. Canopy height grows with the square root of \(f_{LAI}\) up to can_ht_max.

When plnt_pop1 and plnt_pop2 are given, a second curve through (plnt_pop1, frac_lai1) and (plnt_pop2, frac_lai2) limits lai_pot by plant population.

docs.title: Radiation use efficiency
docs.text:
When the co2 column of parameters.bsn is above 350 µL/L, radiation use efficiency is adjusted for CO2 along a curve through (330 µL/L, bm_e) and (co2_hi, bm_e_hi). Otherwise bm_e is used as given. Values for co2_hi and bm_e_hi are needed even when climate change is not simulated, and bm_e_hi should be larger than bm_e. A co2_hi of 330 is replaced by 660.

When the vapor pressure deficit is above 1 kPa, radiation use efficiency drops by ru_vpd for each kPa above 1, down to no less than 27% of bm_e. A value of 6 to 8 is a reasonable approximation for most plants, and 0 turns the adjustment off.

docs.title: Perennials and trees
docs.text:
The maximum leaf area index of a perennial grows with its age:

\[LAI_{max} = \mathrm{lai\_pot} \left(\frac{y}{\mathrm{yrs\_mat}}\right)^{\mathrm{bm\_tree\_acc}}\]

where \(y\) is the number of years since the plant was established (at least 1), and \(LAI_{max}\) is at most lai_pot. With bm_tree_acc = 0 the plant reaches lai_pot in its first year.

At the end of each year, if above-ground biomass \(B\) exceeds bm_tree_max (converted to kg/ha), the amount

\[D = (1 + \mathrm{bm\_dieoff})\,(B - 1000\,\mathrm{bm\_tree\_max})\]

dies and goes to the residue pools, with roots in the same proportion. Nothing dies if \(D\) is not smaller than \(B\). A mature forest stand typically has 30 to 50 t/ha of biomass. bm_dieoff is not used at the start of dormancy in 62.0.1.

docs.title: Nutrient uptake
docs.text: The six fractions frac_n_em to frac_p_mat describe the nitrogen and phosphorus content of the whole plant, roots included, on a dry weight basis, at emergence, at 50% maturity and at maturity. They set the plant's nutrient demand through the season. Each fraction must be smaller than the one before it: if frac_n_50 is not at least 0.0001 below frac_n_em, it is set to frac_n_em − 0.0001, and if frac_n_mat is not at least 0.0001 below frac_n_50, it is multiplied by 0.75. The phosphorus fractions are treated the same way.

docs.title: Residue lignin
docs.text: With carbon = 2 in codes.bsn, residue entering the soil is split into metabolic, structural and lignin pools. Below ground, the lignin fraction is bg_lig_frac, the structural fraction is bg_lig_frac / 0.8, and the rest is metabolic. Above ground the same split uses ab_lig_frac. With carbon = 0 these columns are not used.

docs.title: Values set by the model
docs.text:
After the file is read, SWAT+ changes some values:

Column Change harv_idx Values above 0.7 are set to 0.02. lai_pot Limited to 0 to 10. usle_c_min Limited to 0.001 to 1. plnt_decomp 0 is replaced by rsd_decomp of parameters.bsn. yrs_mat Values below 1 are set to 1. ext_co 0 is replaced by 0.65. bm_dieoff 0 is replaced by 1. rt_st_beg, rt_st_end 0 is replaced by 0.4 and 0.2. Tuber types get rt_st_end = 0.7. aeration, rsd_pctcov, rsd_covfac 0 is replaced by 0.2, 0.4 and 0.04. co2_hi 330 is replaced by 660. frac_n_50, frac_n_mat, frac_p_50, frac_p_mat Adjusted to decrease, as described above.

The harv_idx change affects crops whose harvest index is above 0.7, such as alfalfa (0.9 in the standard database) and tuber crops with a harvest index above 1. Their harvest index becomes 0.02.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text: These parameters can be changed during calibration through calibration.cal: bio_e (bm_e), hvsti (harv_idx), rdmx (rt_dp_max), t_opt (tmp_opt), t_base (tmp_base) and usle_c (usle_c_min).

  • Weather generator: monthly temperatures used for heat units to maturity.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
print.prt controls the output of a SWAT+ run. It sets the number of warm-up years left out of the outputs, the period and spacing of daily output, the extra output formats, a few special output files, and one row per output group with switches for daily, monthly, yearly and average annual files. The file is named in slot 2 of the simulation line of file.cio (default print.prt).

If the name in file.cio is null, SWAT+ uses the built-in values: no warm-up, every output group off, and crop yields written as average annual values only. A name that does not exist in the run folder has the same effect, and SWAT+ creates an empty file of that name. The files listed in Output naming convention are written in every case.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. The file has four short blocks, each a header line followed by a line of values, then a header line and one row per output group. Line 1 is a title. All header lines are skipped, and values are read by position within each line.

Line Content 1 title 2 header 3 nyskip, day_start, yrc_start, day_end, yrc_end, interval 4 header 5 aa_int_cnt, followed by aa_int_cnt end years 6 header 7 csvout, use_obj_lbls, cdfout 8 header 9 crop_yld, mgtout, hydcon, fdcout 10 header (objects daily monthly yearly avann) 11 and on output group rows

docs.title: Print period (line 3)
docs.text:
# Column Units Default Description 1 nyskip years 0 Number of years at the start of the simulation left out of all outputs (warm-up period). 2 day_start day of year 1 Day of the year on which daily output starts. 0 means 1. 3 yrc_start year first simulated year Year in which daily output starts. 0 means the first year in time.sim. 4 day_end day of year 366 Day of the year on which daily output ends. 0 means 366, the end of the year. 5 yrc_end year after the last simulated year Year in which daily output ends. 0 means daily output runs to the end of the simulation. 6 interval days 1 Days between daily output rows. 0 or less means 1. With 2, every other day is written.

A warm-up period lets soil water, nutrient pools and plant cover settle from their initial values before results are used. It matters more for short simulations; for a simulation of five years or less, a warm-up period is recommended.

docs.title: Average annual intervals (line 5)
docs.text:
# Column Units Default Description 1 aa_int_cnt count 0 Number of average annual print intervals. When it is above 0, the end year of each interval follows on the same line, in order.

For example, 3 1995 2005 2015 would end intervals in 1995, 2005 and 2015. In 62.0.1 the end years are read but have no effect on the outputs: every average annual file covers the whole printed period. See Average annual values.

docs.title: Output formats (line 7)
docs.text:
# Column Values Default Description 1 csvout y, n n y also writes a comma-separated .csv copy of most output files. 2 use_obj_lbls y, n n How the output group rows are read: y by name, n by position. See Output group rows. 3 cdfout y, n n netCDF output. Read and not used.

print.prt files written by older versions of the SWAT+ Editor have the header csvout dbout cdfout on line 6. SWAT+ reads the second value as use_obj_lbls whatever the header says, so an old file with n there is read by position.

docs.title: Special outputs (line 9)
docs.text:
# Column Values Default Description 1 crop_yld a, y, b, n a Crop yield files: a average annual (crop_yld_aa), y yearly (crop_yld_yr and the basin crop yield files), b both, n none. 2 mgtout y, n n y writes mgt_out.txt, the log of management operations, decision table actions and water allocation deliveries. 3 hydcon y, n n y writes hydcon.out, the list of hydrograph connections between objects. It is mostly useful for finding connection errors. 4 fdcout y, n n y computes flow duration curves and a flashiness index for SWAT+ channels and writes them to flow_duration_curve.out.

Older Editor versions write the header soilout in place of crop_yld; the value is read as crop_yld.

docs.title: Output group rows
docs.text:
Each row from line 11 on has a group name and four switches, for the daily, monthly, yearly and average annual files of that group. A switch of y opens the file for that interval and any other value leaves it off. The legacy carbon rows hru_cb and hru_cb_vars also accept l. The files each row opens, and the pages that describe them, are listed in Output naming convention.

How the rows are read depends on use_obj_lbls on line 7:

  • use_obj_lbls = y: each row is matched by its name, so rows can be in any order and rows can be left out. A row that is left out has all four switches off. A name SWAT+ does not know stops the run with Error: The output object <name> in the input file print.prt is not a valid object, and a name that appears twice stops it with print object is duplicated. Names are case-sensitive.
  • use_obj_lbls = n: the rows are read in the fixed order of the table below, and the names in the first column are not checked. A missing row or an extra row shifts every later row, so its switches are applied to the wrong output group, with no message. Rows after the end of the file are off. The carbon and gwflow rows cannot be set in this mode.

See Legacy CSU carbon outputs. gwflow_wb, gwflow_flux, gwflow_heat, gwflow_solute, gwflow_obs, gwflow_pump gwflow output. A row that is present replaces the setting from the gwflow input files; a row that is absent leaves it. See gwflow output switches.

Some rows write data only when the project has the matching objects. The channel_sd and basin_sd_cha files need SWAT+ channels, and the channel and basin_cha files need legacy channels. The basin landscape files (basin_wb, basin_nb, basin_ls, basin_pw) are summed from the landscape unit element file ls_unit.ele, and the landscape unit files need ls_unit.def; both are named on the regions line of file.cio.

docs.title: Print timing
docs.text:
Every output file leaves out the first nyskip years of the simulation. After those years:

  • Daily rows are written from day_start of yrc_start until day_end of yrc_end, every interval days, starting with the first day of the window. Output starts on the first simulated day whose day of the year is at least day_start in a year at or after yrc_start. If the simulation starts in a later year than yrc_start, daily output therefore starts on day day_start of the first simulated year. Days before it in that year are not written.
  • Monthly rows are written at the end of each month, yearly rows at the end of each year, and average annual rows once, at the end of the simulation.

The print window applies to daily rows only. Monthly, yearly and average annual files always cover all years after the warm-up.

docs.title: Average annual values
docs.text:
The average annual files give the sum over the printed period divided by the number of printed years \(Y\). SWAT+ counts the printed days \(D\) (all days after the warm-up) and divides by 365:

\[Y = \frac{D}{365}\]

Leap days are counted in \(D\), so \(Y\) is slightly larger than the number of calendar years. When nyskip is above 0, 62.0.1 starts the count at the number of simulated years \(N_{yr}\) instead of 0:

\[Y = \frac{D + N_{yr}}{365}\]

For a 10-year simulation with 2 warm-up years, \(Y\) is about 8.03 instead of 8.00, and the average annual values are about 0.3% lower than the true averages over the printed years. If nyskip is equal to or larger than the number of simulated years, no output is written.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
refdata/Ames_sub1/print.prt in the SWAT+ repository:

print.prt: 
nyskip      day_start  yrc_start  day_end   yrc_end   interval  
0           0               1975         0     2020         1         
aa_int_cnt  
0           
csvout        use_obj_lbls  cdfout        
n             y             n             
crop_yld      mgtout        hydcon        fdcout        
b             y             n             n             
objects                  daily       monthly        yearly         avann
hru_wb                       y             n             n             y  
hru_nb                       y             n             n             y  
hru_ls                       n             n             n             y  
hru_pw                       y             n             n             y  
hru_cb                       l             y             y             y  
hru_cb_vars                  l             y             y             y

There is no warm-up period. Daily output covers the whole simulation (1975 to 2020) at an interval of one day. There is no .csv output. Crop yields are written both yearly and as average annual values, and the management log mgt_out.txt is written.

use_obj_lbls = y, so the rows are read by name and every row not listed is off. The HRU water balance, nutrient balance, and plant and weather files are written daily and as average annual values; the HRU losses only as average annual values. The hru_cb and hru_cb_vars rows switch on the legacy carbon files, with l in the daily column for the full set of layer diagnostics. The hru_cb_vars files are written only when the carbon model is on (carbon = 2 in codes.bsn).

refdata/Osu_1hru/print.prt, written by an older SWAT+ Editor, has dbout in place of use_obj_lbls with the value n, so its rows are read by position. Its list has an hru_cb row after hru_pw, which is not part of the fixed order: the reader applies that row to hru-lte_wb and every later row moves down one group. All rows in that file have the same switches (n n n y), so the shift has no visible effect there.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
SWAT+ can follow pathogens (bacteria and other microorganisms) listed in constituents.cs. Three files describe them:

File Named in Content pathogens.pth hru_parm_db line of file.cio (default pathogens.pth) Die-off, growth and transport properties of each pathogen. path_hru.ini init line of file.cio Initial pathogens in soils and on plants. path_water.ini init line of file.cio Initial pathogens in channels, reservoirs and aquifers.

Every pathogen named in constituents.cs should have a row in pathogens.pth with the same name.

The pathogen code in 62.0.1 does not yet work as a complete model. Several columns are read but not used, and the landscape and channel routines have the limitations listed in Behaviour in 62.0.1. Read that section before using pathogen results.

docs.title: pathogens.pth
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one pathogen with the 18 values below in this order. The reader does not match columns by header name.

# Column Units Used in 62.0.1 Description 1 name - yes Pathogen name, up to 16 characters. 2 do_soln 1/day yes Die-off factor in soil solution at 20 °C. 3 gr_soln 1/day yes Growth factor in soil solution at 20 °C. 4 do_sorb 1/day no Die-off factor for pathogens sorbed to soil particles at 20 °C. 5 gr_sorb 1/day no Growth factor for pathogens sorbed to soil particles at 20 °C. 6 kd - yes Partition coefficient between solution and sorbed phases. 7 t_adj - yes Temperature adjustment factor for die-off and growth. 8 washoff fraction yes Fraction of the pathogens on foliage washed off by a rainfall event. 9 do_plnt 1/day yes Die-off factor on foliage at 20 °C. 10 gr_plnt 1/day yes Growth factor on foliage at 20 °C. 11 fr_manure fraction no Fraction of manure containing active colony forming units. 12 perco - yes Percolation coefficient: ratio of the concentration in percolate to the concentration in the surface layer solution. 13 det_thrshd cfu/m² no Detection threshold below which soil pathogens would be set to zero. 14 do_stream 1/day yes Die-off factor in streams at 20 °C. 15 gr_stream 1/day no Growth factor in streams at 20 °C. 16 do_res 1/day no Die-off factor in reservoirs at 20 °C. 17 gr_res 1/day no Growth factor in reservoirs at 20 °C. 18 conc_min cfu/m² yes Minimum pathogen level on foliage and in the soil surface layer.

docs.title: Die-off and growth
docs.text:
On foliage and in the top soil layer the pathogen count \(N\) changes each day by the net die-off rate, adjusted for the mean air temperature \(T\):

\[N_d = N_{d-1}\,\exp\!\left(-(k_{die} - k_{grow})\,\theta^{\,T - 20}\right) - c_{min}\]

where \(k_{die}\) and \(k_{grow}\) are do_plnt and gr_plnt on foliage, or do_soln and gr_soln in the soil, \(\theta\) is t_adj and \(c_{min}\) is conc_min. The result is not allowed to fall below conc_min.

On a day with at least 2.54 mm of precipitation, washoff of the pathogens on each plant's foliage moves to the top soil layer.

docs.title: path_hru.ini
docs.text:
Initial pathogens in the soil and on plants of HRUs. An HRU selects a record by name in the path column of soil_plant.ini.

Line 1 is a title. Each record has a header line, a name line, and then the values as one list: a label, the soil value of each pathogen, then the plant value of each pathogen, in the order of constituents.cs. Line breaks within the list are free, but the list must take one line per pathogen so that the records are counted correctly. For two pathogens:

path_hru.ini: initial pathogens
name
hru_init
ecoli  1000.  500.
50.  10.

Here ecoli is the label, the soil values are 1000 and 500 and the plant values 50 and 10.

Value Units Description soil cfu/m² Pathogens in the top soil layer. plant cfu/m² Pathogens on the foliage.

docs.title: path_water.ini
docs.text:
Initial pathogens in channels, reservoirs and aquifers. Reservoirs and channels select a record by name in their initial condition files (initial.res, initial.cha), and aquifers in initial.aqu.

Line 1 is a title and line 2 a header. The record has a name line and then the values as one list: a label, the water value of each pathogen, then the bed sediment value of each pathogen. The list must take two lines per pathogen. Use one record (see below).

Value Units Description water - Pathogens in the water. The value is used as given, without conversion, so give it in the units of the pathogen loads in the model. benthic - Pathogens in the bed sediment, used as given.

docs.title: Behaviour in 62.0.1
docs.text:
• Columns do_sorb, gr_sorb, fr_manure, det_thrshd, gr_stream, do_res and gr_res are not used.
  • The landscape routines (die-off, wash-off, runoff and percolation) do not look up each pathogen's row by name. They use the row of pathogens.pth whose position equals the position of the HRU's record in path_hru.ini, and use that one row for every pathogen.
  • Each day the runoff step removes all pathogens left in the top soil layer after percolation and reports them as lost in surface runoff, whether or not there is runoff that day.
  • Initial soil pathogens from path_hru.ini are set to zero again for any soil with more than one layer. Initial plant pathogens are written to the balance output but not put on the foliage.
  • path_water.ini is read with a header line before each record in the reading pass and without one in the counting pass, so only a file with one record is read correctly.
  • Channels take their initial pathogens from the path_water.ini record in the position of the channel's pesticide initial record, not its pathogen record. Aquifers take the name match from path_water.ini but the values from the path_hru.ini soil column of the record in the same position. Reservoirs use their path_water.ini record.
  • The channel die-off step does not identify the channel being routed, so do_stream does not act on the routed water.
