docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
snow.sno is the snow parameter database. Each row is a named set of parameters for snowfall, snowpack temperature, snowmelt and snow cover. An HRU picks a row by name in the snow column of hru-data.hru. The file is named on the hru_parm_db line of file.cio (default snow.sno).

If hru-data.hru gives null for an HRU's snow entry, or a name that is not in snow.sno, the HRU uses the first row of snow.sno. No message is written in either case. A model therefore needs a snow.sno file with at least one row: if the file is missing or named null in file.cio, every HRU refers to a first row that does not exist.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one parameter set with nine values in the order below. The reader does not match columns by header name, so all nine values must be present and in this order.

# Column Units Typical range Description 1 name - - Name of the snow parameter set, matched against the snow column of hru-data.hru. 2 fall_tmp °C -5 to 5 Snowfall temperature. On a day when the mean air temperature is at or below fall_tmp, all precipitation falls as snow and is added to the snowpack. 3 melt_tmp °C -5 to 5 Snowmelt base temperature. Melt occurs only on days when the maximum air temperature is above melt_tmp. 4 melt_max mm H₂O/°C/day 0 to 10 Melt factor on 21 June (day 172). 5 melt_min mm H₂O/°C/day 0 to 10 Melt factor on 21 December (day 355). 6 tmp_lag - 0.01 to 1 Snowpack temperature lag factor. See Snowpack temperature for how 62.0.1 uses it. 7 snow_h2o mm H₂O 0 to 500 Snow water content at and above which the HRU is fully covered by snow. 8 cov50 fraction 0.05 to 0.95 Fraction of snow_h2o at which 50% of the HRU is covered by snow. 9 snow_init mm H₂O 0 and up Snow water content at the start of the simulation.

docs.title: Snow processes
docs.text: All snow calculations run daily for each HRU, after canopy interception.

docs.title: Snowfall
docs.text: If the mean air temperature \(\bar{T}\) is at or below fall_tmp, the day's precipitation (after canopy interception) is added to the snowpack and no rain reaches the ground. In sub-daily runs the rainfall for every time step of that day is set to zero.

docs.title: Snowpack temperature
docs.text:
The intended snowpack temperature keeps part of the previous day's value:

\[T_{snow,d} = T_{snow,d-1}\,(1 - \ell) + \bar{T}_d\,\ell\]

where \(\ell\) is tmp_lag. Values near 1 give the current day's air temperature most of the weight. Values near 0 make the snowpack respond slowly.

In 62.0.1 the previous day's snowpack temperature is reset to zero at the start of each day, so the calculation reduces to

\[T_{snow,d} = \ell\,\bar{T}_d\]

and tmp_lag acts as a scaling factor on the day's mean air temperature. It has no lag effect.

docs.title: Melt factor
docs.text:
The melt factor \(b_{mlt}\) varies through the year between melt_min and melt_max, which accounts for the effect of snowpack density on melt:

\[b_{mlt} = \frac{\mathrm{melt\_max} + \mathrm{melt\_min}}{2} + \frac{\mathrm{melt\_max} - \mathrm{melt\_min}}{2}\,\sin\!\left(\frac{2\pi}{365}\,(d - 81)\right)\]

where \(d\) is the day of the year. The factor equals melt_max on day 172 and melt_min on day 355 for every HRU. SWAT+ 62.0.1 does not swap the two for the Southern Hemisphere, so a model there should give the winter (June) factor in melt_max and the summer (December) factor in melt_min.

In rural areas the melt factor ranges from 1.4 to 6.9 mm H₂O/°C/day (Huber and Dickinson, 1988). Urban values tend to the high end because traffic compresses the snowpack: urban studies in Sweden reported 3.0 to 8.0 mm H₂O/°C/day (Bengston, 1981; Westerstrom, 1981), and snow on asphalt gave 1.7 to 6.5 mm H₂O/°C/day (Westerstrom, 1984).

docs.title: Snow cover
docs.text:
Drifting, shading and topography mean that snow rarely covers an HRU evenly. SWAT+ describes the covered fraction with an areal depletion curve. With \(r = SNO / \mathrm{snow\_h2o}\), the ratio of the current snow water content to snow_h2o,

\[sno_{cov} = \frac{r}{r + \exp(c_1 - c_2\,r)} \quad \text{for } r < 1, \qquad sno_{cov} = 1 \quad \text{for } r \ge 1\]

The shape coefficients \(c_1\) and \(c_2\) are set once at the start of the run so that the curve passes through 50% cover at \(r = \text{cov50}\) and 95% cover at \(r = 0.95\). cov50 must therefore lie between 0 and 0.95.

The depletion curve affects melt only while the snow water content is between 0 and snow_h2o. A small snow_h2o makes its effect on melt minor; a large one makes it more important.

docs.title: Snowmelt
docs.text:
When the maximum air temperature \(T_{max}\) is above melt_tmp and there is snow on the ground, melt is

\[SNO_{mlt} = b_{mlt}\; sno_{cov} \left(\frac{T_{snow} + T_{max}}{2} - \mathrm{melt\_tmp}\right)\]

limited to between zero and the snow water content. Melt water is added to the day's water input at the surface, together with any rain. In sub-daily runs it is spread evenly over the day's time steps.

docs.title: Calibration and decision tables
docs.text:
Five of the parameters can be changed during calibration through calibration.cal, using these parameter names: snofall_tmp (fall_tmp), snomelt_tmp (melt_tmp), snomelt_max (melt_max), snomelt_min (melt_min) and snomelt_lag (tmp_lag). snow_h2o, cov50 and snow_init have no calibration parameter. See parameter change files.

A decision table action snow_change switches an HRU to another snow.sno row during the run and logs the change to lu_change_out.txt. The snow cover curve is not recalculated after the switch, so it keeps the shape from the HRU's original cov50.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
refdata/Ames_sub1/snow.sno in the SWAT+ repository:

snow.sno: written by SWAT+ editor v2.3.3 on 2023-10-25 08:58 for SWAT+ rev.60.5.7
name                  fall_tmp      melt_tmp      melt_max      melt_min       tmp_lag      snow_h2o         cov50     snow_init
snow001                1.00000       0.50000       4.50000       4.50000       1.00000       1.00000       0.50000       0.00000

One parameter set named snow001. melt_max and melt_min are both 4.5, so the melt factor is constant through the year. With tmp_lag at 1.0 the snowpack temperature equals the day's mean air temperature, and with snow_h2o at 1 mm the HRU is fully covered by any snowpack of 1 mm or more.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
soils.sol defines every soil used in the watershed. Each soil is a block of lines: one profile line with the soil name, number of layers, hydrologic soil group and other whole-profile values, followed by one line per layer with depth, bulk density, available water capacity, saturated hydraulic conductivity, organic carbon, texture and other layer properties. An HRU picks a soil by name in the soil column of hru-data.hru. The file is named first on the soils line of file.cio (default soils.sol).

Every HRU should name a soil that is in the file. An unknown name is not reported: the HRU silently gets the first soil in soils.sol. Check the sname column of checker.out, which lists the soil each HRU uses.

The initial nutrient and carbon contents of the soil come from nutrients.sol, which an HRU selects through soil_plant.ini. The same soils line of file.cio names nutrients.sol second and soils_lte.sol third (see soils_lte.sol below).

docs.title: Format
docs.text: Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each soil then takes nly + 1 lines: the profile line and nly layer lines. The reader counts soils by reading each profile line and skipping the next nly lines, so nly must equal the number of layer lines that follow. Columns are read by position; the header names are not checked. Spacing is not significant, so the wide indentation the SWAT+ Editor gives the layer lines has no meaning.

docs.title: Profile line
docs.text: # Column Units Used if zero or out of range Description 1 name - - Soil name, up to 20 characters, matched against the soil column of hru-data.hru. 2 nly - - Number of layer lines that follow. There is no upper limit in the model. 3 hyd_grp - - Hydrologic soil group: A, B, C or D. It selects the curve number from cntable.lum and the conductivity used when soil_k is zero. Dual groups such as A/D and lower-case letters are not recognized. 4 dp_tot mm - Maximum rooting depth. See Rooting depth for how 62.0.1 uses it. 5 anion_excl fraction 0.5 if 0; 0.99 if 1 or more Fraction of porosity from which anions are excluded. 6 perc_crk fraction - Potential (maximum) crack volume of the soil profile as a fraction of total soil volume. Used only when crack flow is switched on (crack = 1 in codes.bsn). 7 texture - - Texture label, up to 16 characters. Only the first whitespace-delimited word is read, so L-L-L-L is read whole but L- L- L- L is read as L-. The label is not used in any process; it can serve as a condition in calibration.cal (condition texture).

docs.title: Layer lines
docs.text:
Layers are listed from the surface down. Each line has fourteen values.

# Column Units Used if zero or out of range Description 1 dp mm - Depth from the soil surface to the bottom of the layer. 2 bd Mg/m³ 1.3 if 0; capped at 2.0 Moist bulk density: oven-dry mass divided by the soil volume at or near field capacity. 3 awc mm H₂O/mm soil 0.005 if 0; capped at 0.8 Available water capacity: water held between field capacity (-0.033 MPa) and permanent wilting point (-1.5 MPa). 4 soil_k mm/h by hyd_grp if 0 or less: A 50, B 20, C 5, D 2, other 10 Saturated hydraulic conductivity. 5 carbon % of soil mass 0.001 if below 0.001 Organic carbon content of the fine earth (material passing a 2 mm sieve). 6 clay % - Clay, particles below 0.002 mm. 7 silt % - Silt, particles between 0.002 and 0.05 mm. 8 sand % - Sand, particles between 0.05 and 2.0 mm. 9 rock % of total mass capped at 98 Rock fragments, particles above 2 mm. 10 alb fraction - Moist soil albedo. Only the top layer value is used. 11 usle_k 0.013 t m² h/(m³ t cm) - USLE soil erodibility factor. Only the top layer value is used. 12 ec dS/m - Electrical conductivity. Read and reported, but not used by any process in 62.0.1. 13 caco3 % 2.8 if 0 Calcium carbonate content. 14 ph - 6.5 if 0 Soil pH. Read and reported, but not used by any process in 62.0.1.

clay, silt and sand are percentages of the mineral fraction and should add up to 100. The model does not check this, except that in sub-daily runs the sand content of the top layer is reset to \(100 - \mathrm{clay} - \mathrm{silt}\).

docs.title: Thin first layer
docs.text: After reading a soil, the reader checks the first layer. If it is shallower than 20 mm and the soil has only one layer, or the second layer reaches deeper than 20 mm, the bottom of the first layer is set to 20 mm.

docs.title: Added 10 mm surface layer
docs.text:
Without a soil_lyr_depths.sol file in the run folder (the usual case), SWAT+ adds a 10 mm surface layer to every soil whose first layer is deeper than 19.5 mm. The new layer takes all its properties from the first input layer, so a soil with four input layers is simulated with five. The first input layer then runs from 10 mm to its listed depth. Outputs by layer count this added layer.

If the first layer is 19.5 mm or shallower (possible only when the second layer is also within 20 mm), no layer is added and the first layer is given a depth of 10 mm.

docs.title: soil_lyr_depths.sol
docs.text:
If a file named soil_lyr_depths.sol is in the run folder, every soil is re-layered to the depths it lists. The file is not named in file.cio; SWAT+ looks for this name.

  • Line 1 is a title, line 2 a header and line 3 a units label; all three are skipped.
  • Each later line gives one depth in mm, from the surface down, as a whole number.
  • Depths of 10 mm or less are skipped. The first layer is always 0 to 10 mm.
  • A depth beyond the bottom of a soil is replaced by its total depth, and the list ends there for that soil. If the deepest listed depth is shallower than a soil, the profile is cut off at that depth.

Each new layer takes the depth-weighted average of the input layers it overlaps, computed millimetre by millimetre, for every layer property. refdata/Ames_sub1/soil_lyr_depths.sol lists 10, 25, 50, 100, 150, 200, 300, 450, 600, 750, 900, 1050, 1200, 1500, 1800 and 2100 mm, so a 2000 mm soil gets sixteen layers with the last from 1800 to 2000 mm.

docs.title: Septic biozone layer
docs.text: In an HRU with a septic system (the sep column of landuse.lum), the profile is split further so that the biozone set in septic.str is a separate layer.

docs.title: Derived layer properties
docs.text:
At the start of the run SWAT+ derives the water contents of each layer from bd, awc and clay. As volume fractions:

\[\theta_{wp} = 0.40\,\frac{c\,\rho_b}{100}, \qquad \theta_{fc} = \theta_{wp} + AWC, \qquad \phi = 1 - \frac{\rho_b}{2.65}\]

where \(c\) is clay (%), \(\rho_b\) is bd and \(AWC\) is awc. If \(\theta_{wp}\) is zero (no clay) it is set to 0.005. If \(\theta_{fc}\) reaches the porosity \(\phi\), field capacity is set to \(\phi - 0.05\) and the wilting point to \(\theta_{fc} - AWC\); if that is not positive, field capacity becomes \(0.75\,\phi\) and the wilting point \(0.25\,\phi\).

For a layer of thickness \(h\) (mm), the plant-available water at field capacity is \(FC = h\,(\theta_{fc} - \theta_{wp})\), the water between wilting point and saturation is \(UL = h\,(\phi - \theta_{wp})\), and the percolation travel time (h) is

\[TT_{perc} = \frac{UL - FC}{K_{sat}}\]

with a minimum of 1 hour, where \(K_{sat}\) is soil_k. The profile sums of \(FC\) and \(UL\) are reported as sumfc and sumul in checker.out.

The crack volume of each layer is

\[V_{crk} = \mathrm{perc\_crk} \times 0.916\,e^{-0.0012\,z}\,h\]

where \(z\) is the depth to the bottom of the layer (mm).

The top layer's sand, silt and clay set the particle-size make-up of eroded sediment (sand, silt, clay, small and large aggregates). For the Green and Ampt infiltration method, the wetting front suction head is estimated from the porosity, clay and sand of the top layer.

docs.title: Initial soil water
docs.text:
Each layer starts at a fraction of its field capacity water. The fraction is sw_init in parameters.bsn. If sw_init is zero, it is estimated from the average annual precipitation \(P\) (mm) of the HRU's weather generator:

\[f = \frac{P}{P + \exp(9.043 - 0.002135\,P)}\]

The sw_frac column of soil_plant.ini is read but not used for this in 62.0.1.

docs.title: Rooting depth
docs.text: dp_tot limits root depth only while plants that start the run already growing are initialized. After that the model sets the HRU's maximum rooting depth to the bottom of the soil profile. Each planting operation then lowers it to the smaller of its current value and the plant's maximum root depth in plants.plt. The value is never raised again during the run, so after a shallow-rooted crop is planted, later crops in the same HRU are limited to that depth as well. The zmx column of checker.out shows this profile depth. It does not show dp_tot.

docs.title: Runoff, percolation and solute leaching
docs.text:
hyd_grp picks one of the four curve numbers in cntable.lum for the HRU's land use. anion_excl reduces the pore volume available to nitrate, salts and other constituents moving down with percolating water. The nitrate that moves with a water volume \(w\) (mm) leaving a layer is

\[NO3_{mobile} = NO3_{ly}\left[1 - \exp\!\left(\frac{-w}{(1 - \mathrm{anion\_excl})\,UL}\right)\right]\]

See hydrology, soil water and temperature and nutrient cycling.

docs.title: Erosion
docs.text:
The MUSLE soil factor of an HRU uses the top layer only:

\[K \cdot CFRG = \mathrm{usle\_k}_1\; e^{-0.053\,\mathrm{rock}_1}\]

which is multiplied by the support practice factor from cons_practice.lum and the slope length and steepness factor. See erosion and sediment.

docs.title: Albedo
docs.text: On days with less than 0.5 mm of snow, the albedo of a bare HRU is the top layer alb. With plant cover it is \(0.23\,(1 - e) + \mathrm{alb}_1\,e\), where \(e = \exp(-5\times10^{-5}(CV + 0.1))\) and \(CV\) is above-ground biomass plus residue (kg/ha). There is no lower limit on alb, so a zero value gives zero albedo for bare soil.

docs.title: Carbon and nutrients
docs.text:
carbon, bd and the layer thickness set the starting organic matter of each layer: the soil mass is \(10\,000\,h\,\rho_b\) kg/ha, organic carbon is carbon percent of that, and organic matter is carbon divided by 0.58. How this is split into pools depends on the carbon model (the carbon column of codes.bsn) and on nutrients.sol; see nutrients.sol. In 62.0.1 the 0.001% floor on carbon applies to every layer; earlier revisions applied it to the top layer only.

With the Vadas and White phosphorus model (soil_p = 1 in codes.bsn), clay and carbon set the initial phosphorus sorption coefficient and caco3 sets the rate of transfer between the active and stable mineral P pools:

\[k_{as} = 0.0023\,\mathrm{caco3} + 0.005, \qquad 0.002 \le k_{as} \le 0.05\]

caco3 is not used with the original phosphorus model.

docs.title: Calibration and conditions
docs.text:
Soil columns can be changed in calibration.cal with these parameter names, for a range of layers: anion_excl, crk (perc_crk), z (dp), bd, awc, k (soil_k), cbn (carbon), clay, silt, sand, rock, alb, usle_k, ec, cal (caco3) and ph. Changes to z, bd, awc and clay recompute the layer water contents and the curve number coefficients. See parameter change files.

Calibration changes are applied before the soil organic pools are set up, and that setup works from the carbon column. A cbn change acts on the layer's organic carbon pool, so it is replaced when the pools are initialized and has no lasting effect in 62.0.1.

The calibration.cal conditions hsg and texture select HRUs by hyd_grp and texture. Decision tables can test hyd_soil_group and k_factor (the top layer usle_k).

docs.title: soils_lte.sol
docs.text:
soils_lte.sol is used only by HRU-LTE objects (hru-lte.hru), which select a soil texture by name instead of a layered profile. Line 1 is a title and line 2 a header. The next twelve lines are read, one per texture class, each with four values:

# Column Units Description 1 texture - Texture class name, matched against the soil texture column of hru-lte.hru. 2 awc mm/mm Available water capacity, multiplied by the soil depth given in hru-lte.hru. 3 por mm/mm Porosity, multiplied by the same soil depth. 4 scon mm/h Saturated hydraulic conductivity.

Twelve lines are always read. A project with HRU-LTE objects needs this file, since there is no built-in texture table.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Structural practices are field-scale conservation structures attached to a land use. Five files contain their parameter sets: tiledrain.str, septic.str, filterstrip.str, grassedww.str and bmpuser.str. They are named on the structural line of file.cio. Two databases on the hru_parm_db line belong with them: septic.sep (septic tank effluent quality) and urban.urb (urban land types). The saturated buffer file satbuffer.str is read from the run folder under that fixed name; it is not listed in file.cio.

Each record in a structural file has a name. A land use in landuse.lum points to records by name in its tile, sep, vfs, grww and bmp columns, and an urban land use points to urban.urb in its urban column. Every HRU that uses that land use gets the practice. Write null in a landuse.lum column for no practice. A name that is not found in the structural file is reported in diagnostics.out as <landuse> <name> not found (landuse-tiledr) (or landuse-septic, landuse-fstrip, landuse-grassww, landuse-bmpuser), and the HRU then gets no practice of that kind.

Practices can also be added during a run with the decision table actions tile_install, septic_install, fstrip_install, grassww_install, grassww_uninstall and user_def_bmp, which name a record in the matching file. See decision tables.

All files are optional. If a file is missing, or named null in file.cio, it is treated as empty.

docs.title: File layout
docs.text: All of these files share one layout. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is a column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one record, read as free-format values separated by spaces. The reader takes the values by position and ignores the header text, so every column must be present and in the order shown. Text after the last numeric column (the description column written by SWAT+ Editor) is ignored.

docs.title: tiledrain.str
docs.text:
Subsurface (tile) drain parameter sets, referenced from the tile column of landuse.lum.

# Column Units Typical range Description 1 name - - Name of the tile drain record. 2 dp mm 0 to 6000 Depth of the drain tube below the soil surface. 0 means no drain: the HRU produces no tile flow. 3 t_fc hours 0 to 100 Time to drain the soil to field capacity. Used only by the drawdown method (tiledrain = 0 in codes.bsn). 4 lag hours 0 to 100 Drain tile lag time. Tile flow is held in a lag store that releases a fraction \(1 - \exp(-24/\mathrm{lag})\) each day. 5 rad mm 3 to 40 Effective radius of the drains. DRAINMOD method only. 6 dist mm 5000 to 100000 Distance between two drain tubes or tiles. DRAINMOD method only. 7 drain mm/day 10 to 51 Drainage coefficient: the largest daily tile flow the drains can take. Used by both methods. 8 pump mm/hr 0 to 10 Pump capacity for subirrigation. DRAINMOD method only. 9 lat_ksat - 0.01 to 4 Multiplier on the saturated hydraulic conductivity of each soil layer (k in the soil file) to give its lateral conductivity. DRAINMOD method only.

docs.title: Tile flow methods
docs.text:
Tile flow is computed only when the HRU's land use names a tile drain record with dp greater than 0, the soil temperature of the second layer is above 0 °C and the shallow water table is above the drains. The tiledrain column of codes.bsn selects the method, and its wtable column selects how the water table depth is found.

With tiledrain = 0 (drawdown method), the water above field capacity drains at a rate set by t_fc:

\[q_{tile} = \frac{h_{wt} - h_d}{h_{wt}}\,(SW - FC)\,\left(1 - \exp\!\left(\frac{-24}{t_{fc}}\right)\right)\]

where \(h_{wt}\) is the height of the water table above the bottom of the soil profile, \(h_d\) is the height of the drains above the bottom of the profile (profile depth minus dp), \(SW\) is the soil water content and \(FC\) the water content at field capacity, all in mm. If \(t_{fc}\) is below 1 hour the exponential factor is left out. The result is limited to drain.

With tiledrain = 1 (DRAINMOD method), the drainage flux comes from the Hooghoudt and Kirkham equations used in DRAINMOD, which use rad, dist, lat_ksat, drain and pump. When the water table is below the drains the same equations give a subirrigation flux, limited by pump.

In both methods the day's tile flow then passes through the lag store described under lag. If lag is 0.01 hours or less, the release fraction is zero and tile water stays in the lag store for the rest of the run.

dist, rad and dp enter the DRAINMOD equations together with the soil depth, all in millimetres, so dist must be given in millimetres. The SWAT+ Editor default record (example below) has dist = 30, which the model reads as 30 mm.

docs.title: septic.str
docs.text:
On-site septic system parameter sets, adapted from Siegrist et al. (2005): system type, biozone geometry, biomass properties and reaction coefficients in the biozone. A record is meant to be referenced from the sep column of landuse.lum.

# Column Units Description 1 name - Name of the septic system record. 2 typ - Septic system type: the record number (row position, starting at 1) of the effluent type in septic.sep, given as an integer. 3 yr year Year the system starts operating. 0 means it operates from the start of the simulation. 4 operation - Operation flag: 0 not operating, 1 active, 2 failing. An active system becomes failing when the biozone clogs; a failing system returns to active after t_fail days. 5 residents - Number of permanent residents per house. A typical US value is 2.5. 6 area m² Average drainfield area of one septic system. About 40 to 70 m² per person is usual; 100 m² for a household of 2.5. 7 t_fail days Time until a failing system is fixed (0 to 150). 8 dp_bioz mm Depth to the top of the biozone layer from the ground surface. 9 thk_bioz mm Thickness of the biozone layer, the thin soil layer under the effluent distribution chamber where pollutants are degraded by live bacteria. 10 cha_dist km Distance from the septic system to the stream. 11 sep_dens per km² Number of septic systems per square kilometre. 12 bm_dens kg/m³ Density of biomass. 13 bod_decay m³/day BOD decay rate coefficient in the biozone. 14 bod_conv - Ratio of bacterial growth to BOD degraded in the septic tank effluent. 15 fc_lin - Linear coefficient for field capacity in the biozone. 16 fc_exp - Exponential coefficient for field capacity in the biozone. 17 fecal_decay m³/day Fecal coliform decay rate coefficient. 18 tds_conv - Conversion factor for plaque from total dissolved solids. 19 mort - Mortality rate coefficient. 20 resp - Respiration rate coefficient. 21 slough1 - Linear coefficient for the rate of biomass sloughing. 22 slough2 - Exponential coefficient for the rate of biomass sloughing. 23 nit - Nitrification rate coefficient. 24 denit - Denitrification rate coefficient. 25 p_sorp L/kg Linear P sorption distribution coefficient. 26 p_sorp_max mg P/kg soil Maximum P sorption capacity. 27 solp_slp - Slope of the linear effluent soluble P equation. 28 solp_int - Intercept of the linear effluent soluble P equation.

docs.title: Septic simulation in 62.0.1
docs.text:
In revision 62.0.1 septic systems run, but receive no effluent:

  • The sep column of landuse.lum assigns the named septic.str record to every HRU with that land use before the soil layers are set up. If operation is not 0, a biozone layer is added to the soil profile at dp_bioz with thickness thk_bioz, and from year yr the biozone routine runs on each day the biozone layer is above freezing. Unknown names are reported in diagnostics.out.
  • The daily septic tank effluent volume is never computed and stays at zero. No effluent water reaches the biozone, and the effluent concentrations in septic.sep, which are multiplied by that volume, add no nitrogen, phosphorus or BOD to the soil. The biozone routine works only on the water and nutrients already in the layer. residents, area, cha_dist, sep_dens and the q_rate column of septic.sep are read but not used.
  • The decision table action septic_install assigns a septic.str record to an HRU during the run. The biozone layer is placed only when the soils are set up at the start of the run, so an HRU that gets a septic system this way has no biozone layer.

docs.title: septic.sep
docs.text:
Septic tank effluent quality database. Each record describes the effluent of one type of on-site wastewater system (from Siegrist et al., 2005; McCray et al., 2005). A septic.str record selects a row by its position through typ.

# Column Units Description 1 name - Name of the effluent type (for example gcon, generic conventional system). 2 q_rate m³/capita/day Septic tank effluent flow rate per person. McCray et al. (2005) give 0.227 as the US median. Not used. 3 bod mg/L 7-day biological oxygen demand of the effluent. Typically 170 for a conventional system. 4 tss mg/L Total suspended solids in the effluent. Typically 75 for a conventional system. 5 nh4_n mg N/L Ammonium nitrogen in the effluent. Typically 60 (17 to 78) for a conventional system. 6 no3_n mg N/L Nitrate nitrogen in the effluent. 0 to 1.94 for a conventional system. 7 no2_n mg N/L Nitrite nitrogen in the effluent. Usually very low. 8 org_n mg N/L Organic nitrogen in the effluent. 9.4 to 15 for a conventional system. 9 min_p mg P/L Mineral phosphorus in the effluent. 10 org_p mg P/L Organic phosphorus in the effluent. Typically 1 for a conventional system. 11 fcoli cfu/100 mL Fecal coliform in the effluent. Typically 1E7 for a conventional system.

Values vary widely between system types; Table A-1 of Siegrist et al. (2005) lists them. The database distributed with SWAT+ Editor has 28 types, from generic conventional (gcon) and advanced (gadv) systems to sand filters, constructed wetlands, biofilters and textile filters.

docs.title: filterstrip.str
docs.text:
Vegetative filter strip parameter sets, referenced from the vfs column of landuse.lum. A filter strip is a strip of dense vegetation at the field edge that intercepts runoff from upslope. It slows overland flow so particles settle, and it infiltrates part of the runoff. The model follows White and Arnold (2009). It reduces sediment, organic N, nitrate, particulate and soluble P, and pesticides in surface runoff leaving the HRU. The runoff volume itself is not changed.

# Column Units Range used Description 1 name - - Name of the filter strip record. 2 flag - 0 or 1 On/off switch. The filter strip is simulated only when flag is greater than 0. 3 fld_vfs ratio above 0, up to 300 Ratio of field area to filter strip area. Values of 30 to 60 are most common. Values above 300 are set to 300. 4 con_vfs fraction 0.1 to 0.95 Fraction of the field runoff that enters the most concentrated 10% of the strip. Runoff is rarely spread evenly: 10% of the strip often receives 25 to 75% of the runoff. A value of 0 or less is replaced by 0.5; other values are kept between 0.1 and 0.95. 5 cha_q fraction 0 to 0.95 Fraction of the flow in the most concentrated 10% of the strip that is fully channelized. Channelized flow passes the strip without filtering or infiltration. Values above 0.95 are set to 0.95.

fld_vfs divides the field area to give the strip area, so it must be greater than 0 when the strip is switched on.

field_border             0       0.10000       0.00300       0.20000  Field_border
high_engineered          0       0.10000       0.00100       0.05000  Highly_engineered_low_channelized

Both records in this example have flag = 0, so a land use pointing to either one gets no filter strip.

docs.title: grassedww.str
docs.text:
Grassed waterway parameter sets, referenced from the grww column of landuse.lum. A grassed waterway is a broad, shallow vegetated channel that takes runoff away from a field. The vegetation slows the flow, which protects the channel from scour and lets sediment and attached pollutants settle. SWAT+ simulates it as a trapezoidal channel with 8:1 side slopes.

# Column Units Typical range Default used when 0 Description 1 name - - - Name of the grassed waterway record. 2 flag - - - Read but not used. The waterway is simulated whenever the land use names a record. 3 mann - 0.001 to 0.5 0.35 Manning's n of the waterway. 4 sed_co - 0 to 1 0.005 Sediment transport coefficient, used to compute the transport capacity of the waterway. 5 dp m 0 to 10 3/64 of wd Depth of the waterway. 6 wd m 0 to 1000 - Top width of the waterway. 7 len km 0 to 10000 square root of the HRU area Length of the waterway. 8 slp m/m 0 to 1 0.75 × HRU slope Slope of the waterway.

Values of 0 or less in mann, sed_co, dp, len and slp are replaced by the defaults shown. If dp and wd together cannot form a trapezoid with 8:1 side slopes (the bottom width would be zero or negative), dp is reset to 3/64 of wd.

docs.title: bmpuser.str
docs.text:
User-defined BMP removal efficiencies, referenced from the bmp column of landuse.lum. Many conservation practices are not modelled explicitly in SWAT+ but have published removal efficiencies. This record applies fixed reductions to the loads leaving the HRU. Surface runoff volume is not reduced, which keeps the water balance closed.

# Column Units Range Description 1 name - - Name of the user BMP record. 2 flag - - Read but not used. The BMP is applied whenever the land use names a record. 3 sed_eff fraction 0 to 1 Sediment removal. 4 ptlp_eff fraction 0 to 1 Particulate P removal (organic P and sorbed mineral P). 5 solp_eff fraction 0 to 1 Soluble P removal in surface runoff. 6 ptln_eff fraction 0 to 1 Particulate (organic) N removal. 7 soln_eff fraction 0 to 1 Soluble N removal: nitrate in surface runoff and in lateral flow. 8 bact_eff fraction 0 to 1 Bacteria removal. Read but not used.

Each load is multiplied by \((1 - \mathrm{eff})\), so the efficiencies are fractions: 0.2 removes 20%. A value of 20 would give a negative load.

docs.title: satbuffer.str
docs.text:
Saturated buffer links. A saturated buffer diverts part of the tile flow from a source HRU into the soil of a receiving (buffer) HRU. Each record links one source to one receiver. The file is read only if a file named satbuffer.str is present in the run folder.

# Column Units Description 1 name - Name of the buffer record. 2 hru_src - Number of the source HRU whose tile flow feeds the buffer. 3 frac_src fraction Fraction of the source HRU contributing tile flow to the buffer. 4 flocon_dtbl - Name of the flow control decision table (in the flow control decision table file) that sets how much tile flow goes into the buffer. 5 hru_rcv - Number of the receiving (buffer) HRU. 6 lyr - Soil layer of the receiving HRU that takes the diverted tile flow (0 = surface).

docs.title: urban.urb
docs.text:
Urban land type database, referenced from the urban column of landuse.lum. The urb_ro column of landuse.lum selects the urban load method: usgs_reg (USGS regression equations) or buildup_washoff (build-up and wash-off of solids from impervious surfaces).

# Column Units Built-in value Description 1 name - - Name of the urban land type. 2 frac_imp fraction 0.05 Fraction of the HRU area that is impervious. 3 frac_dc_imp fraction 0.05 Fraction of the HRU area that is directly connected impervious area. 4 curb_den km/ha 0 Curb length density. 5 urb_wash 1/mm 0 Wash-off coefficient for removal of constituents from impervious surfaces. 6 dirt_max kg/curb km 1000 Maximum amount of solids that can build up on impervious surfaces. 7 t_halfmax days 1 Time for solids on impervious surfaces to build up to half of dirt_max. 8 conc_totn mg N/kg sed 0 Total nitrogen concentration in suspended solids from impervious areas. 9 conc_totp mg P/kg sed 0 Total phosphorus concentration in suspended solids from impervious areas. 10 conc_no3n mg N/kg sed 0 Nitrate nitrogen concentration in suspended solids from impervious areas. 11 urb_cn - 98 Curve number for impervious areas (moisture condition II). Read but not used: 62.0.1 uses a fixed curve number of 98 for impervious areas.

With the curve number method, surface runoff from an urban HRU is a weighted mix of runoff from the pervious part (the HRU's daily curve number) and from the directly connected impervious part (curve number 98), with frac_dc_imp as the weight. frac_imp is the weight for urban sediment and nutrient loads in both urban load methods.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
.tem is an older extension for temperature data files, used by some data sets and preprocessing tools. SWAT+ opens a temperature file by the name given in tmp.cli and does not look at the extension, so a .tem file is read in the same way as a .tmp file. SWAT+ Editor writes .tmp.

The name has to be the same, extension included, in two places:

  • a line of tmp.cli, which tells SWAT+ to read the file, and
  • the tmp column of weather-sta.cli, which assigns it to a weather station.

If the tmp column names a file that is not listed in tmp.cli, SWAT+ writes <name> file not found (tgage) to diagnostics.out and generates the temperatures of that station for the whole run.

docs.title: Format
docs.text: The format is that of a .tmp file: a title line, a header line, a gauge line with nbyr, tstep, lat, lon and elev, and one record per day with year, day of year, maximum and minimum temperature in °C. Values of -97 or less mark missing data.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
refdata/Ames_sub1/ames.tem in the SWAT+ repository:

AME.Tmp
 NBYR    TSTEP      LAT     LONG     ELEV
   121        0    42.04   -93.89   316
1900    1   -99 -99
1900    2   -99 -99
...
1975    1   4.4 -7.2
1975    2   5   -7.8
...
2020    365 -1.7    -7.8
2020    366 -2.8    -8.9

A daily record of 121 years, 1900 to 2020, separated by tabs, which free-format reading accepts. In this data set the tmp column of weather-sta.cli names ames.tem, while tmp.cli lists ames.tmp, which is an empty file. SWAT+ therefore does not find ames.tem, never reads it, and generates the temperatures of the Ames run. Listing ames.tem in tmp.cli instead of ames.tmp makes the run use the measured record.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
tillage.til is the tillage database. Each row describes one tillage implement or operation: how much of the soil it mixes and how deep. A till operation in management.sch, a till or tillage action in a decision table, and a puddling operation all name a row of this file.

One row has a special role. A row named biomix sets the biological mixing efficiency and depth used by the dynamic carbon model (see Biological mixing).

The file is named on the hru_parm_db line of file.cio (default tillage.til). If the file is missing or named null, the database is empty and tillage operations find no row.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one operation with the values below in this order. The reader does not match columns by header name. It reads the first six values and ignores the rest of the line, so the description column written by the SWAT+ Editor has no effect.

# Column Units Default Typical range Description 1 name - - - Name of the tillage operation, up to 16 characters. Management schedules and decision tables refer to the operation by this name, so names must be unique. The name biomix is reserved for biological mixing. 2 mix_eff fraction 0.0 0.0 to 1.0 Mixing efficiency. The fraction of the soil, residue, nutrients and other constituents in each layer within the mixing depth that is mixed uniformly over that depth. The rest stays in its original layer. 3 mix_dp mm 0.0 0 to 750 Depth of mixing caused by the operation. 4 rough mm 0.0 - Random roughness. Read but not used. 5 ridge_ht mm 0.0 - Ridge height. Read but not used. 6 ridge_sp mm 0.0 - Ridge interval or row spacing. Read but not used.

docs.title: Tillage mixing
docs.text:
On the day of a tillage operation SWAT+ takes mix_eff and mix_dp from the named row. For each soil layer whose bottom is within mix_dp, the fraction mix_eff of the layer's mass is mixed. A layer that straddles mix_dp contributes in proportion to the part of it above the mixing depth. The mixed material is then spread over the mixing depth in proportion to layer thickness. Soil water, texture, mineral and organic nutrient pools, residue and constituents are all mixed this way.

A mixing depth greater than 0 and less than 10 mm is raised to 11 mm. A row with mix_dp of 0 mixes nothing.

The carbon column of codes.bsn decides what else happens. With carbon = 2 (dynamic carbon), the operation also raises the tillage factor of each mixed layer, which speeds the decomposition of soil organic matter for till_eff_days days. The tillage factor curve uses tillmix_a, tillmix_b and tillmix_c from carbon.bsn. With carbon = 0, only the mixing is done.

A puddling operation (pudl in management.sch) names a row of puddle.ops and a row of this file. When the HRU has more than 1 mm of ponded water, the soil is mixed with a routine for flooded soils. Otherwise the mixing is the same as for an ordinary tillage operation.

docs.title: Biological mixing
docs.text:
Biological mixing is the slow mixing of the soil by roots, worms and other organisms. How it is set depends on the carbon model.

With carbon = 2 in codes.bsn, the biomix row of tillage.til sets it. Its mix_eff is the biological mixing efficiency and its mix_dp the maximum biological mixing depth. Biological mixing runs every day in layers above 0 °C. After a tillage operation the efficiency drops to zero and builds back up over the following days at a rate set by bio_consol in carbon.bsn. If the file has no biomix row, the efficiency is 0.2 and the depth 50 mm. A biomix row with mix_eff of 0 turns daily biological mixing off.

With carbon = 0, the biomix row is not used for mixing. Biological mixing then happens once a year, at the end of the year, with the efficiency in the bio_mix column of hydrology.hyd and a fixed depth of 50 mm (or the soil depth, if smaller).

docs.title: Surface roughness
docs.text: rough, ridge_ht and ridge_sp are not used. The random roughness used for surface depression storage is 20 mm for every HRU in 62.0.1, whatever tillage is done.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
refdata/Osu_1hru/tillage.til in the SWAT+ repository:

tillage.til: written by SWAT+ editor v2.2.0 on 2023-03-22 04:25 for SWAT+ rev.60.5.4
name                   mix_eff        mix_dp         rough      ridge_ht      ridge_sp  description
puddle                 0.980       150.000        00.000         0.000         0.000    rice_paddy_puddling_oprtn

One operation named puddle, used for rice paddy puddling. It mixes 98% of the soil in the top 150 mm. The file has no biomix row; Osu_1hru runs with carbon = 0 in codes.bsn, so biological mixing comes from hydrology.hyd and the missing row has no effect.

The first lines of refdata/Ames_sub1/tillage.til, as shipped:

name           mix_eff         mix_dp        rough    ridge_ht    ridge_sp           description
bedderd            0.55           150           35           0           0           bedder(disk)
bedders            0.55           150           30           0           0           beddershaper
beddhipr           0.65           150           35           0           0           bedderdisk-hipper
beddkrow           0.85           100           40           0           0           bedderdisk-row
bedrollr           0.25            50            5           0           0           bedroller
beetcult           0.25            25           15           0           0           beetcultivator
biomix             0.01            50            0           0           0           biological_mixing

This file has no title line. SWAT+ skips the first two lines whatever they contain, so it takes the header as the title and the bedderd row as the header, and bedderd is not in the database. A schedule that names bedderd would not find it. The other 98 rows are read normally; for example mldboard (moldboard plow) mixes 95% of the top 250 mm. Ames_sub1 runs with carbon = 2, so its biomix row sets a daily biological mixing efficiency of 0.01 over the top 50 mm.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: time.sim sets the first and last day of the simulation and the number of time steps per day. Weather input, routing and every output file follow this period. The file is named in slot 1 of the simulation line of file.cio (default time.sim).

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Line 3 contains five integers in the order below. The reader does not match columns by header name.

# Column Units Default Description 1 day_start day of year 1 Day of the year on which the simulation starts, 1 to 366. A value of 0 or less is set to 1 (1 January). 2 yrc_start year - Calendar year in which the simulation starts. 3 day_end day of year 0 Day of the year on which the simulation ends in yrc_end. A value of 0 or less means the last day of that year (31 December). 4 yrc_end year - Calendar year in which the simulation ends. 5 step time steps per day 1 Number of time steps per day for precipitation, surface runoff and routing. A value of 0 or less is set to 1 (daily).

docs.title: Simulation period
docs.text:
The simulation runs over the calendar years yrc_start to yrc_end, which is

\[N_{yr} = \mathrm{yrc\_end} - \mathrm{yrc\_start} + 1\]

years. The first year starts on day_start, and every later year starts on 1 January. Every year but the last runs to 31 December. The last year ends on day_end, or on 31 December if day_end is 0. A day_end of 366 in a year that is not a leap year is treated as day 365. Leap years follow the Gregorian rule: years divisible by 4 are leap years, except century years that are not divisible by 400.

day_start and day_end make it possible to simulate water years or other periods that do not follow the calendar year. For example, day_start = 274, yrc_start = 1999, day_end = 273 and yrc_end = 2019 runs from 1 October 1999 to 30 September 2019. Neither year is a leap year, so day 274 is 1 October and day 273 is 30 September; in a leap year the same dates are days 275 and 274.

The warm-up years and the print window for daily output are set in print.prt. A zero yrc_start or yrc_end in print.prt is filled from this file.

docs.title: Time step
docs.text:
step is the number of time steps in a day:

step Time step 0 or 1 1 day 2 12 hours 24 1 hour 96 15 minutes 1440 1 minute

Any positive whole number works. The length of one time step in minutes is

\[\Delta t = \frac{1440}{\mathrm{step}}\]

With step greater than 1, the day is split into sub-daily steps for precipitation, infiltration and surface runoff, hydrograph routing through channels and reservoirs, and sub-daily channel output. The Green and Ampt infiltration method (gampt = 1 in codes.bsn) uses the sub-daily rainfall. Other processes, such as plant growth, soil water and nutrient cycling, still run once a day.

Sub-daily precipitation records (*.pcp files with a time step above 0) must have the same number of values per day as step. SWAT+ stores step values per day and does not check the record against it.

When step is greater than 1 and precipitation is generated, the weather generator also distributes each day's rainfall over the time steps. For a station with measured daily records, 62.0.1 does not fill the sub-daily values: the daily total is read, but the rainfall in each time step stays at zero. A sub-daily run therefore needs sub-daily precipitation records or generated precipitation.

docs.title: Weather outside the observed record
docs.text: When the simulation starts before, or ends after, the measured daily weather records listed in the climate index files, SWAT+ generates the weather for the days outside the record with the weather generator (weather-wgn.cli). The same applies to days that are flagged as missing in a record.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
refdata/Ames_sub1/time.sim in the SWAT+ repository:

time.sim:
day_start  yrc_start   day_end   yrc_end      step
       0      1975         0      2020         0

The simulation runs from 1 January 1975 to 31 December 2020, 46 years. day_start and day_end are 0, so the first and last days of the year are used. step is 0, which SWAT+ sets to 1, so the simulation is daily.

docs.title: Related files
docs.text:
• file.cio: names this file.
  • print.prt: warm-up years and print window for the outputs inside this period.
  • pcp.cli and the precipitation data files: their time step must match step for sub-daily records.
  • codes.bsn: selects Green and Ampt infiltration, which uses sub-daily rainfall.
Sources
  • Reader: time_read.f90
  • Type definition: type time_current in time_module.f90
  • Time step length: proc_bsn.f90
  • Year and day loop, leap years, end day: time_control.f90
  • Measured and generated precipitation: cli_pmeas.f90, cli_precip_control.f90
  • File name slot: in_sim%time in input_file_module.f90
Column Fortran variable day_start time%day_start yrc_start time%yrc_start day_end time%day_end yrc_end time%yrc_end step time%step

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
A temperature data file contains the measured daily maximum and minimum air temperature of one gauge. Each file is named on one line of tmp.cli, and a weather station uses it when the tmp column of weather-sta.cli gives the same name. Days without usable values are filled by the weather generator station named in the wgn column of the same weather station.

SWAT+ does not check the file extension. SWAT+ Editor writes .tmp; some older data sets use .tem. If tmp_path in file.cio is not null, its value is put in front of every file name in tmp.cli (see path prefixes).

Temperature is always read as daily data, also in sub-daily runs.

docs.title: Format
docs.text: Free format, whitespace-separated. Line 1 is a title and line 2 is a column header; both are skipped. Line 3 describes the gauge and every later line is one daily record.

docs.title: Gauge line
docs.text:
SWAT+ Editor writes the header nbyr tstep lat lon elev above this line.

# Column Units Description 1 nbyr years Number of years of record. SWAT+ uses it to size the store for the data, so it must be at least the number of calendar years the record spans. 2 tstep - Time step of the data. Not used by SWAT+; give 0. 3 lat decimal degrees Latitude of the gauge. Not used by SWAT+. 4 lon decimal degrees Longitude of the gauge. Not used by SWAT+. 5 elev m Elevation of the gauge. Used only for the elevation adjustment.

docs.title: Daily records
docs.text:
# Column Units Description 1 year - Calendar year. 2 day - Day of the year, 1 to 366. Called jday in earlier documentation. 3 tmax °C Maximum air temperature for the day, called tmpmax in earlier documentation. A value of -97 or less marks it as missing. 4 tmin °C Minimum air temperature for the day, called tmpmin in earlier documentation. A value of -97 or less marks it as missing.

Records must be continuous and in date order, as for precipitation: SWAT+ counts years by watching for day 365 or 366 followed by a record from a new year. Records before the simulation start are skipped when the file is read, by the rule described for precipitation files.

docs.title: Missing days
docs.text:
SWAT+ generates both temperatures for a day when

  • tmax or tmin is -97 or less (SWAT+ Editor and most tools write -99), or
  • the day is before the first record or after the last record of the file.

When only one of the two values is missing, the measured value of the other is replaced by a generated one as well, so the pair always comes from one source. The generated maximum is lower on wet days than on dry days, using the day's precipitation from the same weather station. The method is described in Climate and weather.

The daily mean air temperature used by snow, plant growth and other processes is

\[T_{av} = \frac{T_{max} + T_{min}}{2}\]

docs.title: Elevation adjustment
docs.text:
When lapse = 1 in codes.bsn, the temperatures of each HRU are changed for the difference between the gauge elevation and the HRU elevation:

\[T_{hru} = T + \mathrm{tlaps}\,\frac{z_{gauge} - z_{hru}}{1000}\]

applied to the maximum, minimum and mean temperature. tlaps is the temperature lapse rate in parameters.bsn (°C per km, default 6.5), \(z_{hru}\) is the elev column of hru.con and \(z_{gauge}\) is elev from this file (m). When the station's tmp column is sim, the elevation of the weather generator station is used for \(z_{gauge}\). As for precipitation, the adjustment values are calculated during channel and reservoir routing, so in a model without channels or reservoirs they remain zero.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text: The calibration parameter temp (object type cli) is meant to change the stored values of listed temperature records, but in 62.0.1 it does not change the listed records. See Climate changes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
First lines of refdata/Osu_1hru/Imsiltmp.tmp in the SWAT+ repository:

Imsiltmp.tmp: Temperature data - file written by SWAT+ editor 2023-03-22 04:22:29.141050
nbyr     tstep       lat       lon      elev
  42         0    35.610   127.290   247.900
1981    1    2.70000   -17.50000
1981    2   -3.00000    -7.50000
...
2023  364        2.3        -4.3
2023  365        0.8        -8.4

A daily record from 1 January 1981 to 31 December 2023 at 247.9 m. The record spans 43 calendar years while nbyr is 42. The Osu run starts in 2010, so only the 14 years from 2010 are stored and the smaller nbyr does no harm here; a run starting in 1981 would need nbyr of at least 43.

docs.title: Related files
docs.text:
• tmp.cli: lists the temperature files.
  • weather-sta.cli: assigns a temperature file to each weather station in its tmp column.
  • weather-wgn.cli: weather generator statistics that fill missing days.
  • *.tem: the same format under another extension.
  • file.cio: names tmp.cli and the tmp_path prefix.
  • codes.bsn and parameters.bsn: lapse switch and tlaps rate.
  • snow.sno: snowfall and melt use the daily mean and maximum temperature.
Sources
  • Reader: cli_tmeas.f90
  • Type definition: type climate_measured_data in climate_module.f90
  • Gauge name lookup from weather-sta.cli: cli_staread.f90, search.f90
  • Daily use, missing values and range check: climate_control.f90, cli_bounds_check.f90
  • Weather generator: cli_weatgn.f90, cli_tgen.f90
  • Elevation adjustment: cli_lapse.f90, applied in hru_control.f90
  • Path prefix: in_path_tmp in input_file_module.f90, read in readcio_read.f90
  • Calibration change temp: cal_conditions.f90
Column Fortran variable nbyr tmp(i)%nbyr tstep tmp(i)%tstep lat tmp(i)%lat lon tmp(i)%long elev tmp(i)%elev tmax tmp(i)%ts(day, iyr) tmin tmp(i)%ts2(day, iyr)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
treatment.trt is a file name kept from the SWAT2012 treatment table. Project setup tools can still write it into a project folder, but SWAT+ 62.0.1 does not open it, and file.cio has no slot for it. Its contents have no effect on a run, and the file can be left empty or deleted.

Water treatment in SWAT+ is part of water allocation. Treatment plants are defined in water_treat.wal, and the composition of treated water in om_treat.wal.

docs.title: Format
docs.text: None. The file is not read.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: Both reference datasets in the SWAT+ repository, refdata/Ames_sub1 and refdata/Osu_1hru, contain an empty treatment.trt.

docs.title: Related files
docs.text:
• Water allocation: water_treat.wal and om_treat.wal, the treatment inputs SWAT+ reads.
  • file.cio: lists the input files SWAT+ reads.
Sources
  • File name slots read from file.cio: input_file_module.f90, readcio_read.f90
  • Treatment inputs: water_treatment_read.f90 (water_treat.wal), om_treat_read.f90 (om_treat.wal)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
A routing unit collects the outflow of a group of objects, usually the HRUs of one landscape unit, and routes the sum as a single object. Its row in rout_unit.con sends the result on, typically the total flow to a channel and the recharge to an aquifer. Three files describe routing units: rout_unit.def lists the elements of each unit, rout_unit.ele describes each element, and rout_unit.rtu gives each unit its topography and field records.

A landscape unit is a group of HRUs used only for output. ls_unit.def lists the elements of each landscape unit and ls_unit.ele gives each element its area fractions. The same element file also weights the HRUs in the basin output files. aqu_catunit.ele lists aquifer elements; in 62.0.1 its only effect is to switch on the data rows of the basin aquifer output.

The files are named in file.cio:

File file.cio line Slot Read rout_unit.def routing_unit (line 8) 1 when the rtu count in object.cnt is above 0 rout_unit.ele routing_unit (line 8) 2 when the rtu count is above 0 rout_unit.rtu routing_unit (line 8) 3 when the rtu count is above 0 ls_unit.ele regions (line 26) 1 every run ls_unit.def regions (line 26) 2 every run aqu_catunit.ele regions (line 26) 9 every run, with the calibration inputs

Slot 4 of the routing_unit line (rout_unit.dr) is read from file.cio but never opened.

All six files are free format and whitespace-separated. The readers take the values in column order and do not check the header names.

For rout_unit.rtu, a name of null or a name that does not exist in the run folder means the file is not read. The other five files are skipped when the name is null. When the name is not null and the file does not exist, SWAT+ creates an empty file of that name in the run folder, reads nothing from it, and continues as if the name were null. What a missing file means for the run is given under each file.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line defines one routing unit. The line ends with a list of element numbers, and only the first number of that list has a header.

# Column Units Description 1 id - Number of the routing unit. Not used: the rows are taken in order, so row \(n\) defines routing unit \(n\). 2 name - Name of the routing unit. Not used. 3 elem_tot - Number of values in the element list that follows. When the list uses ranges, this is smaller than the number of elements. 4 and on elements - Element list: id values of rows in rout_unit.ele, written as described under Element lists.

docs.title: Element lists
docs.text:
rout_unit.def and ls_unit.def use the same list format. Each value is an element number, and a negative value closes a range that starts at the value before it. The list 1 -4 7 therefore means elements 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7, and elem_tot is 3 because the list has three values. A list with a single value gives one element. An elem_tot of 0 gives a unit with no elements.

A negative value must follow a positive one. Two negative values in a row, or a negative first value in a list of more than one value, put negative element numbers into the list.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Routing unit \(n\) is the routing unit whose id in rout_unit.con is \(n\). It uses row \(n\) of rout_unit.def, counted from the first data line, whatever the id column says. SWAT+ reads as many rows as the rtu count in object.cnt. Extra rows are ignored, and units without a row have no elements.
  • The define column of rout_unit.rtu is not used to find the row. The routing unit ids in rout_unit.con, the rows of rout_unit.def and the ids in rout_unit.rtu therefore have to run 1, 2, 3 in the same order. The SWAT+ Editor writes them that way.
  • An object can be an element of one routing unit only. If two element rows of rout_unit.ele point to the same object and both are listed in rout_unit.def (in one unit or in two), SWAT+ stops at start-up with an allocation error.
  • A routing unit with no elements produces no outflow, and no message is written.
  • If rout_unit.def is missing or null in a project with routing units, every routing unit has no elements. The HRUs then reach the rest of the model only through their rows in hru.con, and an HRU without outflow connections there loses its water.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
refdata/Osu_1hru/rout_unit.def in the SWAT+ repository:

rout_unit.def: written by SWAT+ editor v2.2.0 on 2023-03-22 04:25 for SWAT+ rev.60.5.4
      id              name  elem_tot  elements  
       1             rtu001         1      1

Routing unit 1 has one element, element 1 of rout_unit.ele.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one element.

# Column Units Description 1 id - Element number, used in the element lists of rout_unit.def. The rows can be in any order and the numbers do not have to be consecutive; the largest id sets the size of the table. 2 name - Name of the element. Not used. 3 obj_typ - Object type of the element, one of the codes below. 4 obj_id - Number of the object within its type: its id in the connection file of that type. 5 frac fraction Fraction of the element in the routing unit, used to scale the element's outflow. See Expansion factor. 6 dlr - Delivery ratio: 0 or calc, 1 or full. See Delivery ratio.

The object type codes SWAT+ recognises are:

obj_typ Object Connection file hru HRU hru.con hlt HRU-lte hru-lte.con ru routing unit rout_unit.con cha legacy channel channel.con sdc SWAT+ channel chandeg.con res reservoir reservoir.con exc export coefficient exco.con dr delivery ratio delratio.con out outlet outlet.con

Any other code, including aqu, rec and rtu, is not recognised. No message is written, and the element is linked to object 1, the first object in the model (HRU 1 in a model with HRUs). Earlier documentation listed aquifers, recall objects and "another rtu" as possible elements; in 62.0.1 a routing unit inside a routing unit has the code ru.

docs.title: Expansion factor
docs.text:
Each day a routing unit adds up the hydrographs of its elements. Each element's hydrographs are multiplied by an expansion factor \(e\) before they are added:

  • HRU and HRU-lte elements with frac below 0.99999:

    \[e = \mathrm{frac}\;\frac{A_{ru}}{A_{obj}}\]

    where \(A_{ru}\) is the routing unit's area in rout_unit.con and \(A_{obj}\) the HRU's area in its connection file. When frac is the HRU's share of the routing unit area, \(e\) is 1 and the whole HRU outflow is added. - HRU and HRU-lte elements with frac of 0.99999 or more: \(e = 1\), so the whole HRU outflow is added whatever the areas. - Export coefficient elements: \(e\) as for HRUs when the export coefficient object has an area above 0.01 ha, otherwise 1. - All other elements: \(e = \mathrm{frac}\), the fraction of the object's outflow that enters the routing unit.

The frac values are not checked. If they do not add up as intended, the routing unit outflow is scaled accordingly.

The factor and the delivery ratio apply to the total, surface, lateral and tile hydrographs. The recharge hydrograph is multiplied by the factor only. Pesticide, salt and constituent loads are added in full: 62.0.1 applies neither the expansion factor nor the delivery ratio to them.

When another object sends flow to a routing unit through its connection file, the inflow is shared among the unit's elements. Each element receives the sender's fraction multiplied by its frac. How an HRU uses that inflow is described under Inflow to HRUs and routing units.

docs.title: Delivery ratio
docs.text:
The dlr column sets a ratio for each hydrograph variable of the element:

dlr Ratio 0 or calc Flow 1. All other variables (sediment, nutrients, chlorophyll-a, CBOD, dissolved oxygen, sediment size classes) are multiplied by a calculated ratio, given below. 1 or full 1 for every variable. any other value 0 for every variable.

For HRU and HRU-lte elements the calculated ratio is

\[DR = \min\left(1,\ \sqrt{\frac{t_{c,\mathrm{elem}}}{t_{c,ru}}}\right)\]

where \(t_{c,\mathrm{elem}}\) is the HRU's time of concentration (see Surface runoff lag), or for an HRU-lte the time of concentration of its hru-lte.hru record, and \(t_{c,ru}\) is the routing unit's time of concentration (see Time of concentration). For sdc and ru elements the calculated ratio is 1. For the other element types no ratio is calculated, and the element takes the ratio last calculated for an earlier element (0 if there is none).

A dlr value that names a record in delratio.del does not work in 62.0.1. The names are looked up when the routing units are set up, and delratio.del is read only after that, so no name is ever found. The ratio then stays at 0 for every variable, and the element contributes only its recharge hydrograph. The same happens for any other value, such as null. Use 0, calc, 1 or full. The SWAT+ Editor writes 0.

The decision table action hru_fr_update (see decision tables) reads a replacement rout_unit.ele during the run. By then delratio.del has been read, so a dlr that names a delratio.del record does take that record's ratios from dr_om.del. Elements whose dlr is 0, calc, 1, full or an unknown name keep the ratios they had before.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• rout_unit.ele is required in a project with routing units. If it is missing or null, the routing unit tables are never set up and the run fails during start-up.
  • In sub-daily runs (time step below one day) with Green and Ampt infiltration (gampt = 1 in codes.bsn), the routing unit's sub-daily flow is set from each HRU element in turn, so only the last HRU element in the list is kept, and the result is shifted by a fixed 2 hours instead of the routing unit's time of concentration.
  • The ru row of print.prt writes the sum of the element hydrographs of each routing unit to the ru_* files (see ru files).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
refdata/Osu_1hru/rout_unit.ele:

rout_unit.ele: written by SWAT+ editor v2.2.0 on 2023-03-22 04:25 for SWAT+ rev.60.5.4
      id  name                   obj_typ    obj_id          frac               dlr  
       1  hru0001                    hru         1            1                 0

Element 1 is HRU 1. With frac = 1 the whole HRU outflow enters the routing unit. With dlr = 0 the water is delivered in full, and sediment and nutrients are multiplied by the calculated delivery ratio.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one routing unit.

# Column Units Description 1 id - Number of the routing unit. Routing unit \(n\) (the id in rout_unit.con) uses the row whose id is \(n\). The ids must lie between 1 and the rtu count in object.cnt. An id of 0 ends the file. 2 name - Name of the routing unit. Not used. 3 define - Name of the rout_unit.def row. Not used: routing unit \(n\) always uses row \(n\) of rout_unit.def. 4 dlr - Delivery ratio of the routing unit. Not used; delivery ratios are set per element in rout_unit.ele. 5 topo - Name of a record in topography.hyd. Its slope and slope length are used for the routing unit's time of concentration. 6 field - Name of a record in field.fld. Its field length is used for the routing unit's time of concentration.

docs.title: Time of concentration
docs.text:
The routing unit's time of concentration is the sum of an overland flow time and a channel flow time:

\[t_{ov} = \frac{0.0556\,(L_{slp}\,n)^{0.6}}{(slp + 0.001)^{0.3}}, \qquad t_{ch} = \frac{0.62\,L\,n^{0.75}}{A^{0.125}\,\left(0.5\,(slp + 0.001)\right)^{0.375}}, \qquad t_{c,ru} = t_{ov} + t_{ch}\] Symbol Meaning Units \(t_{ov}\), \(t_{ch}\), \(t_{c,ru}\) overland, channel and total time of concentration hr \(L_{slp}\) slope length, slp_len of the topo record m \(slp\) average slope, slp of the topo record m/m \(L\) channel length, len of the field record divided by 1000 km \(A\) routing unit area, area in rout_unit.con km² \(n\) Manning's n for overland flow, averaged over the HRU elements -

The Manning's n is the area-weighted mean of the ov_mann values of the HRU elements' land uses (see landuse.lum):

\[n = \frac{\sum_i n_i\,A_i}{A}\]

where \(A_i\) is the full area of HRU element \(i\); frac is not used. When the routing unit has an element that is not an HRU, the running sum is set to 0.1 at that element and the HRU elements after it are added to 0.1. The result then depends on the order of the elements.

The time of concentration is used for the calculated delivery ratio of the elements and, in sub-daily runs, for the unit hydrograph of the routing unit.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• A topo name that is null or not found in topography.hyd gives the first record of that file. A field name that is null or not found gives the built-in field length of 500 m. No message is written in either case.
  • rout_unit.rtu is required in a project with routing units. If it is missing or null, no routing unit records are set up and the run fails during start-up.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
refdata/Osu_1hru/rout_unit.rtu:

rout_unit.rtu: written by SWAT+ editor v2.2.0 on 2023-03-22 04:25 for SWAT+ rev.60.5.4
      id              name            define               dlr              topo             field  
       1            rtu01             rtu001              null        toportu011            fld011

fld011 is in field.fld with a length of 500 m. toportu011 is not in this dataset's topography.hyd, so the routing unit uses its first record, topohru0001 (slope 0.01078, slope length 10 m), without a message. define and dlr have no effect.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Line 1 is a title, line 2 gives the number of landscape units, and line 3 is the column header. Each later line defines one landscape unit, and the line ends with an element list as in rout_unit.def.

# Column Units Description 1 id - Number of the landscape unit. Not used: row \(n\) defines landscape unit \(n\). 2 name - Name of the landscape unit, written in the name column of the landscape unit output files. 3 area ha Area of the landscape unit. Not used. 4 elem_tot - Number of values in the element list. 0 gives a landscape unit with no elements, whose output is all zeros. 5 and on elements - Element list: id values of rows in ls_unit.ele, written as described under Element lists.

SWAT+ reads as many rows as line 2 gives.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Landscape units are used for output only. Each one gets a row in the lsunit_wb, lsunit_nb, lsunit_ls and lsunit_pw files and in the landscape unit carbon files (lsu_cb_gl, lsu_cb_trf, lsu_cb_plt), switched on in print.prt. Each value is the sum over the unit's elements of the HRU (or HRU-lte) value multiplied by the element's sub_frac in ls_unit.ele. See Aggregation.
  • The element number is used as the HRU number: element \(n\) adds the output of HRU \(n\) (or HRU-lte \(n\)), and its obj_typ_no is not consulted. The element ids in ls_unit.ele therefore have to equal the HRU numbers.
  • In the output files, unit is the landscape unit number and gis_id is taken from the routing unit with the same number in rout_unit.con.
  • With gwflow and landscape unit connection (conn_type 2, see lsucell.gw), the element lists also decide which HRUs pass recharge and remaining evapotranspiration to the cells of each landscape unit. Here too element \(n\) is HRU \(n\).
  • ls_unit.def needs ls_unit.ele. If ls_unit.def is missing or null, the project has no landscape units and the landscape unit output files are not opened.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
refdata/Osu_1hru/ls_unit.def:

ls_unit.def: written by SWAT+ editor v2.2.0 on 2023-03-22 04:25 for SWAT+ rev.60.5.4
1
      id              name          area  elem_tot  elements  
       1            rtu001       10.0000         1      1

One landscape unit of 10 ha, named rtu001 after the routing unit, with element 1 of ls_unit.ele.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one element. Six values are read from each line.

# Column Units Description 1 id - Element number, used in the element lists of ls_unit.def. The largest id sets the size of the table. Must equal the HRU number (see below). 2 name - Name of the element. Not used. 3 obj_typ - hru or hlt. Elements of any other type are skipped in the sums. 4 obj_typ_no - HRU or HRU-lte number. 5 bsn_frac fraction Fraction of the basin land area (ls_area in object.cnt) covered by the HRU. Weight of the HRU in the basin output files. 6 sub_frac fraction Fraction of the landscape unit area covered by the HRU. Weight of the HRU in the landscape unit output files. Called lsu_frac in earlier documentation; the Ames_sub1 file labels it RU_FRAC.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Basin output: the basin_wb, basin_nb, basin_ls and basin_pw files, including the starting soil water and snow in basin_wb, are the sums of the HRU values multiplied by bsn_frac. The fractions are used as given; if they do not add up to 1, the basin values are scaled by their sum.
  • For each HRU number \(n\), the basin sum reads row \(n\), takes its obj_typ_no \(m\), and then uses the obj_typ and bsn_frac of row \(m\) with the output of HRU \(m\). The sum is right when row \(n\) describes HRU \(n\), which is how the SWAT+ Editor writes the file. HRU-lte objects are summed the same way over the first rows of the file.
  • Landscape unit output uses sub_frac (see ls_unit.def).
  • The soft calibration of the whole basin in water_balance.sft takes each HRU's area as ls_area times its bsn_frac (see soft calibration).
  • The decision table action hru_fr_update reads a replacement ls_unit.ele during the run and sets the area of each hru element to bsn_frac times ls_area.
  • If ls_unit.ele is missing or null, the basin landscape files are opened and get their headers, and no data rows are written. The routine that stores the basin's starting soil water at the end of the warm-up years still reads the element table, so a model with HRUs and no ls_unit.ele can stop with a memory error at that point. Treat the file as required in any model with HRUs.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
refdata/Ames_sub1/ls_unit.ele:

lsu_unit.ele
          ID    NAME      OBJ_TYP  OBJ_TYP_NO    BSN_FRAC       RU_FRAC
           1    hru0001      hru           1     0.20           0.0
           2    hru0002      hru           2     0.20           0.0
           3    hru0003      hru           3     0.20           0.0
           4    hru0004      hru           4     0.20           0.0
           5    hru0005      hru           5     0.10           0.0
           6    hru0006      hru           6     0.10           0.0
           7    hru0007      hru           7     0.20           0.0
           8    hru0008      hru           8     0.20           0.0
           9    hru0009      hru           9     0.20           0.0
          10    hru0010      hru          10     0.20           0.0
          11    hru0011      hru          11     0.10           0.0
          12    hru0012      hru          12     0.10           0.0

This file is not in the SWAT+ Editor layout: it has six columns and upper-case headers. Each row describes the HRU of the same number, as the basin sums require. The BSN_FRAC values add up to 2.0, so every basin output of this dataset is twice the area-weighted HRU average. Ames_sub1 has no ls_unit.def, so the RU_FRAC values of 0 are not used.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Line 1 is a title and line 2 is the column header; both are skipped. Each later line is one element, and seven values are read from it. A line with fewer values takes the missing ones from the next line.

# Column Units Description 1 id - Element number. The largest id sets the size of the table. 2 name - Name of the element. 3 obj_typ - Object type, aqu in files written by the SWAT+ Editor. 4 obj_typ_no - Aquifer number. 5 bsn_frac fraction Fraction of the basin covered by the aquifer. 6 sub_frac fraction Fraction of the aquifer region covered by the element. 7 reg_frac fraction Fraction of the calibration region covered by the element.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• In 62.0.1 the file works as a switch. When it has at least one element, the basin aquifer files (basin_aqu row in print.prt) get one data row per interval. Without it they get headers only.
  • The basin aquifer values are weighted by each aquifer's area divided by tot_area in object.cnt (see aquifer output). The columns of aqu_catunit.ele are not used for this.
  • The columns are meant for aquifer regions defined in aqu_catunit.def and aqu_reg.def. SWAT+ 62.0.1 reads those files, but no calculation or output uses the regions.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The first rows of refdata/Osu_1hru/aqu_catunit.ele:

aqu_catunit.ele: written by SWAT+ editor v2.2.0 on 2023-03-22 04:25 for SWAT+ rev.60.5.4
