docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The carbon output files report the carbon budget of the soil, residue and plants. Two kinds of file are available:

  • Flat files with one row per HRU or landscape unit per interval: carbon gains and losses, soil carbon transformations and plant carbon.
  • Per-layer files with one row per HRU per interval and one column per soil layer for each variable: soil carbon totals, carbon pools, N and P in the pools, carbon and N fluxes, process drivers, pool dynamics and soil properties.

Every family has a row in print.prt with the usual daily, monthly, yearly and average annual flags. The rows are recognised only when print.prt uses object labels (use_obj_lbls = y); in the fixed-order layout there is no place for them. A row name that SWAT+ does not know stops the run with an error.

Most columns are filled by the dynamic carbon model, which runs when carbon = 2 in codes.bsn. Four per-layer families (hru_cb_cpool, hru_cb_flux, hru_cb_drv, hru_cb_dyn) are written only with carbon = 2. The other families are written for any setting, but with carbon = 0 many of their columns stay at zero. See the carbon model theory for the pools and transformations.

docs.title: Files and switches
docs.text:
print.prt row Files Rows Layers hru_cb_gl hru_carb_gl_{day,mon,yr,aa} HRU no hru_cb_trf hru_scf_{day,mon,yr,aa} HRU no hru_cb_lyr hru_cbn_lyr_{day,mon,yr,aa} HRU yes hru_cb_cpool hru_cpool_stat_{day,mon,yr,aa} HRU yes, carbon = 2 only hru_cb_npool hru_n_p_pool_stat_{day,mon,yr,aa} HRU yes hru_cb_plt hru_plc_stat_{day,mon,yr,aa} HRU no hru_cb_flux hru_cflux_stat_{day,mon,yr,aa} HRU yes, carbon = 2 only hru_cb_drv hru_carb_drv_{day,mon,yr,aa} HRU yes, carbon = 2 only hru_cb_dyn hru_carb_dyn_{day,mon,yr,aa} HRU yes, carbon = 2 only hru_cb_snap hru_soil_snap_{day,mon,yr} and hru_soil_snap_tot HRU yes lsu_cb_gl lsu_carb_gl_{day,mon,yr,aa} landscape unit no lsu_cb_trf lsu_scf_{day,mon,yr,aa} landscape unit no lsu_cb_plt lsu_plc_stat_{day,mon,yr,aa} landscape unit no

Each file is written as .txt, plus .csv when csvout = y. The hru_cb_snap row writes _tot in place of _aa; see Soil snapshot. The landscape unit files are written only when the model defines landscape units in ls_unit.def.

Example print.prt rows (labelled layout):

objects                  daily       monthly        yearly         avann
hru_cb_gl                    n             y             y             y
hru_cb_lyr                   n             n             y             y
hru_cb_snap                  n             n             n             y

docs.title: Value types and aggregation
docs.text:
The flat gain and loss files (hru_carb_gl, hru_scf, lsu_carb_gl, lsu_scf) report fluxes. Monthly and yearly files are sums over the interval, and the average annual file divides the run total by the number of printed years.

All other files report a state at the moment the row is written: the monthly file gives the value on the last day of the month, the yearly file the value on the last day of the year, and the average annual file the value at the end of the run. They are not averages. This also applies to the per-layer flux file hru_cflux_stat: its daily, monthly and yearly rows give the flux of the last day of the interval in kg/ha/day, and only the average annual file gives the run total divided by the number of printed years, in kg/ha/yr.

docs.title: Carbon gains and losses
docs.text:
hru_carb_gl_* (row hru_cb_gl). One row per HRU. After the seven leading columns (jday, mon, day, yr, unit, gis_id, name) come 21 columns in kg C/ha, in three groups.

Soil:

Column Description sed_c carbon removed with eroded sediment surq_c dissolved carbon in surface runoff latq_c dissolved organic carbon in lateral flow, all layers perc_c dissolved carbon in percolation below the profile res_decay carbon added to the soil by residue decay man_app_c carbon added with applied manure man_graze_c carbon added with manure from grazing animals rsp_c CO₂-C from soil respiration, whole profile soil_emit_c CO₂-C from burning soil carbon

Residue:

Column Description plant_surf_c carbon added to surface residue by leaf drop and kill plant_root_c carbon added to soil residue by root death rsd_surfdecay_c carbon lost from surface residue by decay rsd_rootdecay_c carbon lost from root and incorporated residue by decay harv_stov_c carbon removed by residue harvest rsd_emit_c CO₂-C from burning surface residue

Plant:

Column Description npp_c plant carbon growth (net primary production) harv_abgr_c carbon removed by grain and biomass harvest harv_root_c carbon removed by tuber (root) harvest drop_c carbon moved to residue by leaf drop and kill grazeat_c carbon eaten by grazing animals plant_emit_c CO₂-C from burning plants

docs.title: Soil carbon transformations
docs.text:
hru_scf_* (row hru_cb_trf). One row per HRU with 13 columns in kg C/ha: meta_micr, str_micr, str_hs, co2_meta, co2_str, micr_hs, micr_hp, hs_micr, hs_hp, hp_micr, co2_micr, co2_hs, co2_hp. Each name gives the source and destination pool: meta metabolic litter, str structural litter, micr microbial biomass, hs slow humus, hp passive humus, and co2 carbon lost as CO₂.

In 62.0.1 these columns are reset to zero each day and never filled, so every value in hru_scf_* and lsu_scf_* is zero. For the same flows by layer, use hru_cflux_stat (cfmets1 for meta_micr, co2fs1 for co2_micr, and so on).

docs.title: Plant carbon
docs.text:
hru_plc_stat_* (row hru_cb_plt). One row per HRU with seven columns in kg C/ha:

Column Description total_c carbon in all plant parts ab_gr_c carbon in above-ground biomass leaf_c carbon in leaves stem_c carbon in stems seed_c carbon in seeds root_c carbon in roots surf_rsd_c carbon in residue

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
Each row starts with the seven leading columns, then a depth block depth_lyr1 to depth_lyrN giving the depth to the bottom of each soil layer in mm, then one block of N columns for each variable, named <variable>_lyr1 to <variable>_lyrN. There is no units line: line 1 is the project name and version, line 2 the column header, and the data start on line 3.

N is the same for every HRU. By default it is the largest number of soil layers among all HRUs, so the deepest profile is written in full. The optional file carbon_layers.prt sets N directly. In an HRU with fewer layers than N, the extra columns contain -99.

docs.title: Soil carbon by layer
docs.text:
hru_cbn_lyr_* (row hru_cb_lyr). Line 1 ends with the note total soil carbon (Mg/ha) by layer depth in mm. The value columns are in Mg C/ha:

Columns Description depth_lyr1 ... depth_lyrN depth to the bottom of each layer (mm) tot_300_sum total soil organic carbon in the top 300 mm tot_lyr1 ... tot_lyrN total soil organic carbon in each layer seq_300_sum sequestered (humus and microbial) carbon in the top 300 mm seq_lyr1 ... seq_lyrN sequestered carbon in each layer

For the 300 mm sums, the layer that crosses 300 mm is counted in proportion to its thickness above 300 mm. With carbon = 0, both totals are the sum of the active humus, stable humus and microbial carbon.

docs.title: Carbon pools
docs.text:
hru_cpool_stat_* (row hru_cb_cpool, carbon = 2 only). Ten variables per layer:

Variable Units Description residue_c kg C/ha residue carbon in the layer structural_c kg C/ha structural litter metabolic_c kg C/ha metabolic litter hs_c kg C/ha slow humus hp_c kg C/ha passive humus microbial_c kg C/ha microbial biomass lignin_c kg C/ha lignin part of structural litter nonlignin_c kg C/ha non-lignin part of structural litter root_mass kg/ha root mass in the layer soil_water mm water in the layer

docs.title: N and P in the pools
docs.text: hru_n_p_pool_stat_* (row hru_cb_npool). Eighteen variables per layer, in kg N/ha and kg P/ha: tot_pool_n, residue_n, structural_n, metabolic_n, hs_n, hp_n, microbial_n, lignin_n, nonlignin_n, then the same nine with _p. tot_pool_n and tot_pool_p add residue, structural and metabolic litter, slow and passive humus, microbial biomass, the dissolved organic pool and manure.

docs.title: Carbon and N fluxes
docs.text:
hru_cflux_stat_* (row hru_cb_flux, carbon = 2 only). Thirty-seven variables per layer. In the names, s1 is microbial biomass, s2 slow humus, s3 passive humus, met metabolic litter and str structural litter, so cfs1s2 is the carbon flow from microbial biomass to slow humus.

Variables Units Description cfmets1, cfstrs1, cfstrs2 kg C/ha/day carbon moved from litter to microbial biomass or slow humus efmets1, efstrs1, efstrs2 kg N/ha/day nitrogen moved with those flows immmets1, immstrs1, immstrs2 kg N/ha/day N immobilised by the litter flows mnrmets1, mnrstrs1, mnrstrs2 kg N/ha/day N mineralised by the litter flows co2fmet, co2fstr kg C/ha/day CO₂-C from metabolic and structural litter cfs1s2, cfs1s3, cfs2s1, cfs2s3, cfs3s1 kg C/ha/day carbon moved between the humus and microbial pools efs1s2, efs1s3, efs2s1, efs2s3, efs3s1 kg N/ha/day nitrogen moved with those flows imms1s2, imms1s3, imms2s1, imms2s3, imms3s1 kg N/ha/day N immobilised by those flows mnrs1s2, mnrs1s3, mnrs2s1, mnrs2s3, mnrs3s1 kg N/ha/day N mineralised by those flows co2fs1, co2fs2, co2fs3 kg C/ha/day CO₂-C from microbial biomass, slow humus and passive humus

The average annual file gives yearly totals (kg/ha/yr); see Value types and aggregation.

docs.title: Process drivers
docs.text:
hru_carb_drv_* (row hru_cb_drv, carbon = 2 only). Fourteen variables per layer, all for the day the row is written:

Variable Units Description sut fraction soil water control on decomposition tillagef - tillage factor of the layer cons_bmix - biological mixing coefficient of the layer tillagef_biomix - part of the tillage factor from biological mixing tillagef_tillmix - part of the tillage factor from tillage operations till_eff fraction tillage effect on decomposition cdg fraction soil temperature control on decomposition ox fraction oxygen control on decomposition cs fraction combined control on decomposition no3 kg N/ha nitrate available to the transformations nh4 kg N/ha ammonium available to the transformations co2_resp kg C/ha CO₂-C respired in the layer soil_temp °C soil temperature emix fraction fraction of the layer mixed by tillage or biological mixing

docs.title: Pool dynamics
docs.text:
hru_carb_dyn_* (row hru_cb_dyn, carbon = 2 only). Twenty-one variables per layer:

Variables Units Description asp, abp fraction share of decomposed slow humus and of decomposed microbial biomass sent to passive humus abco2, a1co2, asco2, apco2 fraction share of decomposed microbial biomass, metabolic and passive pools, slow humus and passive humus lost as CO₂ ncbm, nchp, nchs ratio N:C ratio of microbial biomass, passive humus and slow humus bmctp, bmntp kg/ha/day potential C and N transformation of microbial biomass hsctp, hsntp kg/ha/day potential C and N transformation of slow humus hpctp, hpntp kg/ha/day potential C and N transformation of passive humus lmctp, lmntp kg/ha/day potential C and N transformation of metabolic litter lsctp, lslctp, lslnctp, lsntp kg/ha/day potential transformation of structural litter: C, lignin C, non-lignin C and N

docs.title: Soil snapshot
docs.text:
hru_soil_snap_* (row hru_cb_snap). Thirteen soil properties per layer:

Variable Units Description bd Mg/m³ bulk density awc mm/mm available water capacity soil_k mm/h saturated hydraulic conductivity tot_c kg C/ha total soil organic carbon clay, silt, sand, rock % particle size fractions and rock fragments alb fraction albedo usle_k - USLE soil erodibility ec dS/m electrical conductivity caco3 % calcium carbonate content ph - soil pH

The daily, monthly and yearly flags write hru_soil_snap_day, _mon and _yr. The average annual flag writes hru_soil_snap_tot instead, which has one row per HRU at the start of the run (marked jday = 0) and one at the end. Both rows give tot_c in kg C/ha, so the change in soil carbon in layer K over the run is tot_c_lyrK on the end row minus tot_c_lyrK on the start row. The start rows are written only when carbon = 2.

docs.title: Repeated rows
docs.text: In 62.0.1 the files of the hru_cb_lyr, hru_cb_cpool, hru_cb_npool, hru_cb_plt, hru_cb_flux, hru_cb_drv and hru_cb_dyn rows, and the daily, monthly and yearly files of hru_cb_snap, repeat their block of HRU rows once per HRU. In a model with 12 HRUs, every interval has 144 rows: the 12 HRU rows written 12 times with the same values. Keep the first occurrence of each unit within an interval when reading these files. hru_soil_snap_tot, hru_carb_gl, hru_scf and the landscape unit files are not affected.

docs.title: Landscape unit files
docs.text:
The landscape unit files are area-weighted averages of the HRU values, each HRU weighted by its fraction of the landscape unit. Per-layer files have no landscape unit version because the HRUs in a unit can have different soil profiles.

File Columns lsu_carb_gl_* the 21 columns of hru_carb_gl lsu_scf_* the 13 columns of hru_scf (all zero in 62.0.1) lsu_plc_stat_* one column, lsu_plt_c: carbon in all plant parts (kg C/ha)

lsu_plt_c is a state value: the monthly, yearly and average annual files give the value on the last day of the interval.

docs.title: Layer count file
docs.text:
carbon_layers.prt is optional and is not listed in file.cio. When it is present in the run folder, it fixes N, the number of layer columns in every per-layer file. Use it to keep the same number of columns across runs, or to write only the top layers.

  • Line 1: title, skipped.
  • Line 2: header, skipped.
  • Line 3: the number of layers, a whole number of 1 or more.
carbon_layers.prt: layers to expand in per-layer carbon output
n_layers
10

With 10, every per-layer file has ten columns per variable, whatever the soils. A value below 1 is rejected with a message in diagnostics.out, and N then defaults to the largest layer count among the HRUs.

docs.title: Legacy CSU carbon outputs
docs.text:
An older set of carbon files, kept for existing CSU workflows, runs beside the files above. SWAT+ Editor does not write the rows that switch them on; they are added to print.prt by hand. The code marks them for removal in revision 63.

print.prt row and flag Files hru_cb with y or l in the daily, monthly or yearly column hru_cbn_lyr.txt, hru_seq_lyr.txt, hru_n_p_pool_stat.txt as above, with l in any column adds hru_begsim_soil_prop.txt and hru_endsim_soil_prop.txt (the start rows need carbon = 2) as above, with carbon = 2 adds hru_plc_stat.txt, hru_cflux_stat.txt, hru_cpool_stat.txt hru_cb with any flag other than n basin_carbon_all.txt (header lines only when hru_nb has y in the average annual column) hru_cb_vars with y or l in the daily, monthly or yearly column, and carbon = 2 hru_carbvars.txt, hru_org_allo_vars.txt, hru_org_ratio_vars.txt, hru_org_trans_vars.txt

These files have no interval suffix: one file collects the rows for every interval switched on. Each also gets a .csv copy when csvout = y. The legacy files contain the same quantities as the files above in a different layout. For example, legacy hru_cbn_lyr.txt and hru_seq_lyr.txt together contain the values that the new hru_cbn_lyr_yr.txt gives in one table.

The legacy files do not use the layer count file. The cbn_diagnostics setting from the old carb_coefs.cbn no longer exists; the l flag on the hru_cb row takes its place.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
These files report what happens in the channel network: flow, sediment and nutrients entering, leaving and stored in each channel, channel geometry and erosion, and sediment budgets for each channel, each stream order and the whole basin.

SWAT+ routes channels defined in the channel files of the SWAT+ Editor (see Channels and channel-lte). Two rows of print.prt control all of the channel files:

print.prt row Files opened channel_sd channel_sd_*, channel_sdmorph_*, sd_chanbud_*, and the sediment budget files ch_sedbud_*, chanbud_order_* and sedbud_*. With a sub-daily time step and daily set to y, also channel_sd_subday.txt. basin_sd_cha basin_sd_cha_*, basin_sd_chamorph_*, basin_sd_chanbud_*

Each y in the daily, monthly, yearly or avann column of a row opens the matching file. Most files use the suffixes _day, _mon, _yr and _aa. The ch_sedbud and chanbud_order files use _d, _m, _y and _a. With csvout set to y, a .csv copy of each file is written as well.

The channel files are opened only when the project has at least one channel, except sd_chanbud_*, which is opened whenever its switch is on.

The channel and basin_cha rows open the legacy channel files described at the end of this page.

docs.title: Files at a glance
docs.text: File One row per Content channel_sd_* channel Water surface, storage, inflow and outflow of water, sediment and nutrients, and stream temperature. channel_sdmorph_* channel Flow rates, sediment transport and erosion, and channel width, depth and slope. sd_chanbud_* channel Sediment and nutrient budget: inflow, outflow, deposition and erosion. ch_sedbud_* channel Bank and bed erosion, floodplain deposition, channel size. chanbud_order_* stream order (1 to 12) The ch_sedbud values summed over all channels of each stream order. sedbud_* basin (one row) Basin sediment budget: upland yield, bank and bed erosion, floodplain, reservoir and wetland deposition. basin_sd_cha_* basin channel_sd summed over all channels. basin_sd_chamorph_* basin channel_sdmorph summed over all channels. basin_sd_chanbud_* basin sd_chanbud summed over all channels. channel_sd_subday.txt channel and time step Outflow for each sub-daily time step.

docs.title: Leading columns
docs.text:
Files with one row per channel start with seven columns:

# Column Description 1 jday Day of the year of the last day in the print step. 2 mon Month. 3 day Day of the month. 4 yr Calendar year. 5 unit Channel number. 6 gis_id GIS identifier of the channel. 7 name Channel name.

The basin files have the same seven columns with unit and gis_id set to 1 and the project name in name. In ch_sedbud_* the same three columns are labelled ichan, ob and name. chanbud_order_* has iord (the stream order) in place of all three, and sedbud_* has only the four date columns.

docs.title: channel_sd files
docs.text:
After the leading columns come four values for the water surface, then three blocks of 18 values (storage, inflow, outflow) and a final stream temperature.

Column Units Description area ha Water surface area of the channel. precip m³ Precipitation falling on the water surface. evap m³ Evaporation from the water surface. seep m³ Seepage through the channel bed.

Each block has the same 18 quantities. The column names end in _stor, _in or _out:

Quantity Storage units Inflow and outflow units Description flo m³ m³/s Water: volume stored, or average flow rate. sed tons tons Sediment. orgn kg N kg N Organic nitrogen. sedp kg P kg P Organic (sediment-attached) phosphorus. no3 kg N kg N Nitrate. solp kg P kg P Soluble mineral phosphorus. chla kg kg Chlorophyll a. nh3 kg N kg N Ammonium. no2 kg N kg N Nitrite. cbod kg kg Carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand. dox kg kg Dissolved oxygen. san tons tons Sand. sil tons tons Silt. cla tons tons Clay. sag tons tons Small aggregates. lag tons tons Large aggregates. grv tons tons Gravel. null °C °C Water temperature.

The 18th column of each block is headed null and has no unit in the units row. It is the water temperature of the stored water, the inflow and the outflow. The outflow temperature is the stream temperature from the heat balance calculation.

The last column, water_temp (°C), is not the heat balance temperature. It is \(5 + 0.75\,\bar{T}\), where \(\bar{T}\) is the mean air temperature of the day at the weather station of the channel that was routed last. All channels therefore show the same value for a given day. Use the null column of the outflow block for the stream temperature of each channel.

docs.title: Aggregation
docs.text:
• The storage block is the storage at the end of the print step, also in the monthly, yearly and average annual files.
  • Inflow and outflow rates (flo_in, flo_out) are averaged over the days of the step. All other inflow and outflow quantities are totals for the step; the average annual file gives the average yearly total.
  • Water temperatures in the inflow and outflow blocks are flow-weighted averages.
  • precip, evap and seep are totals for the step. area is the average daily area in the monthly and yearly files.

docs.title: channel_sdmorph files
docs.text:
Column Units Description flo_in m³/s Inflow rate. geo_bf m³/s Base flow from the geomorphic aquifer method. flo_out m³/s Outflow rate. peakr m³/s Peak flow rate. sed_in tons Sediment entering the channel. sed_out tons Sediment leaving the channel. washld tons Wash load (suspended sediment) leaving the channel. bedld tons Sediment deposited in the channel. dep tons Sediment deposited on the floodplain. deg_btm tons Bed erosion. deg_bank tons Bank erosion. hc_sed tons Sediment from gully headcut erosion. width m Bankfull top width at the end of the step. depth m Bankfull depth at the end of the step. slope m/m Channel slope at the end of the step. deg_btm m Bed downcutting. deg_bank m Bank widening. hc_len m Headcut retreat. flo_in_mm mm Inflow as a depth over the channel's drainage area. aqu_in_mm mm Geomorphic base flow as a depth over the drainage area. flo_out_mm mm Outflow as a depth over the drainage area. sed_stor tons Sediment stored in the channel. n_tot kg N Total nitrogen leaving the channel (organic N, nitrate, ammonium and nitrite). p_tot kg P Total phosphorus leaving the channel (organic and soluble P). dep_bf m Flow depth at bankfull. velav_bf m/s Average velocity at bankfull.

deg_btm and deg_bank each appear twice, first in tons and then in m; read them by position. The units row labels n_tot as kg_N, p_tot as kg_P and dep_bf as m/s; dep_bf is a depth in m.

In the monthly and yearly files, the flow rates, sed_stor, n_tot, p_tot, dep_bf and velav_bf are daily averages; the tons, mm and m erosion columns are totals; and width, depth and slope are the values at the end of the step. The average annual file gives daily averages for the first group and average yearly totals for the second.

docs.title: sd_chanbud files
docs.text:
Column Description in_sed, out_sed Sediment entering and leaving the channel. fp_dep Sediment deposited on the floodplain. ch_dep Sediment deposited in the channel. bank_ero Bank erosion. bed_ero Bed erosion. in_no3, in_orgn, out_no3, out_orgn Nitrate and organic nitrogen entering and leaving. fp_no3 Nitrate lost on the floodplain. bank_no3, bed_no3 Nitrate gained from bank and bed erosion. fp_orgn, ch_orgn Organic nitrogen deposited on the floodplain and in the channel. bank_orgn, bed_orgn Organic nitrogen gained from bank and bed erosion. in_solp, in_orgp, out_solp, out_orgp Soluble and organic phosphorus entering and leaving. fp_solp Soluble phosphorus lost on the floodplain. bank_solp, bed_solp Soluble phosphorus gained from bank and bed erosion. fp_orgp, ch_orgp Organic phosphorus deposited on the floodplain and in the channel. bank_orgp, bed_orgp Organic phosphorus gained from bank and bed erosion. no3_orgn Nitrate converted to organic nitrogen in the channel. solp_orgp Soluble phosphorus converted to organic phosphorus in the channel.

The sediment columns (in_sed to bed_ero) are in tons. The nitrogen and phosphorus columns are in kg, although the units row shows tons for every column. All values are totals for the print step; the average annual file gives the average yearly total.

docs.title: Sediment budget files
docs.text: These three file groups are new in 62.0.1. They use the same channel erosion and deposition values, summed in different ways. Their rows are written in free format (list-directed), so column widths vary.

docs.title: ch_sedbud files (per channel)
docs.text:
Column Units Description num - Number of days in the step on which the channel had inflow. wid m Bankfull width, summed over those days. dep m Bankfull depth, summed over those days. fp_km2 km² Floodplain area, summed over those days. The floodplain is taken as five times the channel width over the channel length. ebank_t tons Bank erosion. ebtm_t tons Bed erosion. ebank_m m Bank erosion as a width. ebtm_m m Bed erosion as a depth. fp_t tons Floodplain deposition. fp_mm mm Floodplain deposition as a depth over the floodplain, assuming a bulk density of 1 t/m³.

wid, dep and fp_km2 are summed over days, so divide them by num to get the average width, depth and floodplain area in the daily, monthly and yearly files. In the average annual file the sums are divided by the number of printed years but num is not, so the ratio is too small by that factor.

docs.title: chanbud_order files (per stream order)
docs.text: One row for each stream order from 1 to 12 in every step, with the ch_sedbud columns summed over all channels of that order. num is then the number of channel-days with inflow, and wid / num and dep / num give the average width and depth for the order. fp_mm is summed over channels and is not a depth for the order as a whole. The stream order of each channel comes from the order column of the channel database.

docs.title: sedbud files (basin)
docs.text:
Column Units Description upland_t tons Sediment yield from all HRUs. ebank_t tons Bank erosion in all channels. ebtm_t tons Bed erosion in all channels. fp_t tons Floodplain deposition in all channels. res_dep_t tons Net deposition in all reservoirs (sediment in minus sediment out). wet_dep_t tons Net deposition in all wetlands.

Deposition inside the channels themselves is not part of this file; it is in the ch_dep column of sd_chanbud.

docs.title: Print timing
docs.text: The three sediment budget file groups start after the nyskip warm-up years, like the other files. Their daily files have a row for every day after that and do not follow the daily print window (day_start to day_end, interval) in print.prt.

docs.title: Basin files
docs.text: basin_sd_cha_*, basin_sd_chamorph_* and basin_sd_chanbud_* have the same columns as channel_sd_*, channel_sdmorph_* and sd_chanbud_*, with one row for the basin. Each value is the sum over all channels in the basin. Flows are summed along the whole network, so flo_out in basin_sd_cha is not the flow leaving the basin; use the outlet channel's row in channel_sd for that. basin_sd_cha has no water_temp column, and in basin_sd_chamorph the width, depth and slope columns are those of the last channel.

docs.title: Sub-daily outflow
docs.text: When the simulation uses a sub-daily time step and the channel_sd row has y in daily, channel_sd_subday.txt has one row per channel per time step: jday, mon, day, yr, unit, gis_id, tstep (time step number), name and flo_out. flo_out is the volume of water (m³) leaving the channel in that time step, although the header gives m³/s. The units row and the header of the .csv copy are those of the channel_sdmorph file.

docs.title: Legacy channel files
docs.text:
The channel and basin_cha rows of print.prt open channel_*.txt and basin_cha_*.txt for legacy channel objects (chan in object.cnt). Their 59 columns cover flow, sediment, nutrients, pesticides, bacteria, metals, sediment size classes and erosion:

flo_in flo_out evap tloss sed_in sed_out sed_conc orgn_in orgn_out orgp_in orgp_out
no3_in no3_out nh4_in nh4_out no2_in no2_out solp_in solp_out chla_in chla_out
cbod_in cbod_out dis_in dis_out solpst_in solpst_out sorbpst_in sorbpst_out react
volat setlpst resuspst difus reactb bury sedpest bacp baclp met1 met2 met3 sand_in
sand_out silt_in silt_out clay_in clay_out smag_in smag_out lag_in lag_out grvl_in
grvl_out bnk_ero ch_deg ch_dep fp_dep tot_ssed

SWAT+ 62.0.1 does not route legacy channels (the routing call is disabled), so these files contain only zeros. Projects built with the SWAT+ Editor use the channels described above.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The columns of every chanbud_order_* file:

jday  mon  day  yr  iord  num  wid  dep  fp_km2  ebank_t  ebtm_t  ebank_m  ebtm_m  fp_t  fp_mm

Take 40 first-order channels, each 5 m wide, that have flow on every day of a 10-year print period. In chanbud_order_y.txt the row with iord 1 has num = 40 × 365 = 14,600 and wid = 73,000, so wid / num gives the 5 m average width. In chanbud_order_a.txt the same row has num = 146,000 (the count over all ten years) and wid = 73,000 (the ten-year sum divided by 10), so the average width is 10 × wid / num.

The reference outputs in refdata/Ames_sub1 of the SWAT+ repository were written by revision 61.0.1 and contain none of the sediment budget files.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
SWAT+ writes the files on this page on every run; print.prt cannot switch them off. They show whether the run finished, which inputs SWAT+ could not match, the soil and HRU settings it used, and which output files it wrote. Check them before using any other output.

File Content simulation.out run log: version banner, weather files read, one line per simulated day, completion message diagnostics.out input problems found while reading: names not found, files missing, values rejected checker.out one row per HRU with soil and hydrology settings after setup files_out.out list of output files opened in this run success.fin written only at the end of a run that finished area_calc.out drainage areas of routed objects, as given and as calculated erosion.out header lines only in 62.0.1 erosion.txt empty in 62.0.1 paddy_test.csv daily paddy rice water balance; column header only unless the model has paddy wetlands

With the gwflow module on, gwflow_record is also always written; see gwflow outputs.

docs.title: simulation.out
docs.text:
The run log. It contains, in order:

  • a banner with the revision, the compiler and its version, the build date and the operating system
  • the date and time of the run
  • one line for each weather input read (reading from precipitation file, reading from temperature file, and so on)
  • one line per simulated day, giving the simulation name, month, day, year, the year number and the number of years, and the clock time
  • at the end, Execution successfully completed and the date and time again

Each daily line starts with Original Simulation in a normal run. During soft calibration other names appear in that place.

                   SWAT+
             Revision 62.0.1
      Soil & Water Assessment Tool
IntelLLVM (2025.0.4), 2026-10-05 00:10:27, Linux
    Program reading . . . executing


 Date of Sim  10/20/2026 Time  12: 9:24
 reading from wgn file                                       Time  12: 9:24
 reading from wx station file                                Time  12: 9:24
 reading from precipitation file                             Time  12: 9:24
 reading from temperature file                               Time  12: 9:24
  ...
  Original Simulation            1   1  1975 Yr    1 of    2 Time  12: 9:24
  ...
  Original Simulation           12  31  1976 Yr    2 of    2 Time  12: 9:35

 Execution successfully completed

  Date of Sim  10/20/2026 Time  12: 9:35

If the completion message is missing, the run stopped early. The last daily line shows the last day that finished, so the problem occurred on the next day. Messages printed to the screen when the run stopped are not copied to this file.

docs.title: diagnostics.out
docs.text:
Line 1 is DIAGNOSTICS.OUT FILE. Every later line reports a problem found while reading the inputs. About 60 places in the code write to this file. Most lines say that a name given in one file was not found in the file it points to; SWAT+ then uses a default or skips the setting and continues.

Common messages:

Message Meaning <land use> <schedule> not found in management.sch a row of landuse.lum names a management schedule that is not in management.sch <name> not found (snow.sno), (soils.sol), (topography.hyd), and similar an HRU or object points to a record that does not exist; the default record is used <file> file not found (tgage), (pgage), and similar a weather station names a climate file that is missing ... could not be opened an input file listed in file.cio could not be opened ... is required when carbon is enabled (codes.bsn carbon = 2) a carbon input file is missing while the dynamic carbon model is on carbon_layers.prt: n_layers must be >= 1 ... the optional layer count file has an invalid value

Example from a run of the Ames_sub1 reference dataset with 62.0.1:

 DIAGNOSTICS.OUT FILE
 agrr_lum                                AGRR_rot                                 not found in management.sch
 soyb_lum                                SOYB_rot                                 not found in management.sch
 oats_lum                                OATS_rot                                 not found in management.sch
 wwht_lum                                WWHT_rot                                 not found in management.sch
 ames.tem                                          file not found (tgage)

A file with only the first line means no problems were found. Read the whole file after each run and decide for each line whether the default SWAT+ used is acceptable.

docs.title: checker.out
docs.text:
One row per HRU, in HRU order, written after the HRUs are set up. Line 1 is the project name and version, line 2 the column header and line 3 the units; the last unit entry, 0=notile;1=tile;, explains the tiledrain column.

# Column Units Description 1 sname - soil name used by the HRU (no header label; the name is in the units line) 2 hydgrp - hydrologic soil group, A to D (no header label) 3 zmx mm maximum rooting depth of the soil 4 usle_k - USLE soil erodibility factor 5 sumfc mm water held at field capacity, whole profile 6 sumul mm water held at saturation, whole profile 7 usle_p - USLE support practice factor 8 usle_ls - USLE slope length and steepness factor 9 esco - soil evaporation compensation factor 10 epco - plant uptake compensation factor 11 cn3_swf - soil water factor for curve number condition III 12 perco - percolation coefficient 13 latq_co - lateral flow coefficient 14 tiledrain 0 or 1 1 if the HRU has tile drainage

The file has no HRU number or name column. Row K belongs to HRU K in hru-data.hru.

Example from a run of Ames_sub1 with 62.0.1:

 demo                      SWAT+ 2026-10-05        MODULAR Rev 2026.62.0.1
                                        zmx       usle_k       sumfc       sumul      usle_p     usle_ls        esco        epco     cn3_swf       perco     latq_co   tiledrain
 sname           hydgrp                 (mm)                    (mm)        (mm)                                                                                     0=notile;1=tile;
soil_01-h1      B                  2000.0000      0.0000    361.5003    616.0899      1.0000      0.3638      0.9500      1.0000      0.0000      0.5000      0.0100           0
soil_02         B                  2000.0000      0.0000    361.5004    449.0375      0.7500      0.3638      0.9500      1.0000      0.0000      0.5000      0.0100           0

Look for zero, negative or extreme values: here usle_k is zero for both soils, so these HRUs produce no USLE erosion. Check whether that is intended.

docs.title: files_out.out
docs.text:
Line 1 is files_out.out - OUTPUT FILES WRITTEN. Each later line names one output file opened in the run, after a tag for its type, such as CHK, HRU, LSU, BASIN, BASIN_AQUIFER, BASIN_CROP_YLD, CROP, RES or DTBL. .csv copies are listed separately.

 files_out.out - OUTPUT FILES WRITTEN
 CHK                       checker.out
 HRU                       hru_carb_gl_mon.txt
 HRU                       hru_carb_gl_mon.csv

Use it to confirm that every file you asked for in print.prt was opened. A file missing from the list was not switched on, or its object type is not in the model (for example, reservoir files in a model without reservoirs). Some files are not listed even when they are written, including the gwflow files and reservoir_mon.csv.

docs.title: success.fin
docs.text: Written at the end of a run that finished. It contains a blank line and Execution successfully completed. Calibration tools and scripts test for this file to tell whether a run finished. Delete it before starting a run if you rely on it, because SWAT+ does not remove an old copy at the start.

docs.title: area_calc.out
docs.text: Drainage areas of every routed object except HRUs and routing units: the object number, type and number within its type, the drainage area given in the connection file and the area SWAT+ calculated from the routing, followed by the same areas for each incoming object. Use it to check that the routing delivers the expected area to each channel and outlet. The file is empty when the model has only HRUs and routing units.

docs.title: Other files
docs.text:
erosion.out contains three header lines and no data in 62.0.1. erosion.txt is opened at the start of each run and left empty.

paddy_test.csv is a temporary paddy rice output. It has a header line, and one line per day for each HRU that has a paddy wetland with water: date, HRU, precipitation, irrigation, seepage, PET, soil evaporation, plant transpiration, weir height, water depth, weir outflow, soil water, sediment concentration and yield, nitrate concentration and yield, LAI, salt concentration and soil water as a percentage of field capacity.

docs.title: Checks after a run
docs.text:
1. simulation.out ends with Execution successfully completed, and success.fin exists.
  2. diagnostics.out has only its first line, or every remaining line is understood and accepted.
  3. checker.out has plausible values for every HRU, and tiledrain matches the design.
  4. files_out.out lists every file requested in print.prt.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The gwflow module simulates groundwater on a grid of cells and replaces the one-dimensional aquifers. It runs when gw_flow = 1 in codes.bsn and writes the output files described here. The input files are described on the gwflow input page.

The files fall into these groups:

  • basin and cell water balance (gwflow_basin_wb_*, gwflow_cell_wb_*)
  • heat and solute balances (gwflow_basin_heat_*, gwflow_basin_sol_*)
  • observation wells (gwflow_obs_*)
  • HRU pumping (gwflow_hru_pump_*)
  • diagnostic files for canals, ponds, tiles and channels
  • channel hydrograph separation (gwflow_chan_hydsep_day.txt)
  • the cell definition and the run log, which are always written

docs.title: Output switches
docs.text:
The write_day, write_mon, write_yr and write_aa flags in codes.gw (1 on, 0 off) switch the water balance files. The heat and solute balance files follow the same flags, and the hydrograph separation file follows write_day. Observation well, pumping and diagnostic output is on by default.

print.prt can override these settings with six rows, each with the usual daily, monthly, yearly and average annual flags. The rows are recognised only when print.prt uses object labels (use_obj_lbls = y). A row that is present replaces the default; a row that is absent leaves it as it is. All overrides are applied before any gwflow output file is opened, so a file that is switched off is not created.

print.prt row Effect gwflow_wb each flag switches the water balance file for that interval; heat, solute and hydrograph separation files follow it unless their rows are present gwflow_heat each flag switches the heat balance file for that interval (there is no monthly heat file) gwflow_solute each flag switches the solute balance files for that interval gwflow_obs each flag switches the observation well file for that interval gwflow_pump any flag set to y switches on all HRU pumping files gwflow_flux the daily or yearly flag switches on the canal, pond, tile and channel diagnostic files

Example rows that keep only the monthly water balance and the daily observation wells:

objects                  daily       monthly        yearly         avann
gwflow_wb                    n             y             n             n
gwflow_obs                   y             n             n             n
gwflow_pump                  n             n             n             n
gwflow_flux                  n             n             n             n

docs.title: Basin water balance
docs.text:
gwflow_basin_wb_day.txt, _mon.txt, _yr.txt and _aa.txt give the water balance of the whole grid. Volumes are summed over all active cells and divided by the watershed area, so they are in mm over the watershed. Line 1 is a title, line 2 the column header and line 3 the units. The seven leading columns are jday, mon, day, yr, unit, gis_id and name (the project name).

The daily file has these columns after the leading ones:

Column Units Description ts day gwflow time step vbef mm groundwater volume at the start of the day vaft mm groundwater volume at the end of the day recharge mm recharge from the soil profile gw_et mm groundwater evapotranspiration gw_sw mm groundwater discharge to channels sw_gw mm channel seepage to groundwater sat_excess mm saturation excess flow to the land surface soil mm groundwater moved into the soil profile lateral mm net lateral flow between cells boundary mm exchange across the grid boundary pump_allo mm pumping for water allocation (irrigation) pump_ext mm pumping specified in pumpex.gw tile mm tile drain outflow reservoir mm exchange with reservoirs wetland mm exchange with wetlands canal mm canal seepage floodplain mm exchange with floodplains pond mm recharge pond seepage phytorem mm phreatophyte transpiration error % volume balance error sat_frac fraction fraction of active cells with saturation excess flow that day wt_depth m average depth to the water table (see the note below) pump_def mm allocation pumping demand that could not be met

The monthly, yearly and average annual files replace ts, vbef and vaft with dvol (change in storage, mm) and drop error, sat_frac and wt_depth. They end with pump_def after phytorem.

The daily wt_depth is the average over the active cells. In the average annual file, dvol is the total change in storage over the run divided by the number of years, and every flux is the run total divided by the number of years.

docs.title: Cell water balance
docs.text:
gwflow_cell_wb_day.txt, _mon.txt, _yr.txt and _aa.txt have one row per active cell per interval. Lines 1 and 2 are notes on units; line 3 is the column header.

Column Units Description jday, mon, day, yr - date of the row unit - cell number in the gwflow grid gis_id - cell ID from the gis_id column of cells.gw (the gwflow cell shapefile ID) name - cell name from cells.gw, such as cell0001 (first 12 characters) head m groundwater head wt_depth m land surface elevation of the cell minus the head recharge m³/day recharge gw_et m³/day groundwater evapotranspiration gw_sw m³/day discharge to channels sw_gw m³/day channel seepage sat_excess m³/day saturation excess flow soil m³/day transfer to the soil profile lateral m³/day net lateral flow pump_allo m³/day allocation pumping pump_ext m³/day specified pumping tile m³/day tile drain outflow reservoir m³/day reservoir exchange wetland m³/day wetland exchange floodplain m³/day floodplain exchange canal m³/day canal seepage pond m³/day recharge pond seepage phytorem m³/day phreatophyte transpiration

The monthly, yearly and average annual files give the average daily rate over the interval, so all fluxes stay in m³/day.

wt_depth is measured from the cell's land surface elevation, which on a coarse grid represents the valley and not the streambed. Cells along channels can therefore show a deep water table while the head is close to the channel level. This comes from the grid resolution; the head itself is not affected.

docs.title: Heat balance
docs.text:
When heat transport is on (heat = 1 in codes.gw), gwflow_basin_heat_day.txt, _yr.txt and _aa.txt are written. They follow the daily, yearly and average annual water balance switches, or the gwflow_heat row of print.prt when it is present; there is no monthly heat file. Values are in MJ.

The daily file has ts, hbef and haft (heat stored at the start and end of the day), then recharge, gw_et, gw_sw, sw_gw, sat_excess, soil, lateral, dispersion, boundary, pump_allo, pump_ext, tile, reservoir, wetland, canal, floodplain, pond, then error (%) and tavg (average groundwater temperature, °C). The yearly and average annual files start with hdel (change in heat stored) and end at pond.

docs.title: Solute balances
docs.text:
When solute transport is on (solute = 1 in codes.gw), one file per solute and interval is written, named gwflow_basin_sol_<solute>_<interval>.txt. Nitrate (no3) and phosphorus (p) are always included; with salts in the model, so4, ca, mg, na, k, cl, co3 and hco3 are added; with constituents, seo4 and seo3. Values are in kg. The interval files follow the water balance switches, or the gwflow_solute row of print.prt when it is present.

The daily file has ts, mbef and maft (solute mass at the start and end of the day), then recharge, gw_sw, sw_gw, sat_excess, soil, advection, dispersion, react_in, react_out, mineral, sorption, pump_allo, pump_ext, tile, reservoir, wetland, canal, floodplain, pond and error (%). The monthly, yearly and average annual files start with delm (change in mass) and end at pond.

docs.title: Observation wells
docs.text:
Observation cells are listed as observation_cell lines in outputs.gw. The files gwflow_obs_day.txt, _mon.txt, _yr.txt and _aa.txt have one row per observation cell:

Column Units Description unit - observation well number, in the order listed in outputs.gw gis_id - cell number of the observation cell name - obs_0001, obs_0002, ... head m groundwater head wt_depth m land surface elevation minus head temperature °C groundwater temperature; -99 when heat transport is off no3 mg/L nitrate concentration; -99 when solute transport is off p mg/L phosphorus concentration; -99 when solute transport is off

The monthly and yearly files give averages over the interval, and the average annual file the average over the run.

docs.title: HRU pumping
docs.text:
When pumping for water allocation is simulated, gwflow_hru_pump_day.txt, _mon.txt, _yr.txt and _aa.txt report the groundwater pumped for each HRU in the pump_allo column. The daily file is in m³/day and lists only HRUs that pumped that day; the monthly and yearly files give totals in m³, and the average annual file m³/yr.

When hru_pump.gw lists HRUs to observe, gwflow_cell_wb_ppag_obs_day.txt gives their daily pumping in m³, one column per listed HRU. It is written under the same switch as the other pumping files.

docs.title: Diagnostic files
docs.text:
These files are written when the related feature is in use and diagnostic output is on (gwflow_flux):

File Content gwflow_canal_wb_day.txt daily canal water balance in m³: diversion, storage, pond_xfer, seepage gwflow_canal_sol_day.txt daily canal solute balance in kg: div_mass, storage, pond_mass, seep_mass for each solute gwflow_pond_wb_day.txt daily recharge pond water balance: area (m²), storage, rain, div_added, evap, recharge, div_spec, div_unsat (m³) gwflow_pond_sol_day.txt daily pond solute balance: area, storage, solute, mass, div_added, recharge (kg) gwflow_pond_mass_day.txt, gwflow_pond_conc_day.txt daily solute mass (kg) and concentration (g/m³), one column per pond gwflow_tile_group_day.txt daily tile flow (m³/s) for each group of tile cells gwflow_gwsw_group_day.txt daily groundwater and channel exchange (m³) for each channel cell group in sw_group.gw gwflow_chan_obs_flow_day.txt daily groundwater and channel exchange (m³) at the channel cells flagged in chancell.gw gwflow_chan_obs_no3_day.txt the same for nitrate (g), when solute transport is on

When gwflow.wbgroups is present, one daily water balance file per cell group is also written, named gwflow_group_wb_day_ followed by the group number as two characters (a space and the digit for groups 1 to 9). Its columns follow the daily basin file, in m³.

docs.title: Hydrograph separation
docs.text: gwflow_chan_hydsep_day.txt is written when daily water balance output is on. It gives, for each channel and day, the flow from each source in m³/s: surf_runoff, lateral, gw_discharge, stream_seep, satex_gw, satex_sw and tile_drain.

docs.title: Files always written
docs.text:
File Content gwflow_record run log: which input files were found, which features are active, which print.prt rows changed the output switches, and error messages from reading gwflow_cell_definition.txt one line per cell: cell_id, row, col, x_coord, y_coord, zone, status, area

When transit.gw is present on a structured grid, gwflow_transit_cell, gwflow_transit_chan and (with tiles) gwflow_transit_tile give travel times in days.

The head_output_time lines in outputs.gw are still read but no longer produce output; cell heads are in the cell water balance files.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
SWAT+ moves water and its loads between objects (HRUs, routing units, channels, reservoirs, aquifers and so on) as hydrographs: a record of water volume, sediment, nutrients and temperature for the day. The files on this page report those hydrographs.

File One row per Content hydout_* object and outgoing connection What each object sends to each receiving object. hydin_* object and incoming connection What each object receives from each source object. deposition_* HRU or routing unit that receives inflow Material deposited from incoming water. ru_* routing unit Sum of the hydrographs of the routing unit's elements. hydcon.out object The routing order and connections, written once at the start of the run.

hydin, hydout and deposition are switched on by the hyd row of print.prt, and ru by the ru row. Each y in the daily, monthly, yearly or avann column opens the _day, _mon, _yr or _aa file. hydcon.out is switched on by hydcon on the line after csvout. With csvout set to y, a .csv copy of each file is written as well.

The connections themselves are defined in the connection files (see connection files): each object lists the objects it sends water to, the hydrograph type it sends and the fraction.

docs.title: Hydrograph columns
docs.text:
All four time-step file groups end with the same 18 columns:

Column Units Description flo m³ Volume of water. sed tons Sediment. orgn kg N Organic nitrogen. sedp kg P Organic (sediment-attached) phosphorus. no3 kg N Nitrate. solp kg P Soluble mineral phosphorus. chla kg Chlorophyll a. nh3 kg N Ammonium. no2 kg N Nitrite. cbod kg Carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand. dox kg Dissolved oxygen. san tons Sand. sil tons Silt. cla tons Clay. sag tons Small aggregates. lag tons Large aggregates. grv tons Gravel. null °C Water temperature.

flo is a volume: m³ per day in the daily file, the total for the month or year in the monthly and yearly files, and the average yearly total in the average annual file. The units row of the files gives m³/s for flo. To convert a daily value to an average rate, divide by 86,400.

All other loads are totals for the step in the same way. The last column is headed null and is the water temperature; monthly, yearly and average annual values are flow-weighted averages.

docs.title: hydout files
docs.text:
# Column Description 1 jday Day of the year of the last day in the print step. 2 mon Month. 3 day Day of the month. 4 yr Calendar year. 5 name Name of the source object. 6 type Object type of the source object (hru, hru_lte, ru, aqu, chandeg, res, recall, exco, dr, outlet). 7 objtyp Type code of the receiving object, as in the connection file (hru, ru, aqu, sdc, res and so on). 8 typ_no Number of the receiving object within its type. 9 hyd_typ Hydrograph type sent: tot (total), rhg (recharge), sur (surface runoff), lat (lateral flow) or til (tile flow). 10 fraction Fraction of that hydrograph sent to this receiving object. 11 to 28 flo to null The hydrograph sent, already multiplied by fraction.

An object with three outgoing connections has three rows per print step. The rows of all objects follow the routing order, so the rows of one step are not sorted by object name.

docs.title: hydin files
docs.text:
The columns are those of hydout, seen from the receiving side:

# Column Description 5 name Name of the receiving object. 6 type Object type of the receiving object. 7 objtyp Type code of the source object. 8 typ_no Number of the source object within its type. 9 hyd_typ Hydrograph type received. 10 fraction Fraction of the source hydrograph received. 11 to 28 flo to null The hydrograph received.

Rows are written for every incoming connection, but values are filled only when the receiving object is not an HRU, HRU-LTE or routing unit. For those three receiving types the incoming water is split into surface, lateral and tile parts and routed inside the object, and the hydin rows stay zero. Use the hydout rows of the source object instead.

hydin_yr.csv has one more column than the other hydin files: the object number is written after type, so the later columns are shifted by one against the header.

docs.title: deposition files
docs.text:
deposition_* has jday, mon, day, yr, name and type, then the 18 hydrograph columns. It has a row for every HRU and routing unit that receives water from another object.

  • For an HRU without a wetland, the sed column is the sediment deposited on the HRU from incoming surface runoff, in tons: the incoming sediment above the transport capacity of the runoff over the HRU. The other columns are zero.
  • For an HRU with a wetland or rice paddy, incoming surface runoff and tile flow go into the wetland, and the row shows that inflow. In this case flo is in mm and the loads are per hectare.
  • For a routing unit, the row shows the hydrograph of the last element processed in the routing unit. It does not measure deposition.

The deposition files are written from the start of the simulation, including the nyskip warm-up years, while the average annual value is divided by the number of printed years only.

docs.title: ru files
docs.text:
ru_* has jday, mon, day, yr, name and type, then the 18 hydrograph columns, with one row per routing unit.

Each value is the sum, over the elements of the routing unit, of every hydrograph type the element produces. For an HRU element that is the total hydrograph plus its recharge, surface, lateral and tile hydrographs, so flo and the loads are larger than the routing unit's outflow. The outflow of a routing unit is in the hydout rows of the routing unit, with hyd_typ tot for the total flow.

docs.title: hydcon.out
docs.text:
hydcon.out has no title or header line. It lists the objects in the order SWAT+ processes them, one line per object:

Field Description 1 Sequence number in the routing order. 2 Object name. 3 Object type. 4 Number of the object's properties record in its data file. 5 Overbank connection pointer to landscape units (0 when none). 6 Number of outgoing connections. 7 Number of incoming connections. 8 and on For each outgoing connection: the receiving object numbers, the receiving type code, its number within the type and the hydrograph type.

In 62.0.1 the receiving object numbers are written as the full list of all receiving objects for every outgoing connection, so lines for objects with more than one outgoing connection repeat that list.

docs.title: Constituent hydrographs
docs.text: print.prt and the source refer to hydrograph files for pesticides, pathogens, metals and salts (hydin_pests_*, hydout_salts_* and so on). SWAT+ 62.0.1 does not write them.

docs.title: Print timing
docs.text: hydin, hydout and ru start after the nyskip warm-up years. Daily rows follow the daily print window and interval in print.prt. deposition is written from the first simulated year, as described above.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The column names of hydout_day.txt and hydin_day.txt:

jday  mon  day  yr  name  type  objtyp  typ_no  hyd_typ  fraction
flo  sed  orgn  sedp  no3  solp  chla  nh3  no2  cbod  dox  san  sil  cla  sag  lag  grv  null

A hydout row for an HRU sending 60% of its total flow to a routing unit has type hru, objtyp ru, hyd_typ tot and fraction 0.6, and its flo is 0.6 times the HRU's water yield in m³.

docs.title: Filename pattern
docs.text:
Most time-step outputs are named

<object>_<group>_<interval>.txt

for example hru_wb_day.txt (HRU water balance, daily) or basin_sd_cha_aa.txt (basin sum of channel outputs, average annual). Some files have no group (aquifer_day.txt, reservoir_mon.txt, ru_yr.txt), and a few files written once per run have no interval (hru_cbn_lyr.txt, mgt_out.txt).

Interval Meaning print.prt column _day one row per object per day daily _mon one row per object per month monthly _yr one row per object per year yearly _aa one row per object, average annual over the printed years avann

The channel sediment budget files ch_sedbud_* and chanbud_order_* use _d, _m, _y and _a instead.

When csvout is y in print.prt, most time-step files also get a comma-separated copy with the same name and the extension .csv.

docs.title: Output folder
docs.text: Output files are written to the folder named on the output path line at the end of file.cio. SWAT+ creates the folder if it does not exist. When the line is missing, empty or null, outputs go to the folder SWAT+ runs in. simulation.out, success.fin and erosion.txt always go to the run folder.

docs.title: File layout
docs.text:
Time-step files share one layout:

  • Line 1: the project name from file.cio and the SWAT+ version banner.
  • Line 2: column headers.
  • Line 3: units (blank for columns without units).
  • Lines 4 and on: data rows.

Rows with one object per row start with jday, mon, day, yr, unit, gis_id and name. Basin files use the same columns with unit and gis_id set to 1. jday, mon, day and yr are the date of the last day in the print step.

docs.title: Print timing
docs.text:
The first blocks of print.prt set when rows are written:

  • Daily rows are written from day_start of yrc_start to day_end of yrc_end, every interval days. A zero day_start means day 1, a zero day_end means day 366, and zero years mean the first and last simulated year.
  • Monthly, yearly and average annual rows start after the first nyskip simulated years. Average annual values are averages over the remaining years.
  • The average annual print intervals (aa_int_cnt and the end years that follow it) are read, but in 62.0.1 they are used only by the region output, which is not written, so they have no effect.

docs.title: print.prt rows and files
docs.text:
Each row in the objects block of print.prt has a name and four y/n switches. When use_obj_lbls is y, rows are matched by name, may come in any order, and rows can be left out (they default to n). A name that appears twice stops the run with an error, and so does a name SWAT+ does not know. When use_obj_lbls is n, the rows are read by position and must follow the order of the table below up to wetland_cs; the carbon and gwflow rows can only be set in labelled mode.

Each y opens the file for that interval. The table shows the file stems; add _day.txt, _mon.txt, _yr.txt or _aa.txt.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Two groups of output files report nutrients on the land:

  • The nutrient balance files (*_nb_*) give the N and P added to, moved within and removed from the soil and plants: grazing and fertiliser inputs, fixation, atmospheric deposition, mineralisation and other transfers between soil pools, denitrification and plant uptake.
  • The losses files (*_ls_*) give the sediment and nutrients that leave the land with surface runoff, lateral flow, tile flow and percolation.

All values are amounts per unit area summed over the print interval. Each group has a row in print.prt for each scope, with daily, monthly, yearly and average annual flags.

docs.title: Files and switches
docs.text:
Scope Nutrient balance row Nutrient balance files Losses row Losses files HRU hru_nb hru_nb_{day,mon,yr,aa}.txt hru_ls hru_ls_{day,mon,yr,aa}.txt HRU-lte hru-lte_nb none (see below) hru-lte_ls hru-lte_ls_{day,mon,yr,aa}.txt Landscape unit lsunit_nb lsunit_nb_{day,mon,yr,aa}.txt lsunit_ls lsunit_ls_{day,mon,yr,aa}.txt Basin basin_nb basin_nb_{day,mon,yr,aa}.txt basin_ls basin_ls_{day,mon,yr,aa}.txt

Each file also gets a .csv copy when csvout = y. Notes on the switches:

  • print.prt also accepts hru-lte_nb, region_nb and region_ls rows, but 62.0.1 writes no files for them.
  • The hru_nb row also opens hru_ncycle_{day,mon,yr,aa}.txt, a nutrient cycling file with the columns lab_min_p, act_sta_p, act_nit_n, act_sta_n, org_lab_p, rsd_hs_c, rsd_nitrorg_n and rsd_laborg_p. In 62.0.1 these files contain only their header lines. The same transfers are in the hru_nb files.
  • Landscape unit files are written only when the model defines landscape units in ls_unit.def.

Line 1 of every file is the project name and version, line 2 the column header and line 3 the units. The first seven columns are jday, mon, day, yr, unit, gis_id and name; see Naming convention.

docs.title: Nutrient balance columns
docs.text:
# Column Units Description 1 grzn kg N/ha nitrogen added to the soil in manure from grazing 2 grzp kg P/ha phosphorus added to the soil in manure from grazing 3 lab_min_p kg P/ha net phosphorus flow from the labile mineral pool to the active mineral pool; negative when the flow goes the other way 4 act_sta_p kg P/ha net phosphorus flow from the active mineral pool to the stable mineral pool; negative when the flow goes the other way 5 fertn kg N/ha nitrogen applied with fertiliser and manure (mineral and organic) 6 fertp kg P/ha phosphorus applied with fertiliser and manure (mineral and organic) 7 fixn kg N/ha nitrogen added to plant biomass by fixation 8 denit kg N/ha nitrogen lost from the nitrate pool by denitrification 9 act_nit_n kg N/ha nitrogen moved from the active organic pool to the nitrate pool (mineralisation) 10 act_sta_n kg N/ha nitrogen moved from the active organic pool to the stable organic pool 11 org_lab_p kg P/ha phosphorus moved from the organic pool to the labile pool (mineralisation) 12 rsd_nitorg_n kg N/ha nitrogen moved from fresh residue to the nitrate (80%) and active organic (20%) pools 13 rsd_laborg_p kg P/ha phosphorus moved from fresh residue to the labile (80%) and organic (20%) pools 14 no3atmo kg N/ha nitrate added to the soil by atmospheric deposition, wet and dry 15 nh4atmo kg N/ha ammonium added to the soil by atmospheric deposition, wet and dry 16 nuptake kg N/ha nitrogen taken up by plants 17 puptake kg P/ha phosphorus taken up by plants 18 gwsoiln kg N/ha nitrate added to the soil from groundwater (gwflow module only) 19 gwsoilp kg P/ha phosphorus added to the soil from groundwater (gwflow module only)

The units line writes kgha for every column. The HRU files add plant_cov and mgt_ops at the end of each row: the plant community and management schedule of the HRU's land use. The landscape unit and basin files have the same two labels in their header but write no values under them.

Columns 9 to 13 (act_nit_n to rsd_laborg_p) are filled only with the static carbon model, carbon = 0 in codes.bsn. With carbon = 2 they stay at zero, and the corresponding flows are in the carbon outputs. denit and the mineral P columns 3 and 4 are filled under both settings.

docs.title: Losses columns
docs.text:
# Column Units Description 1 sedyld t/ha sediment yield leaving the land by water erosion 2 sedorgn kg N/ha organic nitrogen attached to sediment in surface runoff 3 sedorgp kg P/ha organic phosphorus attached to sediment in surface runoff 4 surqno3 kg N/ha nitrate in surface runoff 5 lat3no3 kg N/ha nitrate in lateral flow 6 surqsolp kg P/ha soluble phosphorus in surface runoff 7 usle t/ha soil loss predicted by the USLE (the units line says tons) 8 sedminp kg P/ha mineral phosphorus (active and stable) attached to sediment 9 tileno3 kg N/ha nitrate in tile flow 10 lchlabp kg P/ha soluble (labile) phosphorus leached below the soil profile 11 tilelabp kg P/ha soluble (labile) phosphorus in tile flow 12 satexn kg N/ha nitrate in saturation excess runoff; always 0 in 62.0.1

The HRU files add plant_cov, mgt_ops and percn at the end of each row. percn (kg N/ha) is the nitrate leached below the soil profile, the same value as percn in the plant and weather files. The HRU-lte, landscape unit and basin files have these three labels in their header but write no values under them.

In the HRU-lte files only sedyld is calculated; the other columns are always zero.

docs.title: Aggregation
docs.text:
Every column is a sum. The monthly and yearly files add up the daily values, and the average annual file divides the run total by the number of printed years. Nothing is averaged over days.

Landscape unit values are the sum of the HRU (and HRU-lte) values, each multiplied by its RU_FRAC in ls_unit.ele. Basin values are the sum of the HRU and HRU-lte values, each multiplied by its BSN_FRAC in ls_unit.ele. The fractions are used as given and are not checked: when they do not add up to 1, the basin and landscape unit values are scaled by the same factor. In the Ames_sub1 reference dataset the BSN_FRAC values add up to 2, so its basin values are twice the area-weighted HRU average.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The test folder of the SWAT+ source has two Python scripts. They are not installed with the model; run them from a copy of the source or copy them next to your project.

  • spcheck.py runs SWAT+ on a scenario and compares the numbers in two sets of output files. The build uses it for its regression test.
  • swat_output_to_csv_files.py reads SWAT+ output files into pandas tables and can save them as tab-separated files.

docs.title: spcheck.py
docs.text: spcheck.py needs Python 3.10 or later and no extra packages. It has three commands.

docs.title: run
docs.text:
python spcheck.py run <executable> <scenario>

Run from a folder that contains build/, data/ and runs/. The command copies data/<scenario> to a new folder runs/<scenario>/<NN>#<date and time>#<executable>, where NN is the next two-digit run number (01, 02, ...), and runs build/<executable> there. If SWAT+ ends with an error, the run folder gets the suffix -FAILED.

docs.title: compare
docs.text:
python spcheck.py compare <scenario> <a> <b> [--abserr 1e-8] [--relerr 0.05] [--nlines N] [--nerrorlines N]

Compares two earlier runs of a scenario, given by their run numbers a and b. The files to compare are listed in data/<scenario>/.testfiles.txt, one name per line; lines starting with # are skipped. A failed run cannot be compared.

docs.title: ctest
docs.text:
python spcheck.py ctest <model_path> <data_dir> <tmp_dir> [--abserr 1e-8] [--relerr 0.05] [--nlines N] [--nerrorlines N]

Copies the whole folder <data_dir>, including its output files, to <tmp_dir>, runs <model_path> there, and compares the files listed in <data_dir>/.testfiles.txt between the original and the new run. It exits with code 1 when it finds differences. Because the original outputs are copied too, a listed file that the new run does not write is compared with the copied original and passes.

docs.title: Comparison rule
docs.text:
Both files are read line by line. On each line, only tokens that are decimal numbers are compared, by position; whole numbers (dates, object numbers) and text are skipped, and lines containing the version banner MODULAR are skipped. Two values \(f_1\) (first run) and \(f_2\) (second run) differ when

\[|f_1 - f_2| \ge e_{abs} + e_{rel}\,|f_2|\]

with \(e_{abs}\) = --abserr (default \(10^{-8}\)) and \(e_{rel}\) = --relerr (default 0.05). For each differing line the script prints both lines, the field numbers, the two values and their absolute and relative error, and at the end the total number of differences.

The script assumes both files have the same layout. It stops at the end of the shorter file without reporting a difference in length. A line whose two versions have different numbers of decimal values is not reported, and it lowers the difference count by one. --nlines limits the number of lines checked per file, and --nerrorlines the number of differing lines reported per file.

docs.title: Regression test in the build
docs.text: CMakeLists.txt registers one test, Ames_sub1, which calls spcheck.py ctest with --relerr 0.01 and --abserr 1e-8. The test reads its scenario from <source>/data/Ames_sub1; the reference data in the 62.0.1 source is in refdata/Ames_sub1. The .testfiles.txt of Ames_sub1 lists 42 files; six of them (hru_nut_carb_gl_aa.txt, hru_soilcarb_aa.txt, hru_rescarb_aa.txt, hru_plcarb_aa.txt, hru_soilc_stat.txt, hru_resc_stat.txt) are no longer written by 62.0.1 and pass only because of the copy described above.

docs.title: swat_output_to_csv_files.py
docs.text: The script maps output file names to reading instructions for pandas.read_csv and loads each file into a table.

docs.title: Use
docs.text:
cd <folder with SWAT+ outputs>
python /path/to/swat_output_to_csv_files.py

The script reads files_out.out from the current folder, then reads every file listed there, except mgt_out.txt and yield.out, and writes each one to <name>.csv in the same folder (for example hru_wb_aa.txt.csv). The .csv files are tab-separated.

From Python, one file can be read without writing anything:

import swat_output_to_csv_files as s
df = s.read_output("basin_wb_aa.txt", s.spec_dict, write_csv=False)

docs.title: Supported files
docs.text:
Most files are read by skipping line 1 (title) and line 3 (units) and taking line 2 as the column names. crop_yld_aa.txt and crop_yld_yr.txt skip two lines. lu_change_out.txt, basin_crop_yld_aa.txt and basin_crop_yld_yr.txt keep line 3 as data. checker.out and files_out.out are read with fixed column names.

files_out.out  checker.out  hru_orgc.txt
hru_wb_aa.txt  hru_ncycle_aa.txt  hru_nb_aa.txt  hru_carbon_aa.txt  hru_nut_carb_gl_aa.txt  hru_ls_aa.txt  hru_pw_aa.txt
basin_wb_aa.txt  basin_nb_aa.txt  basin_carbon_aa.txt  basin_ls_aa.txt  basin_pw_aa.txt
crop_yld_yr.txt  crop_yld_aa.txt  lu_change_out.txt  basin_crop_yld_yr.txt  basin_crop_yld_aa.txt
hydout_aa.txt  hydin_aa.txt  deposition_aa.txt  wetland_aa.txt  basin_aqu_aa.txt  basin_res_aa.txt
recall_aa.txt  basin_cha_aa.txt  basin_sd_cha_aa.txt  basin_sd_chamorph_aa.txt  basin_psc_aa.txt  ru_aa.txt

Only average annual files are covered. hru_orgc.txt and hru_nut_carb_gl_aa.txt are not written by 62.0.1.

docs.title: Limits with 62.0.1
docs.text:
• The script stops (exit code 1) at the first file listed in files_out.out that it has no instructions for, with the message Swat+ output filename not found in read specification dictionary. A 62.0.1 run usually lists such files (for example the carbon files, sd_chanbud_aa.txt or any daily file), so a full run stops part way. Reading single files with read_output works.
  • It passes delim_whitespace=True to pandas.read_csv. pandas 2.2 warns about this option and pandas 3.0 no longer accepts it; with pandas 3.0 every file fails with the message could not be parsed for some reason.
  • basin_wb_aa.txt ends with the two-word label Original Simulation and a number, which gives its data row more values than the header has names, so pandas moves the leading columns into the row index.
  • files_out.out is read as two columns, tag and file name. With csvout on, some tags contain a space (CHANBUD ORDER), which breaks those lines.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
A recall object adds a measured or externally simulated time series of water and loads to the model: a point source such as a treatment plant, an inlet from an area outside the model, or, with negative flows, a diversion. The recall output files show what each recall object released into the model.

print.prt row Files One row per recall recall_day.txt, recall_mon.txt, recall_yr.txt, recall_aa.txt recall object basin_psc basin_psc_day.txt, basin_psc_mon.txt, basin_psc_yr.txt, basin_psc_aa.txt basin (sum of all recall objects)

Each y in the daily, monthly, yearly or avann column of print.prt opens the matching file. With csvout set to y, a .csv copy of each file is written as well. The basin_psc files are written only when the project has at least one recall object.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
• Line 1: the project name from file.cio and the SWAT+ version banner.
  • Line 2: column headers.
  • Line 3: units.
  • Lines 4 and on: data rows.
# Column Units Description 1 jday - Day of the year of the last day in the print step. 2 mon - Month. 3 day - Day of the month. 4 yr - Calendar year. 5 name - Name of the recall object. In basin_psc files, the project name. 6 type - Object type, always recall. basin_psc files have no type column; the header has a blank name in its place. 7 flo m³ Water released. 8 sed tons Sediment. 9 orgn kg N Organic nitrogen. 10 sedp kg P Organic (sediment-attached) phosphorus. 11 no3 kg N Nitrate. 12 solp kg P Soluble mineral phosphorus. 13 chla kg Chlorophyll a. 14 nh3 kg N Ammonium. 15 no2 kg N Nitrite. 16 cbod kg Carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand. 17 dox kg Dissolved oxygen. 18 san tons Sand. 19 sil tons Silt. 20 cla tons Clay. 21 sag tons Small aggregates. 22 lag tons Large aggregates. 23 grv tons Gravel. 24 null °C Water temperature.

The values are the recall record used on the day, unchanged: SWAT+ does not convert the numbers read from the recall time series. The model passes flo on to the receiving object as a daily volume in m³, so that is how the column should be read, although the units row gives m³/s. The .csv copies of the recall files use a different units row, which gives flo as m³.

docs.title: Values by recall time step
docs.text:
The time step of each recall object is set in its recall file:

  • Daily: each day uses the record for that day. Outside the years covered by the time series, the values are zero.
  • Monthly: the record for the month is used on every day of that month. A monthly row of recall_mon.txt is therefore the monthly record multiplied by the number of days in the month. Outside the covered years, the values are zero.
  • Yearly: the record for the year is used on every day of that year, so a row of recall_yr.txt is 365 or 366 times the yearly record.
  • Sub-daily: the daily row is the sum of the records for that day's time steps.

A negative flo in a daily recall time series is a withdrawal. The row shows the negative value as read. In addition, SWAT+ removes nitrate, ammonium, nitrite, organic nitrogen, soluble phosphorus and dissolved oxygen from the receiving channel's storage at the channel's current concentration. Those removed amounts are not in the recall files.

docs.title: Aggregation
docs.text:
Monthly and yearly rows are totals over the step for all columns except null, which is a flow-weighted average. The average annual row is the average yearly total. Rows start after the nyskip warm-up years, and daily rows follow the daily print window and interval in print.prt.

basin_psc rows are sums over all recall objects, so withdrawals (negative flows) offset releases.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The column names of recall_day.txt:

jday  mon  day  yr  name  type
flo  sed  orgn  sedp  no3  solp  chla  nh3  no2  cbod  dox  san  sil  cla  sag  lag  grv  null

A treatment plant entered as a monthly recall object with flo = 1,200 for March shows 1,200 on every March row of recall_day.txt and 37,200 in the March row of recall_mon.txt.
